title: Remove runAsGroup field from security context settings
body:
In #1929 we added additional security context settings to ensure that pods in the linkerd control plane are not running as root. As part of that change we added the `runAsGroup` field to a few security contexts, but that field is not available in Kubernetes 1.9 or earlier. In this branch I'm removing the `runAsGroup` field so that the control plane will be installable on 1.9 clusters.

body: In #1980 I pared-down the RBAC privileges for the controller running in single-namespace mode, and I removed the permission for the controller to read all namespaces in the cluster. This branch removes the `--proxy-bind-timeout` flag from the 
`linkerd inject` and `linkerd install` CLI commands, and the

review_threads.author: klingerf
review_threads.body:
This check needs to remain as fatal, unfortunately, since knowing the latest version is a prerequisite for all of the subsequent version checks. If we can't reach versioncheck.linkerd.io to determine the latest version, then we can't validate that any of the components are running the latest version or not.

Also, since the "control plane is up-to-date" check is already marked as a warning, if that check fails because the `/Version` endpoint is unreachable, that won't be reported back to the CLI. Instead, the CLI will ignore the failure, and return the client, even though the client (assumedly) won't be able to connect to the public API.

I recommend reverting this change and adding a separate set of checks, similar to `LinkerdAPIChecks`, that calls the `/Version` endpoint instead of the `/SelfCheck` endpoint. Then we can continue use `LinkerdAPIChecks` for the `linkerd check` and `linkerd dashboard` commands, and we can use the new set of more limited checks (control plane pod exists and `/Version` endpoint returns without error) for all other commands.

review_threads.author: siggy
review_threads.body:
@klingerf Yup, that fatal -> warning change was mine. The intent was to allow cli commands to run if versioncheck.linkerd.io fails, but you're correct that we should just not run the check, and for the `linkerd check` and `dashboard` cases it should fatally fail the subsequent version checks.

@alpeb's correct that we've already broken out a limited set of checks for all commands except `dashboard` and `check`, specifically:
- `KubernetesAPIChecks`
- `LinkerdExistenceChecks`
- `LinkerdVersionChecks`

It sounds like we should not perform `LinkerdVersionChecks` for any commands except `dashboard` and `check`. We can do that by modifying `validatedPublicAPIClient` as follows:

```go
checks := []healthcheck.Checks{
	healthcheck.KubernetesAPIChecks,
	healthcheck.LinkerdExistenceChecks,
}

if apiChecks {
	checks = append(checks, healthcheck.LinkerdAPIChecks)
	checks = append(checks, healthcheck.LinkerdVersionChecks)
```

...and then introduce a new type of `/Version` check (which I think you had in your initial PR), and include that as part of `LinkerdExistenceChecks`, something like:

```go
func GetServerVersion(apiClient pb.ApiClient) (string, error) {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
	defer cancel()

	rsp, err := apiClient.Version(ctx, &pb.Empty{})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	return  rsp.GetReleaseVersion(), nil
}
```

review_threads.author: klingerf
review_threads.body:
Ok great, thanks for the additional info. The updated approach that @siggy laid out makes sense to me.

I'm sorry the code is so convoluted. To help with my own understanding, I made a list of all of the checks that we run when building the public API client that we use when executing the `linkerd stat` command (for example). As this branch is currently written, they are as follows:

* kubernetes-api: can initialize the client
* kubernetes-api: can query the Kubernetes API
* linkerd-existence: control plane namespace exists
* linkerd-existence: controller pod is running
* linkerd-existence: can initialize the client
* linkerd-version: can determine the latest version
* linkerd-version: cli is up-to-date
* linkerd-version: control plane is up-to-date

Those last 3 "linkerd-version" checks will never result in an error message, however, since they are all marked as warnings. The [exitOnError func](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/master/cli/cmd/root.go#L106) that we use when running the checks explicitly ignores all failed checks that are marked as warnings, so they're effectively a no-op.

In order to bring those checks in line with what's described in https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/issues/1854#issuecomment-447976710, we should change them as follows:

* kubernetes-api: can initialize the client
* kubernetes-api: can query the Kubernetes API
* linkerd-existence: control plane namespace exists
* linkerd-existence: controller pod is running
* linkerd-existence: can initialize the client
* __linkerd-existence: can successfully call the `/Version` endpoint__
* ~~linkerd-version: can determine the latest version~~
* ~~linkerd-version: cli is up-to-date~~
* ~~linkerd-version: control plane is up-to-date~~

And I agree that updating `addLinkerdExistenceChecks` to include that one additional check and removing the call to `addLinkerdVersionChecks` should do the trick.

title: Surface logs from control plane pods
body:
When debugging control plane issues or issues pertaining to the linkerd proxy, it can be cumbersome to get logs from affected containers in quickly. 

This PR adds a new command `logs` to the Linkerd CLI to surface log lines from any container within linkerd's control plane. This feature relies heavily on [stern](https://github.com/wercker/stern), which already provides this behavior. This PR integrates this package into the Linkerd CLI to allow users to quickly retrieve logs whenever they run into issues when using Linkerd.  As a follow-up issue, it would be useful to filter logs by log level to avoid users from being inundated with log line output.

```bash
➜  linkerd2 ✗ bin/linkerd logs -h
Tail logs from containers in the Linkerd control plane.

Usage:
  linkerd logs [flags]

Examples:
  # Tail logs from all containers in the prometheus control plane component
  linkerd logs --control-plane-component prometheus

  # Tail logs from the linkerd-proxy container in the grafana control plane component
  linkerd logs --control-plane-component grafana --container linkerd-proxy

  # Tail logs from the linkerd-proxy container in the controller component beginning with the last two lines
  linkerd logs --control-plane-component controller --container linkerd-proxy --tail 2

  # Tail logs from the linkerd-proxy container in the controller component showing timestamps for each line
  linkerd logs --control-plane-component controller --container linkerd-proxy --timestamps


Flags:
  -c, --container string                 Tail logs from the specified container. Options are 'public-api', 'proxy-api', 'tap', 'destination', 'prometheus', 'grafana' or 'linkerd-proxy'
      --control-plane-component string   Tail logs from the specified control plane component. Default value (empty string) causes this command to tail logs from all resources marked with the 'linkerd.io/control-plane-component' label selector
  -h, --help                             help for logs
  -s, --since duration                   Duration of how far back logs should be retrieved (default 48h0m0s)
      --tail int                         Last number of log lines to show for a given container. -1 does not show previous log lines (default -1)
  -t, --timestamps                       Print timestamps for each given log line

Global Flags:
      --api-addr string            Override kubeconfig and communicate directly with the control plane at host:port (mostly for testing)
      --context string             Name of the kubeconfig context to use
      --kubeconfig string          Path to the kubeconfig file to use for CLI requests
  -l, --linkerd-namespace string   Namespace in which Linkerd is installed [$LINKERD_NAMESPACE] (default "linkerd")
      --verbose                    Turn on debug logging
```

```bash
➜  linkerd2  ✗ bin/linkerd logs --control-plane-component web --container web --timestamps
+ linkerd linkerd-web-5856d7cd96-qln4n › web
linkerd linkerd-web-5856d7cd96-qln4n web 2019-01-15T18:34:27.2293628Z time="2019-01-15T18:34:27Z" level=info msg="running version stable-2.1.0"
linkerd linkerd-web-5856d7cd96-qln4n web 2019-01-15T18:34:27.2309416Z time="2019-01-15T18:34:27Z" level=info msg="starting admin server on :9994"
linkerd linkerd-web-5856d7cd96-qln4n web 2019-01-15T18:34:27.2328459Z time="2019-01-15T18:34:27Z" level=info msg="starting HTTP server on :8084"
```

fixes #1994

Signed-off-by: Dennis Adjei-Baah <dennis@buoyant.io>
author: dadjeibaah

comments.author: grampelberg
comments.body:
- Could we more closely match the `kubectl logs` paradigm? In particular:

    ```bash
    -f, --follow=false: Specify if the logs should be streamed.
    --since=0s: Only return logs newer than a relative duration like 5s, 2m, or 3h. Defaults to
    all logs. Only one of since-time / since may be used.
    --tail=-1: Lines of recent log file to display. Defaults to -1 with no selector, showing all
    log lines otherwise 10, if a selector is provided.
    --timestamps=false: Include timestamps on each line in the log output
    ```

- How are you thinking about integrating this in with proxy logs eventually? It would be nice to   maintain a single command for both control plane and proxy logs.

    ```bash
    --control-plane=true: Show control plane logs
    --proxy=false: Show proxy logs
    --data-plane=false: Show data plane logs
    ```

    None of these are a great solution, maybe `--proxy` isn't required at all?

- It looks like we can just use stern wholesale what do you think about using that instead of doing it ourselves? They've got some good functionality there that I suspect will make our lives better in the long run.

@adleong should we do anything around log filtering here? It feels like that should just be handled server side (thinking about proxy logs in particular). I'd hate to have a cli option for DEBUG logs, but have the server side not configured for it. If we could dynamically configure everything, then that would be *amazing*. Unfortunately, I don't think some of the control plane components could ever be made to support it (looking at you grafana and prometheus).

comments.author: adleong
comments.body:
I think it's definitely useful to be able to filter client side.  With the server components having a default log level of INFO and the CLI defaulting to filtering down to WARN.  Perhaps a nice compromise would be that we can detect the log levels of the server components (by parsing their ENV or by adding an annotation perhaps) and have the CLI exit with an error if you try to specify a log level higher than what the server is configured for.  Things are a bit more complex with the proxy because log levels can be set per module, but I think as long as the default log level is INFO, it should work okay.

My preference is to focus on the most common basic use case.  `kubectl logs` is always there as a more advanced tool if you need to get more granular or dive deeper.

title: Add support for retries
body:
This change adds the `isRetryable` property to routes in a service profile.  This causes the proxy to retry failed requests to retryable routes whenever it is able to.  A retry budget may also be added to the service profile which can limit the number of retries.  The `linkerd profile --template` command has been updated to describe these new properties.

The `linkerd routes` command has been updated to differentiate between actual and effective RPS and success rate.  This data is only available for outgoing queries i.e. when the `--to` flag is used.  Effective metrics are the metrics as observed by the client whereas actual metrics are the metrics which describe the requests and responses which are actually sent on the wire.  Adding retries will usually increase the actual RPS and increase the effective success rate while leaving the actual success rate and effective RPS unchanged.

```
$linkerd routes deploy/books --to svc/authors
ROUTE                     SERVICE   EFFECTIVE_SUCCESS   EFFECTIVE_RPS   ACTUAL_SUCCESS   ACTUAL_RPS   LATENCY_P50   LATENCY_P95   LATENCY_P99
HEAD /authors/{id}.json   authors              68.28%          2.4rps           45.21%       3.6rps          14ms          40ms          48ms
[UNKNOWN]                 authors               0.00%          0.0rps            0.00%       0.0rps           0ms           0ms           0ms
```
author: adleong

comments.author: adleong
comments.body:
## How I tested

1. Install Linkerd control plane and booksapp
2. Run `linkerd routes deploy/webapp --to svc/books`, notice: no useful data
3. Apply service profiles from swagger:
```
curl https://run.linkerd.io/booksapp/webapp.swagger | linkerd profile --open-api - webapp | kubectl apply -f -
curl https://run.linkerd.io/booksapp/authors.swagger | linkerd profile --open-api - authors | kubectl apply -f -
curl https://run.linkerd.io/booksapp/books.swagger | linkerd profile --open-api - books | kubectl apply -f -
```
4. Run `linkerd routes deploy/webapp --to svc/books`: Notice SR on the POST and PUT routes is ~50%
5. Run `linkerd routes deploy/books --to svc/authors`: Notice SR on the HEAD route is ~50%
6. Download the authors profile: `kubectl -n linkerd get sp/authors.default.svc.cluster.local -o yaml > authors-profile.yaml`
7. Edit the HEAD route to be retryable:
```
  - condition:
      method: HEAD
      pathRegex: /authors/[^/]*\.json
    name: HEAD /authors/{id}.json
    isRetryable: true
```
8. Apply the new profile `kubectl apply -f authors-profile.yaml`
9. Run `linkerd routes deploy/books --to svc/authors` notice effective SR go to 100%
10. Run `linkerd routes deploy/webapp --to svc/books` notice SR go to 100%

documented.

title: Setup port-forwarding for linkerd dashboard command
body:
This branch switches the `linkerd dashboard` command from using the kubernetes service proxy to access the web UI, to instead using port-forward to access the web pod directly. This simplifies the URLs displayed in the dashboard, and it removes our direct dependency on "k8s.io/kubernetes" 🎉 

As part of this change, I fixed a bug with `linkerd dashboard`, where the proxy would not start until after the dashboard had been successfully loaded in a browser (relates to #2047). And I've updated the integration tests to use port-forwarding instead of proxying to access pods running in the test environment.

Fixes #1696.

title: Added `linkerd uninject` command
body:
uninject.go iterates through the resources annotations, labels,
initContainers and Containers, removing what we know was injected by
linkerd.

The biggest part of this commit is the refactoring of inject.go, to make
it more generic and reusable by uninject. Some common parts were moved
into inject_util.go but others common parts remained in inject.go to
ease review and will then later get moved (marked with a comment).

The entry-point function `transformInput` (formerly called
`runInjectCmd`) receives as a parameter the function holding the logic
specific for injection (`injectResource`) or uninjection
(`uninjectResource`).

`injectResource` was split into the `parse` (reused by uninject) and
`injectResource` methods on the new `resourceConfig` receiver. That
receiver holds all the info required for the injection/uninjection.

The idea is that in a following PR this functionality will get reused by
`linkerd inject` to uninject as as preliminary step to injection, as a
solution to #1970.

This was tested successfully on emojivoto with:

```
1) inject:
kubectl get -n emojivoto deployment -o yaml | bin/linkerd inject - |
kubectl apply -f -
2) uninject:
kubectl get -n emojivoto deployment -o yaml | bin/linkerd uninject - |
kubectl apply -f -
```

title: Hash JS bundle to expire cache
body:
JavaScript assets could be cached across Linkerd releases, showing an
out of date ui, or a broken page.

title: Improve routes command to list all routes
body:
Fixes #1875 

This change improves the `linkerd routes` command in a number of important ways:

* The restriction on the type of the `--to` argument is lifted and any resource type can now be used.  Try `--to ns/books`, `--to po/webapp-ABCDEF`, `--to au/linkerd.io`, or even `--to svc`.
* All routes for the target will now be populated in the table, even if there are no Prometheus metrics for that route.
* [UNKNOWN] has been renamed to [DEFAULT]
* The `Service/Authority` column will now list `Service` in all cases except for when an authority target is explicitly requested.

```
$ linkerd routes deploy/traffic --to deploy/webapp
ROUTE                       SERVICE   SUCCESS      RPS   LATENCY_P50   LATENCY_P95   LATENCY_P99
GET /                        webapp   100.00%   0.5rps          50ms         180ms         196ms
GET /authors/{id}            webapp   100.00%   0.5rps         100ms         900ms         980ms
GET /books/{id}              webapp   100.00%   0.9rps          38ms          93ms          99ms
POST /authors                webapp   100.00%   0.5rps          35ms          48ms          50ms
POST /authors/{id}/delete    webapp   100.00%   0.5rps          83ms         180ms         196ms
POST /authors/{id}/edit      webapp     0.00%   0.0rps           0ms           0ms           0ms
POST /books                  webapp    45.16%   2.1rps          75ms         425ms         485ms
POST /books/{id}/delete      webapp   100.00%   0.5rps          30ms          90ms          98ms
POST /books/{id}/edit        webapp    56.00%   0.8rps          92ms         875ms         975ms
[DEFAULT]                    webapp     0.00%   0.0rps           0ms           0ms           0ms
```

This is all made possible by a shift in the way we handle the destination resource.  When we get a request with a `ToResource`, we use the k8s API to find all Services which include at least one pod belonging to that resource.  We then fetch all service profiles for those services and display the routes from those serivce profiles.  

This shift in thinking also precipitates a change in the TopRoutes API where we no longer need special cases for `ToAll` (which can be specified by `--to au`) or `ToAuthority` (which can be specified by `--to au/<authority>`) and instead can use a `ToResource` to handle all cases.  We deprecate the old fields but continue to support them in the API for now.
author: adleong

title: WIP: CNI Plugin
body:
Issue: #1887

Instructions:
1. Install minikube
2. Start minikube with cni enabled: minikube start --kubernetes-version v1.10.8 --memory 8192 --cpus 4 --network-plugin=cni --extra-config=kubelet.network-plugin=cni
3. Install calico:
    3a. kubectl apply -f https://docs.projectcalico.org/v3.4/getting-started/kubernetes/installation/hosted/etcd.yaml
    3b. kubectl apply -f https://docs.projectcalico.org/v3.4/getting-started/kubernetes/installation/hosted/calico.yaml.
4. Build the linkerd binaries and docker images:
    4a. bin/update-go-deps-shas
    4b. bin/docker-build then copy the docker images over to minikube manually (docker save gcr.io/linkerd-io/[component]:[tag] | (eval $(minikube docker-env) && docker load)) OR bin/mkube bin/docker-build
5. Install the CNI Daemonset: linkerd install-cni | kubectl apply -f - (you can use some of the proxy configuration flags here too)
6. Install linkerd control-plane without init containers: linkerd install --no-init-container | kubectl apply -f -
7. Install and inject without an init container your service: linkerd inject --no-init-container deployment.yaml | kubectl apply -f - as long as deployment.yaml has the linkerd.io/setup-iptables: "true" annotation

Note:
You can also use the auto-inject feature by adding --proxy-auto-inject --tls=optional to the linkerd install --no-init-container command as long as deployment.yaml has the linkerd.io/setup-iptables: "true" annotation

comments.author: codeman9
comments.body:
> In terms of getting this merged, my biggest concern is that the linkerd-cni.yaml file is not templated. It hardcodes the version of the docker image to use, as well as the namespace where linkerd is running. Before we instruct users to start using that file, we'll need to give them some better options for configuring it. Ideally, we could append the CNI resources to the install config by passing a flag to the `linkerd install` command, but it seems like the CNI installation needs to happen in two parts right now. I'll try to see if I can come up with other ways to go about it.

The idea would be to have the linkerd-cni.yaml file go away and just be part of the `--no-init-containers` flag of `linkerd install`. This presents some challenges, though, since the DaemonSet really needs to be in place before the rest of the system is installed. I've found a couple ideas while researching and all of them seem to require an outside program to monitor the state of a particular pod and report back or continue when ready. This seems possible, but would require more smarts in the `linkerd install` command which, right now is nice because it just produces a .yaml you can apply.

Perhaps just having explicit instructions is the easiest. So something like:

Instructions:
Run `linkerd install --no-init-containers` to output the linkerd2 configuration that can be deployed on clusters which do not allow `CAP_NET_ADMIN`. When you do this, you will not be able to `linkerd install --no-init-containers | kubectl apply -f -` because there is an additional DaemonSet that needs to be created and deployed first. Instead, you need to output the results from the command to a .yaml file on your filesystem and then apply the `linkerd-cni` DaemonSet that is contained within that file. Once that is ready, you can apply the rest of the file. Alternatively, you can apply the entire file, wait for the DaemonSet to be ready, then delete and redeploy the pods for the linkerd2 components.

title: Modify all health checks to be specified via enums
body:
Modify all health checks to be specified via enums

The set of health checks to be executed were dependent on a combination
of check enums and boolean options.

This change modifies the health checks to be governed strictly by a set
of enums. This change does not add or remove any checks, but rather
moves checks into more granular categories, such that any set of checks
that are toggle-able are defined together under a single category.

This is a first step in cleaning up the `linkerd check` code, and moving towards #1471.

Next steps:
- tightly couple category IDs to names
- tightly couple checks to their parent categories
- programmatic control over check ordering

Signed-off-by: Andrew Seigner <siggy@buoyant.io>
author: siggy

title: Leave dashboard command running when open URL fails
body:
The `linkerd dashboard` command attempts to load the dashboard URL in the user's browser, and if it fails for any reason, the process exits. Instead, when opening the dashboard fails, we'll now leave the process running and instruct the user to manually load the dashboard. It looks like this:

```
Linkerd dashboard available at:
http://127.0.0.1:52513
Grafana dashboard available at:
http://127.0.0.1:52513/grafana
Opening Linkerd dashboard in the default browser
The file /Users/kl/workspace/go/src/github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/invalid does not exist.
Failed to open Linkerd dashboard automatically
Visit http://127.0.0.1:52513 in your browser to view the dashboard
```

This will allow users running on systems where we can't automatically open the dashboard to still use the command without needing to add the `--show url` flag.

Fixes #2014.
Fixes #2047.
author: klingerf

title: Group checkers by category
body:
The linkerd check command organized the various checks via loosely
coupled category IDs, category names, and checkers themselves, all with
ordering defined by consumers of this code.

This change removes category IDs in favor of category names, groups all
checkers by category, and enforces ordering at the HealthChecker
level.

Part of #1471, depends on #2078.

Signed-off-by: Andrew Seigner <siggy@buoyant.io>
author: siggy

title: Update check and inject output

The outputs of the `check` and `inject` commands did not vary much
between successful and failed executions, and were a bit verbose and
challenging to parse.

Reorganize output of `check` and `inject` commands, to provide more
output when errors occur, and less output when successful.

`linkerd check`

- introduce `hintURL`'s, to provide doc links when checks fail

title: Refactor `install`'s `render` output to be helm compatible
body:
# Problem
In order to refactor `install` to allow for a more flexible configuration, we
should start with the format of the YAML that it renders. Using the Helm
YAML format will make it easier add flexible configuration options in the
future. Currently, the rendered template that `install` produces does not
follow this format.

# Solution
Use the internals that Helm itself uses to render an inject template that
follows the same formatting rules. Helm's `template` cmd provides a good
outline of what is needed to make Linkerd's `install` cmd work as if it was
a Chart.

# Validation
There are no new tests, but there may not be anything to test at this stage.
This is a WIP PR towards the ultimate goal of `install` allowing a more
flexible configuration.

However, `install` now uses all the Helm `template` internals and therefore
satisfies the needed properties for Helm Charts.

Signed-off-by: Kevin Leimkuhler <kevin@kleimkuhler.com>

title: Add cli command to install linkerd service profiles
body:
This introduces a `linkerd install-sp` command to install service
profiles into the linkerd control plane. It installs one service profile
for each of controller-api, proxy-api, prometheus, and grafana.

Fixes #1901

Signed-off-by: Andrew Seigner <siggy@buoyant.io>
author: siggy

comments.author: grampelberg
comments.body: Is there any reason to not just do this by default as part of `linkerd install`?

comments.author: siggy
comments.body:
@grampelberg i'd love to include this as part of `linkerd install`, unfortunately there's a race condition where service profile support via the `linkerd.io/v1alpha1` apiextension (also installed via `linkerd install`) is not available by the time `kubectl apply` gets around to installing the service profiles themselves.

fwiw, istio works around this by having all CRDs / apiextensions installed in a preliminary step:
https://github.com/knative/serving/issues/2195
https://istio.io/docs/setup/kubernetes/quick-start/#installation-steps

i opted to keep the default `linkerd install` as a single step, which i hope will have the added benefit of educating users that installing service profiles is a thing you do, generally, after you've gotten linkerd up and running.

@adleong i did consider the approach of the control-plane posting its own service profiles. i opted for this approach due to the added complexity and added permissions it would require.

another cool option may be to wait for autogeneration of service profiles from proto files, and generate/submit that at install time.

title: Fix Unicode and color output for Windows
body:
The default font in Windows console did not support the Unicode
characters recently added to check and inject commands. Also the color
library the linkerd cli depends on was not being used in a
cross-platform way.

Replace the existing Unicode characters used in `check` and `inject`
with characters available in most fonts, including Windows console.
Similarly replace the spinner used in `check` with one that uses
characters available in most fonts.

Modify `check` and `inject` to use `color.Output` and `color.Error`,
which wrap `os.Stdout` and `os.Stderr`, and perform special
tranformations when on Windows.

Add a `--no-color` option to `linkerd logs`. While stern uses the same
color library that `check`/`inject` use, it is not yet using the
`color.Output` API for Windows support. That issue is tracked at:
https://github.com/wercker/stern/issues/69

Relates to https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/pull/2087

Signed-off-by: Andrew Seigner <siggy@buoyant.io>

title: Rename fast-build to build-cli-bin, fix shasum

`fast-build` was performing a full Docker build minus the cli, and then
building cli locally. Separately, shasum was called with a `-p flag,

`docker-build-cli-bin`.

title: Add a --tap flag to the linkerd profile command
body:
Adds the ability to generate a service profile by running a tap for a configurable amount of time, and using the route results from the routes seen during the tap.

e.g. ` bin/go-run cli profile web --tap deploy/web -n emojivoto --tap-duration 2s`

title: Fix issue where linkerd check would panic with replicationcontroller pod name in control plane
body:
When running Linkerd check with a control plane namespace that may contain an additional pod with a replication controller ID for pod names instead of a replicaSet ID, the check command panics because of an "index out of bounds" error.

This PR adds a check to make sure that, when parsing pod names during the `checkControllerRunning` healthcheck, we only check for linkerd control plane pods and that the pod name results in four or more substrings when split on '-'. This prevents the check from panicking when encountering a replication controller ID pod name.

Fixes #2084 

Signed-off-by: Dennis Adjei-Baah <dennis@buoyant.io>

title: GetProfiles should always respond immediately
body:
When `GetProfiles` is called for a destination that does not have a service profile, the proxy-api service does not return any messages until a service profile is created for that service.  This can be interpreted as hanging, and can make it difficult to calculate response latency metrics.

Change the behavior of the API to always return a service profile message immediately.  If the service does not have a service profile, the default service profile is returned.

Signed-off-by: Alex Leong <alex@buoyant.io>
author: adleong

title: Add support for timeouts in service profiles
body:
Fixes #2042 

Adds a new field to service profile routes called `timeout`.  Any requests to that route which take longer than the given timeout will be aborted and a 504 response will be returned instead.  If the timeout field is not specified, a default timeout of 1 second is used.

title: Add pod spec annotation to disable injection in CLI and auto-injector
body:
This branch adds support for a new annotation -- `linkerd.io/inject` -- which can be used to control whether or not a pod will be injected. It applies to both the CLI and the auto-injector. If set to "disabled" in the pod spec, we'll skip injection for that pod. The same annotation can be used on the namespace when auto-inject is enabled, to control wether or not all pods in the namespace should be injected. When the annotation is set in both the namespace and the pod spec, the pod spec label takes precedence.

As part of this change, I removed the previous use of the `linkerd.io/auto-inject` label that controls auto-injection, since we couldn't use the label selector from the MWC and still support the override behavior described above.

Fixes #1820.

Having said all that, I'm inclined to just remove the label support as part of this branch. Does that work for you?

title: Introduce go generate to embed static templates
body:
# Problem
In order to switch Linkerd template rendering to use `.yaml` files, static
assets must be bundled in the Go binary for use by `linkerd install`.

# Solution
The solution should not affect the local development process of building and
testing.

[vfsgen](https://github.com/shurcooL/vfsgen) generates Go code that statically
implements the provided `http.FileSystem`. Paired with `go generate` and Go
[build tags](https://golang.org/pkg/go/build/), we can continue to use the
template files on disk when developing with no change required.

In `!prod` Go builds, the `cli/static/templates.go` file provides a
`http.FileSystem` to the local templates. In `prod` Go builds, `go generate
./cli` generates `cli/static/generated_templates.gogen.go` that statically
provides the template files.

When built with `-tags prod`, the executable will be built with the staticlly
generated file instead of the local files.

# Validation
The binaries were compiled locally with `bin/docker-build`. The binaries were
then tested with `bin/test-run (pwd)/target/cli/darwin/linkerd`. All tests
passed.

No change was required to successfully run `bin/go-run cli install`. No change
was required to run `bin/linkerd install`.

Fixes #2153

Signed-off-by: Kevin Leimkuhler <kevin@kleimkuhler.com>

title: Consolidate timeouts for `linkerd check`
body:
- Moved the creation of contexts from inside the methods targeted by the checks into a single place in the runCheck() and runCheckRPC() methods where the context is built using a hard-coded timeout of 30 seconds (we decided it's not necessary to expose this as a flag).
- Some checks rely on k8s' client-go, which doesn't allow passing along contexts, but it let's us setting the Timeout manually.
- Reworded the description for the --wait option.

How I tested this
------------------------
I introduced a sleep of 25s in the `Version` API and then I ran `linkerd check --verbose --wait 80s`.
We can see the "can query the control plane API" check (which uses the Version API) succeed after 25s:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/554287/52154147-b0f82a80-264a-11e9-926e-6a8451c62697.png)

Then I changed that sleep to 35s and now the check fails after 30s and it gets retried until we go past the 80s overall timeout:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/554287/52154445-da658600-264b-11e9-89ca-b35732f32c9b.png)

Whenever the check call fails (as opposed to timing out), the check fails immediately (and is retried if `fatal` is false). I tested this just by removing the CP and running the checks. So it seems this wouldn't mean that increasing the timeout per-check would affect how we do retries. Although I would like to see this get better validated under more scenarios.

comments.author: siggy
comments.body:
@dadjeibaah Good question re: the new discovery protobuf. The decision to add this as a new interface, implemented by both `public-api` and `proxy-api` processes, was motivated by two factors:
1) The ServicePort endpoint state we want lives in the `proxy-api` process, so we need a new endpoint into that process. `proxy-api`'s only existing interface is the proxy-facing [Destination service](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy-api/blob/36f54ad8354c677b22a768a4c1c9ecc087ff4aa8/proto/destination.proto#L49), not a good fit for a controller-facing debug endpoint.
2) The CLI currently only talks to `public-api`. Implementing a CLI->`public-api`->`proxy-api` passthrough maintains the `public-api` as the CLI's sole interface into the control-plane.

A few alternatives, in decreasing order of viability:
1) Add a new `service Discovery { rpc Endpoints }` and related to `public.proto`. Implement `rpc Endpoints` in both `public-api` and `proxy-api` to support CLI -> `public-api` -> `proxy-api` passthrough. This avoids creating a new `discovery.proto`, at the expense of `proxy-api` implementing a subset of the APIs defined in `public.proto`.
2) Implement discovery interface in the `proxy-api` (as in this PR), but connect the CLI directly to `proxy-api`, avoiding changes to `public-api`. This creates a dependency between CLI and `proxy-api`, differing from the `tap` pattern of keeping `public-api` the sole interface for the CLI to talk to the control-plane.
3) Add `service Discovery { rpc Endpoints}` to [Destination service](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy-api/blob/36f54ad8354c677b22a768a4c1c9ecc087ff4aa8/proto/destination.proto#L49), coupling a proxy-facing `Destination` service with a CLI-facing `Discovery` service.

* API messages to proxy

This does a good job of allowing us to introspect the endpoints watcher cache.  How do we decide which other layers also require introspection?  What classes of bugs cause data inconsistency at which layers?

title: Use the proper controller identity when configuring pods with TLS
body:
Since 37ae423b, deployments have been prefixed with `linkerd-`; however
the inject logic was not changed to take this into consideration when
constructing the controller's identity.

This means that the proxy's client to the control plane has been unable to
establish TLS'd communcation to the proxy-api. Previously, the proxy would
silently fall back to plaintext, but in master this behavior recently changed to
be stricter, so this bug will prevent the proxy from connecting to proxy-api
in any way.

title: Read service profiles from client or server namespace instead of control namespace
body:
Fixes #2077 

When looking up service profiles, Linkerd always looks for the service profile objects in the Linkerd control namespace.  This is limiting because service owners who wish to create service profiles may not have write access to the Linkerd control namespace.

Instead, we have the control plane look for the service profile in both the client namespace (as read from the proxy's `proxy_id` field from the GetProfiles request and from the service's namespace.  If a service profile exists in both namespaces, the client namespace takes priority.  In this way, clients may override the behavior dictated by the service.

This should not be merged until https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/pull/183 is merged.
author: adleong

comments.body:
Here's how I tested this change:

1. Build docker images: `bin/docker-build`.  This step is important because it picks up a newer version of the proxy.
2. Install Linkerd `bin/linkerd install | kubectl apply -f -`
3. Install booksapp: `curl https://run.linkerd.io/booksapp.yml | bin/linkerd inject - | kubectl apply -f -`
4. Create a new namespace `kubectl create ns alex`
5. Move the traffic deployment to the new namespace: `kubectl get deploy/traffic -o yaml | sed 's/namespace: default/namespace: alex/' | sed 's/webapp:7000/webapp.default:7000/' | kubectl apply -f -`
6. Delete the old deployment: `kubectl delete deploy/traffic`
7. Now we have a traffic deployment in the alex namespace sending requests to the webapp service in the default namespace.
8. Create a service profile for the default namespace: `curl https://run.linkerd.io/booksapp/webapp.swagger | bin/linkerd profile --open-api - webapp > service-profile.yaml`
9. Create a service profile for the alex namespace: 
```
echo "apiVersion: linkerd.io/v1alpha1
kind: ServiceProfile
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: null
  name: webapp.default.svc.cluster.local
  namespace: alex
spec:
  routes:
  - condition:
      pathRegex: '.*'
    name: WHO CARES" > client-profile.yaml
```
10. Try various combinations of creating and deleting those two profiles and running the commands:
```
bin/linkerd routes -n alex deploy --to deploy/webapp --to-namespace default
```
and

```
bin/linkerd routes deploy/webapp
```

title: Add support for `basePath` in swagger 2.0 files
body:
Fixes #2175

Say we've got this swagger file with `basePath` set, and only relative paths declared:
```
swagger: "2.0"
info:
  title: Sample API
  description: API description in Markdown.
  version: 1.0.0
basePath: /emojivoto.v1.EmojiService
schemes:
  - https
paths:
  /ListAll:
    get:
      summary: Returns a list of emojis.
      description: foobar
      produces:
        - application/json
      responses:
        200:
          description: OK
```
Producing a ServiceProfile through `linkerd profile --open-api` should produce this output:
```
apiVersion: linkerd.io/v1alpha1
kind: ServiceProfile
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: null
  name: foo.default.svc.cluster.local
  namespace: linkerd
spec:
  routes:
  - condition:
      method: GET
      pathRegex: /emojivoto\.v1\.EmojiService/ListAll
    name: GET /emojivoto.v1.EmojiService/ListAll
    responseClasses:
    - condition:
        status:
          max: 200
          min: 200
```
note that `pathRegex` now prepends the value of `basePath`. It was being ignored.

title: If GOPATH env var not set, use build.Default.GOPATH
body:
Follow-up to #2189 

When the env var GOPATH is not set, go defaults to `$HOME/go`:
```
$ echo $GOPATH

$ go env
GOARCH="amd64"
GOBIN=""
GOCACHE="/home/alpeb/.cache/go-build"
GOEXE=""
GOFLAGS=""
GOHOSTARCH="amd64"
GOHOSTOS="linux"
GOOS="linux"
GOPATH="/home/alpeb/go"
...
```
That was the case in my machine, which `linkerd install` didn't like. So I updated the part where GOPATH is used to take that into account.

title: Improve ServiceProfile validation in linkerd check
body:
The `linkerd check` command was doing limited validation on
ServiceProfiles.

Make ServiceProfile validation more complete, specifically validate:
- types of all fields
- presence of required fields
- presence of unknown fields
- recursive fields

Also move all validation code into a new `Validate` function in the
profiles package.

Validation of field types and required fields is handled via
`yaml.UnmarshalStrict` in the `Validate` function. This motivated
migrating from github.com/ghodss/yaml to a fork, sigs.k8s.io/yaml.

Fixes #2190

title: Modify klog to be verbose when controller log-level is set to debug
body:
The controller logs innocuous messages when control plane proxies aren't ready to route requests during startup from each control plane component. i.e. tap, public-api and proxy-api. Setting the log level in the control plane to `INFO` would not hide these log messages and would still show up on control plane startup.

title: CNI: Removed unnecessary tolerations; added created-by annotation.
body:
Signed-off-by: Cody Vandermyn <cody.vandermyn@nordstrom.com>

In our cluster, we have some nodes that are tainted with `NoSchedule` and this means that only "master"-level pods will be installed on those nodes (pods that tolerate `NoSchedule`). The linkerd-cni plugin only needs to be installed and executed on nodes that will have "user" pods on them so the output .yaml does not need any special tolerations. Installing the linkerd-cni plugin on nodes that will never have "user" pods scheduled on them by default is unnecessary.

I also removed the `scheduler.alpha.kubernetes.io/critical-pod: ''` based on this documentation which mentions that the annotation is only effective if the pod is in the `kube-system` namespace: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/guaranteed-scheduling-critical-addon-pods/

title: Replacing lodash filter with native filter to avoid additional import
body:
Fixes #2034 

@rmars and I set out to replace all instances of lodash filter with native filter in order to prevent the additional import. However, there was only one use of _filter that could be easily replaced, since our other uses depend on lodash's ability to handle empty variables, and the ability to filter both objects and arrays (JS's native filter is only for arrays). Switching to native filter in those cases would have required us to manually check the value of the variable, set it to an empty array and/or convert it from an object to an array.

comments.author: hawkw
comments.body:
@alpeb and @kleimkuhler:

I think it would definitely be possible to validate proxy log levels on the CLI, but I don't think "one of: panic, fatal, error, warn, info, debug" is sufficient to accept all valid log levels. 

A quick breakdown of the syntax for setting proxy log levels: 
+ `PROXY_LOG_LEVEL` is a comma-separated list of _log directives_
+ A *log directive* consists of either:
  - a *level* (e.g. `info`), which sets the global log level, or 
  - a *module path* (e.g. `foo` or `foo::bar::baz`),
  - a *module path*  followed by an equals sign and a *level* (e.g. `foo=warn` or `foo::bar::baz=debug`), which sets the log level for that module
+ A *level* is one of:
  - trace
  - debug
  - info
  - warn
  - error
+ A *module path* represents the path to a Rust module. it consists of one or more *module name*s, separated by `::`
+ A *module name* starts with a letter, and consists of alphanumeric characters and `_`

We can't easily have a list of valid module paths, since there's potentially a module path for every source code file in the proxy codebase or any of its dependencies. However, we _can_ validate that they're syntactically correct.

We could perhaps test that the log level matches a regex like 
```
(trace|debug|warn|info|error)|(\w|::)+|((\w|::)+=(trace|debug|warn|info|error)?)(?:,|$)*
```
(apologies for my mediocre regex skills)

For more information on the log level format, see https://docs.rs/env_logger/0.6.0/env_logger/#enabling-logging

title: Fix Dockerfile-proxy to error out if fetch fails
body:
`Dockerfile-proxy` executes several commands following
`bin/fetch-proxy`, but the subsequent commands were separated by
semicolon, so the overall RUN command would succeed regardless of what
`bin/fetch-proxy` returned. This meant that if `bin/docker-build-proxy`
was run on a proxy SHA prior to it being available, it would fail the
build, but cache the unsuccessful `fetch-proxy` command, and continue to
fail after the proxy becomes available.

This change concatenates `fetch-proxy` and subsequent commands using
ampersands, failing the build if `fetch-proxy` fails.

Signed-off-by: Andrew Seigner <siggy@buoyant.io>

title: Remove auto proxy inject 'Mutate' function tests
body:
The way these tests compare the hard-coded base64-encoded JSON patches with those generated by the proxy injector, is extremely brittle. Changing any of the proxy configuration causes these tests to break, even though the proxy injector itself isn't affected.

Also, the AdmissionRequest and AdmissionResponse types are "boundary objects" that are largely irrelevant to our code.

Fixes #2201 

Signed-off-by: Ivan Sim <ivan@buoyant.io>
author: ihcsim

comments.author: ihcsim
comments.body:
> Will this PR have new `Mutate` webhook tests

I've been debating about this. At this point, I think I won't add any more tests to the webhook simply because any additional tests will just end up doing the same thing i.e. comparing hard-coded strings. The webhook doesn't care about the proxy specs and configs; it just treats everything as YAML (for request body) and JSON (for response body). It doesn't even validate the response JSON patches; it simply sends the patches back to the k8s api server, and let it re-assemble the resource manifest.

comments.body:
Thanks for tackling this! I agree that maintaining these base64 strings is untenable. I haven't given this too much thought, but how much work do you think it would be to have the tests validate the responses automatically using the CLI code that generates injected YAML?

We could still remove the base64 response fixtures, fixing #2201, but we'd be able to assert that the patch matches what we'd expect to get from running `linkerd inject` manually. That would have the added benefit of guaranteeing that our two inject code paths are in sync, and it would have helped to detect issues like the one #2267.

Anyway, if it's an enormous amount of work, we can just remove the tests outright, but it seems like an opportunity to increase our coverage.

Okay so after thinking about this some more I think I'm back to thinking about the two things @siggy mentioned in https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/pull/2262#discussion_r256152913

1. Should we always query for TCP stats on every stat request?
2. Should TcpStats be integrated into the BasicStats struct?

### Pros/Cons for querying for tcp stats on every stat request
Pros: 
- simplifies logic, we won't need to check for `TcpStats: true` in stat requests
- Doubling the number of Prometheus queries doesn't seem to affect stat query performance in the tests we've done

Cons:
- feels icky to query for a bunch of data that we show in very few places
- in very large deployments in the future, with multiple users viewing the linkerd dashboard, this could be a problem

### Pros/Cons for integrating TcpStats into BasicStats
Pros:
- if we are always requesting tcp stats, it seems like they belong in "BasicStats"
- Simpler structure of returned data

Cons:
- If a resource is tcp-only and doesn't send HTTP traffic, we'll encounter the problem fixed in [90542f0](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/commit/90542f07fd9ba2a5e6a7e7a03898cda22d238a69), which is that we can't differentiate between zero and null values for TcpStats. - The current BasicStats object would better be named HttpStats as it's closer to that. So putting them together would be like mashing together different types of stats

This query represents the number of new connections that were opened in the query time window, but the protobuf documentation for the open_connections field says that we're returning:

```
  // number of currently open connections
  uint64 open_connections = 1;
```

These aren't the same thing; if we want to return the total number of open connections, then we need to instead use the `tcp_open_connections` gauge. I haven't tested it too thoroughly, but I think something like this would work:

```suggestion
	tcpConnectionsQuery  = "sum(tcp_open_connections%s) by (%s)"
```

Note that that query doesn't include a time window, so we'll need to make a change where the query is formatted to account for that.

title: Issue 2276: Do not log error when timeout is blank
body:
# Problem

When a route does not specify a timeout, the proxy-api defaults to the default
timeout and logs an error:

```
time="2019-02-13T16:29:12Z" level=error msg="failed to parse duration for route POST /io.linkerd.proxy.destination.Destination/GetProfile: time: invalid duration"
```

# Solution

We now check if a route timeout is blank. If it is not set, it is set to
`DefaultRouteTimeout`. If it is set, we try to parse it into a `Duration`.

A request was made to improve logging to include the service profile and
namespace as well.

# Validation

With valid service profiles installed, edit the `.yaml` to include an invalid
`timeout`:

```
...
name: GET /
timeout: foo
```

We should now see the following errors:

```
proxy-api time="2019-02-13T22:27:32Z" level=error msg="failed to parse duration for route 'GET /' in service profile 'webapp.default.svc.cluster.local' in namespace 'default': time: invalid duration foo"
```

This error does not show up when `timeout` is blank.

Fixes #2276

Signed-off-by: Kevin Leimkuhler <kevinl@buoyant.io>
author: kleimkuhler

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body: I might be mistaken, but I think you can just do `profile.Name` and `profile.Namespace`.

review_threads.author: kleimkuhler
review_threads.body:

Right - thanks!

title: Rename linkerd-proxy-api to linkerd-destination
body:
Up until now, the proxy-api controller service has been the sole service
that the proxy communicates with, implementing the majoriry of the API
defined in the `linkerd2-proxy-api` repo. But this is about to change:
linkerd/linkerd2-proxy-api#25 introduces a new Identity service; and
this service must be served outside of the existing proxy-api service
in the linkerd-controller deployment (so that it may run under a
distinct service account).

With this change, the "proxy-api" name becomes less descriptive. It's no
longer "the service that serves the API for the proxy," it's "the
service that serves the Destination API to the proxy." Therefore, it
seems best to bite the bullet and rename this to be the "destination"
service.
author: olix0r

title: Fix handling of kubeconfig server urls that include paths
body:
In #2206, we adjusted the way in which we build Kubernetes API URLs to handle API servers that include trailing slashes. Unfortunately in the process we started dropping the paths from API servers that include paths. This change semi-reverts the fix from #2206, to fix both issues. In the process, I've cleaned up some misleadingly-named variables and functions, and fixed some indentation issues in our test kubeconfig file.

Fixes #2304.

review_threads.author: siggy
klingerf
review_threads.body:
I'm ok with having `generateKubernetesAPIURLFor` and `generateKubernetesURL` co-exist in the code base, since `generateKubernetesAPIURLFor` wraps `generateKubernetesURL` and layers on additional functionality.

But I agree that hand-building API urls when `generateKubernetesAPIURLFor` could do that for us feels like a waste. So I could see the value in refactoring `getRequest` to accept a fully-formed URL, allowing the callers to first call `generateKubernetesAPIURLFor` and `generateKubernetesURL` as needed, but that feels like a bigger refactor, and I'm not sure it buys us much. I'm also a bit nervous updating `generateKubernetesAPIURLFor` to allow empty paths, since I feel like that could have unintended consequences. So I'm going to leave this as is for now, but we could consider a larger refactor later.

title: Split install template into component-specific files
body:
chart/templates/base.yaml is nearly 800 lines and contains the
kubernetes configurations for the marjority of the control plane.
Furthermore, its contents are not particularly organized (for example,
the prometheus RBAC bindings are in the middle of the controller's
configuration).

The size and complexity of this file makes it especially daunting to
introduce new functionality.

In order to make the situation easier to understand and change, this
splits base.yaml into several new template files: namespace, controller,
serviceprofile, and prometheus, and grafana. The `tls.yaml` template has
been renamed `ca.yaml`, since it installs the `linkerd-ca` resources.

This change also makes the comments uniform, adding a "header" to each
logical component.

title: Add discovery package for managing discovery API
body:
This is a follow-up to #2195, which introduced the discovery API for the public and proxy APIs, and #2281, which renamed the proxy API to the destination API. The original goal of this change was to update the public API package to stop importing the destination API package, by introducing a shared discovery API package on which they can both depend. Here's a full list of changes in this branch:

* Add a `controller/api/discovery` package for building the discovery client and providing test helpers
* Update public API main and discovery-client main to use the client builder from the discovery package
* Rename all imports of the discovery protobuf to `pb` or `discoveryPb`, which is more consistent with how we handle `tapPb` and `healthcheckPb`
* Update public API tests to use new discovery mock client, instead of using the client builder from the destination package
* Remove the `InitFakeDiscoveryServer` helper from the destination package, since it is only used in one test now
* Fix a bunch of remaining references to the proxy API in comments and variables
author: klingerf

Rather than making an API call for this, I think it would make sense to update the install YAML such that the `proxy-injector` pod mounts the `linkerd-config` configmap, and this process reads the config from the configmap directly (using a shared library for unmarshaling the config JSON back into their protobuf representations).

But for the sake of testing and until #2344 merges, 👍 to hardcoding the structs here for now.

review_threads.author: ihcsim
review_threads.body: Just a nit - I feel like this struct has become a grab bag of configs and non-config related fields. One thought is we should separate the different responsibilities into different structs. As an example, this struct can consist of just the `globalConfig` and `proxyConfig`. And if we made them anonymous fields, we can expose the underlying `Get` accessors. (It's convenient, but also means some of the pb types are exposed.)

review_threads.author: alpeb
review_threads.body: Given `globalConfig` and `proxyConfig` and the other fields in `ResourceConfig` are used all over `inject.go`, if we split them apart that'd mean the one that is no longer in the receiver will have to be passed around. Or did I misunderstand your point?

review_threads.author: ihcsim
review_threads.body: Following my [comment](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/pull/2334#discussion_r260481629) on the exported functions, if we also change `parse()` return values to include a struct that contains all the non-config fields, then we can simplify the `ResourceConfig` struct to just config-related fields and methods.

On the current master, this environment variable is only set when the container name is present in the `proxyOutboundCapacity` map that's provided as part of the `injectOptions` struct, and that map is only populated when we call inject from the install codepath. So it's not the case that injecting any prometheus container with the current master will automatically set this environment variable.

Here's a suggestion of how to fix it:

review_threads.author: klingerf
review_threads.body:
Yeah, I think this must be the source of https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/pull/2334#discussion_r261472515, but I can't figure out what's up.

Only the auto-inject webhook calls `WithNsAnnotations`, so for the CLI inject code path, I'd expect `conf.nsAnnotations` to be `nil`. For CLI inject, we only care about pod annotations, so I'd expect this return statement to be:

```
		return podAnnotation != k8s.ProxyInjectDisabled
```

But it looks like it's also OK to `return true` as written, since the `Injectable` call above this is already checking that the `linkerd.io/inject: disabled` annotation is not set. This is pretty subtle though, so if there was some way to make this easier to reason about, that would be great.

For the auto-inject use case, we're expecting `conf.nsAnnotations` to not be `nil`, since we've called `WithNsAnnotations`, in which case we'll proceed to the namespace annotation check later in this method. But my guess is that's it's still possible for `conf.nsAnnotations` to be `nil` even after calling `WithNsAnnotations`, if the namespace doesn't actually have any annotations. If that were the case (untested), then that would explain why the proxy injector is injecting into namespaces that don't contain the `linkerd.io/inject: enabled` annotation.

Anyway, we might need to refactor this slightly to make it easier to understand how the inject decision is made.

review_threads.body:
I noticed that this log line is printed as:

```
time="2019-03-01T21:39:06Z" level=info msg="working on deployment .."
```

Looks like the proxy injector is calling `WithMeta` with these fields:

```
WithMeta(request.Kind.Kind, request.Namespace, request.Name)
```

But I think the issue is that `request.Namespace` and `request.Name` could be blank, based on this documentation:

```
	// Name is the name of the object as presented in the request.  On a CREATE operation, the client may omit name and
	// rely on the server to generate the name.  If that is the case, this method will return the empty string.
	// +optional
	Name string `json:"name,omitempty" protobuf:"bytes,5,opt,name=name"`
	// Namespace is the namespace associated with the request (if any).
	// +optional
	Namespace string `json:"namespace,omitempty" protobuf:"bytes,6,opt,name=namespace"`
```

The previous implementation parsed `request.Object.Raw` as a Deployment object and used the deployment's name instead of `request.Name`. But if you took that approach, then you'd end up parsing the object meta twice -- once in webhook.go, and once in the `parse` func in this file.

Off the top of my head I can't think of a great way to fix this. If you moved the log line after the `parse` call, that would work, but it also suggests that we're not attaching the right metadata when calling `WithMeta`.

title: pkg/tls: Make it possible to load a CA from disk
body:
In preparation for creating an Identity service that can chain off of an
existing CA, it's necessary to both (1) be able to create an
intermediate CA that can be used by the identity service and (2) be able
to load a CA from existing key material.

This changes the public API of the `tls` package to deal in actual key
types (rather than opaque blobs) and provides a set of helpers that can
be used to convert these credentials between common formats.

title: Authorization-aware control-plane components
body:
The control-plane components relied on a `--single-namespace` param,
passed from `linkerd install` into each individual component, to
determine which namespaces they were authorized to access, and whether
to support ServiceProfiles. This command-line flag was redundant given
the authorization rules encoded in the parent `linkerd install` output,
via [Cluster]Role[Binding]s.

Modify the control-plane components to query Kubernetes at startup to
determine which namespaces they are authorized to access, and whether
ServiceProfile support is available. This allows removal of the
`--single-namespace` flag on the components.

Also update `bin/test-cleanup` to cleanup the ServiceProfile CRD.

TODO:
- Remove `--single-namespace` flag on `linkerd install`, part of #2164

Signed-off-by: Andrew Seigner <siggy@buoyant.io>

comments.body:
@grampelberg I assume we ignore `kube-system` by default since we're not expecting it to be in the mesh. I think this particular setting only applies to the Public API's `ListPods` endpoint.

To be clear, this PR is not changing anything related to `ignore-namespaces`, I had accidentally removed it thinking it was dead code, it's not.

We could potentially do authz checks individually for each namespace in the cluster and watch all namespaces that we have access to.  This would be helpful if you want a Linkerd control plane to manage a data plane that spans more than one namespace, but you don't have full cluster access.

That puts us in an intermediate state where users without cluster access can't install Linkerd without help from someone who does have cluster access to install the CRD, but that should be resolved once we have the install flow broken in two stages.

review_threads.author: siggy
review_threads.body:
Per [requirement 3](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/issues/2164#issuecomment-458265137):
```

```

review_threads.author: klingerf
review_threads.body: The service profile CRD is global to the whole cluster, in that all linkerd installs in the cluster rely on the same CRD being present. If I run this cleanup script in a cluster where I have linkerd installed in a different, non-test namespace, that linkerd install will break, which seems problematic. Would you mind reverting this change?

review_threads.author: siggy
review_threads.body: @klingerf Sure will revert. Should this motivate that we someone scope and/or name the ServiceProfile CRD to a specific Linkerd control-plane, similar to ClusterRoles?

review_threads.author: klingerf
review_threads.body:
Ideally yes, but in practice we can't change the name of our CRDs without also changing the name/group of the ServiceProfile resource itself, since Kubernetes requires that CRDs be named as follows:

> must be spec.names.plural+"."+spec.group

So a name like `linkerd-l5d-integration-serviceprofiles.linkerd.io` is invalid.

title: destination: Only return TLS identities when appropriate
body:
As described in #2217, the controller returns TLS identities for results even when the destination pod may not be able to participate in identity requester: specifically, the other pod may not have the same controller namespace or it may not be injected with identity.

This change introduces a new annotation, `linkerd.io/identity-mode` that is set when injecting pods (via both CLI and webhook). This annotation is _always_ added.

The destination service now only returns TLS identities when this annotation is set to `optional` on a pod and the destination pod uses the same controller. These semantics are expected to change before the 2.3 release.

Fixes #2217

title: Show TCP stats in `linkerd stat` when -o wide or -o json is used
body:
Show TCP stats in the linkerd stat output. They are not shown by default, but will be queried when using `-o wide` or `-o json`.

Also display read/write bytes as bytes per sec in the CLI and dashboard.

```
$ go run cli/main.go stat deploy -n linkerd -o wide
NAME                 MESHED   SUCCESS      RPS   LATENCY_P50   LATENCY_P95   LATENCY_P99   TLS   TCP CONNECTIONS   READ BYTES/SEC   WRITE BYTES/SEC
linkerd-controller      1/1   100.00%   0.9rps           1ms           8ms          10ms    0%                18         979.9bps          968.5bps
linkerd-grafana         1/1   100.00%   0.3rps         250ms         485ms         497ms    0%                 2         347.9bps          344.1bps
linkerd-prometheus      1/1   100.00%   0.2rps           1ms           3ms           3ms    0%                 7          51.5bps           47.7bps
linkerd-web             1/1   100.00%   0.3rps           2ms           3ms           3ms    0%                 2         332.2bps          328.4bps
```

Part of #2224
author: rmars

comments.author: adleong
comments.body: Are the read bytes and write bytes a rate or a total?  Windowed over some time period?  Or total over lifetime of the current connections?  Or total over the lifetime of the pod?  Do these counters reset if Prometheus restarts (unlike our other rate-based stats which only look at a recent window of data and can therefore recover from a Prometheus restart)?

comments.author: rmars
comments.body:
According to https://linkerd.io/2/reference/proxy-metrics/,  ```tcp_read_bytes_total: A counter of the total number of received bytes. This is updated when the connection closes.``` (So total over the connection lifetime).

The query we do to get the stats is windowed, though, (over the time_window specified in the stat query) so it looks like this:
```sum(increase(tcp_read_bytes_total{direction="inbound", namespace="default"}[1m])) by (namespace, deployment)```

Because they're windowed, I believe they'd recover like our other stats.

comments.author: adleong
comments.body: @rmars in that case, this is really bytes per window, right?  I feel like we should call that out in the column name somehow (bytes per 10m) or convert to bytes per second like we do for requests.

comments.author: rmars
comments.body: @adleong yeah that's a great point. Currently the column is called `READ BYTES` so we could either do `READ BYTES/MIN` or just divide the bytes by 60 and display them as `63472bps` or `63472b/sec`. The column headers will probably be the clearest (though for RPS we do call the column RPS and also have the unit RPS in there). If there's no preference I will go the rps route.

comments.author: grampelberg
comments.body: @rmars with zero context, my preference would be BPS for consistency.

review_threads.author: rmars
review_threads.body: I'm actually wondering whether we should just query tcp stats by default if `-o json` is specified, so that we don't have these weird null values

review_threads.author: grampelberg
review_threads.body: I was thinking maybe `-o wide` and `-o json`? I'd rather manage it that way than a new flag. In the future, we'll be able to do something like `kubectl` does with custom columns.

review_threads.author: rmars
review_threads.body: yeah I think auto including it with `-o wide` makes sense

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body: I think I'm agreeing with what you're both saying but I think we should always include all fields in json output, since width is not really a concern.

review_threads.author: siggy
review_threads.body:

title: Skip outbound port 443 in control-plane
body:
linkerd/linkerd2#2349 introduced a `SelfSubjectAccessReview` check at
startup, to determine whether each control-plane component should
establish Kubernetes watches cluster-wide or namespace-wide. If this
check occurs before the linkerd-proxy sidecar is ready, it fails, and
the control-plane component restarts.

This change configures each control-plane pod to skip outbound port 443
when injecting the proxy, allowing the control-plane to connect to
Kubernetes regardless of the `linkerd-proxy` state.

A longer-term fix should involve a more robust control-plane startup,
that is resilient to failed Kubernetes API requests. An even longer-term
fix could involve injecting `linkerd-proxy` as a Kubernetes "sidecar"
container, when that becomes available.

Workaround for #2407

Signed-off-by: Andrew Seigner <siggy@buoyant.io>

```bash
$ kubectl -n linkerd get po
NAME                                  READY     STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
linkerd-ca-779dbfd6f-q9qrn            2/2       Running   0          3m
linkerd-controller-5bb565b7f4-2swr6   4/4       Running   0          3m
linkerd-grafana-68948bdf8d-qmxvv      2/2       Running   0          3m
linkerd-prometheus-6cdbb7b75d-zmp6r   2/2       Running   0          3m
linkerd-web-64d58d9689-h56nn          2/2       Running   0          3m

$ kubectl -n linkerd logs -f pod/linkerd-controller-5bb565b7f4-2swr6 public-api
time="2019-02-27T22:05:38Z" level=info msg="running version git-e0268c40"
time="2019-02-27T22:05:39Z" level=info msg="waiting for caches to sync"
time="2019-02-27T22:05:40Z" level=info msg="caches synced"
time="2019-02-27T22:05:40Z" level=info msg="starting admin server on :9995"
time="2019-02-27T22:05:40Z" level=info msg="starting HTTP server on :8085"
```
author: siggy

review_threads.author: siggy
review_threads.body: @alpeb Would like your thoughts on this, is it expected? Is it related/resolved in #2334?

review_threads.author: klingerf
review_threads.body: These are used to build the `linkerd-proxy-injector-sidecar-config`, which is being removed in #2334. I don't think we need to update them to include 443 as part of this branch, since they only apply to deployments that are auto-injected by the proxy-injector process, and the control plane is manually injected, not auto-injected.

review_threads.author: klingerf
review_threads.body:
It's possible that `ignoreOutboundPorts` is non-empty at this point, so we should append instead of overwrite here:

```suggestion
	injectOptions.ignoreOutboundPorts = append(injectOptions.ignoreOutboundPorts, 443)
```

review_threads.author: klingerf
review_threads.body:
Sigh, it looks like appending to `ignoreOutboundPorts` here breaks our tests, since we reuse the same `installOptions` struct for multiple calls to this `render` method, and we're changing the options on each call. I think it would be better for `render` to not modify the `installOptions` struct that's passed in as a parameter, by creating a new instance of its embedded `proxyConfigOptions` struct. This should do the trick:

```diff
diff --git a/cli/cmd/install.go b/cli/cmd/install.go
index 8b449544..b6734ddd 100644
--- a/cli/cmd/install.go
+++ b/cli/cmd/install.go
@@ -317,7 +317,8 @@ func render(config installConfig, w io.Writer, options *installOptions) error {
 	}
 
 	injectOptions := newInjectOptions()
-	injectOptions.proxyConfigOptions = options.proxyConfigOptions
+	proxyConfigOptions := *options.proxyConfigOptions
+	injectOptions.proxyConfigOptions = &proxyConfigOptions
 
 	// Special case for linkerd-proxy running in the Prometheus pod.
 	injectOptions.proxyOutboundCapacity[config.PrometheusImage] = prometheusProxyOutboundCapacity
```

review_threads.author: klingerf
review_threads.body:
Oooh, I forgot that you could also write this as:

```diff
diff --git a/cli/cmd/install.go b/cli/cmd/install.go
index 8b449544..e350f912 100644
--- a/cli/cmd/install.go
+++ b/cli/cmd/install.go
@@ -317,7 +317,7 @@ func render(config installConfig, w io.Writer, options *installOptions) error {
 	}
 
 	injectOptions := newInjectOptions()
-	injectOptions.proxyConfigOptions = options.proxyConfigOptions
+	*injectOptions.proxyConfigOptions = *options.proxyConfigOptions
 
 	// Special case for linkerd-proxy running in the Prometheus pod.
 	injectOptions.proxyOutboundCapacity[config.PrometheusImage] = prometheusProxyOutboundCapacity
```

review_threads.author: siggy
review_threads.body:
Nice catches. Updates pushed, testing now.

Related (not at all for this PR, mostly academic, and possibly controversial)... I think this class of issue could be somewhat addressed with more intentional use of pointers vs. structs. In this case, modifying `render` to take `options installOptions` would be clearer that `options` is not mutable. Unfortunately `installOptions` itself contains a `*proxyConfigOptions`. So ideally this could change to be structs all the way down, and we only pass them as pointers when we intend to mutate them.

title: Introduce NET_ADMIN cli check
body:
The `linkerd-init` container requires the NET_ADMIN capability to modify
iptables. The `linkerd check` command was not verifying this.

Introduce a `has NET_ADMIN capability` check, which does the following:
1) Lists all available PodSecurityPolicies, if none found, returns
success
2) For each PodSecurityPolicy, validate one exists that:
    - the user has `use` access AND
    - provides `*` or `NET_ADMIN` capability

A couple limitations to this approach:
- It is testing whether the user running `linkerd check` has NET_ADMIN,
  but during installation time it will be the `linkerd-init` pod that
  requires NET_ADMIN.
- It assumes the presense of PodSecurityPolicies in the cluster means
  the PodSecurityPolicy admission controller is installed. If the
  admission controller is not installed, but PSPs exists that restrict
  NET_ADMIN, `linkerd check` will incorrectly report the user does not
  have that capability.

This PR also fixes the `can create CustomResourceDefinitions` check to
not specify a namespace when doing a `create` check, as CRDs are
cluster-wide.

Fixes #1732

Signed-off-by: Andrew Seigner <siggy@buoyant.io>
author: siggy

```
      CREATE

$ kubectl describe mutatingwebhookconfigurations linkerd-proxy-injector-webhook-config

Webhooks:
    ...
    Operations: # operations list isn't updated

...

$ kubectl describe mutatingwebhookconfigurations linkerd-proxy-injector-webhook-config
```

title: Remove GOPATH dependency from cli dev environment
body:
The `linkerd install` output relies on Helm templates in the `chart`
directory. In production cli builds, these templates are compiled into
the binary. In development, they are read from the file system. This
development code path relied on GOPATH to determine the location of the
`chart` directory. In anticipation of Go Modules support (#1488), we
cannot assume the repo is within the GOPATH.

This change removes the GOPATH dependency, and instead relies on
`runtime.Caller` to determine the root of the code repo. This change
only affects development (!prod) builds.

Prerequisite to #1488.

Signed-off-by: Andrew Seigner <siggy@buoyant.io>

title: Introduce cli command to fetch proxy metrics
body:
It's sometimes helpful to spotcheck proxy metrics from a specific pod,
but doing so with kubectl requires a few steps.

Introduce a new `linkerd metrics` command. When given a pod name and
namespace, returns a dump of the proxy's /metrics endpoint.

Also modify the k8s.portforward module to accept initialized k8s config
and client objects, to enable testing.

Fixes #2350.

Signed-off-by: Andrew Seigner <siggy@buoyant.io>

### Example outputs

```bash
$ bin/go-run cli metrics -n linkerd linkerd-controller-7ffbddccb-cp8v6
# HELP request_total Total count of HTTP requests.
# TYPE request_total counter
request_total{direction="inbound",tls="disabled"} 11541
```

```bash
$ bin/go-run cli metrics -h
Fetch metrics from a specific Linkerd proxy.

  This command initiates a port-forward to a given pod, and queries the /metrics
  endpoint on the Linkerd proxy running in that pod.

Usage:
  linkerd metrics [flags] (POD)

Examples:
  # Get metrics from pod-foo-bar in the default namespace.
  linkerd metrics pod-foo-bar

  # Get metrics from the linkerd-controller pod in the linkerd namespace.
  linkerd metrics -n linkerd $(
    kubectl --namespace linkerd get pod \
      --selector linkerd.io/control-plane-component=controller \
      --output jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'
  )

Flags:
  -h, --help               help for metrics
  -n, --namespace string   Namespace of pod (default "default")
```
author: siggy

title: cli: Always display stat tables for all routes
body:
## Problem

When an object has no previous route metrics, we do not generate a table for
that object.

The reasoning behind this was for reducing output of the following command:

```
$ linkerd routes deploy --to deploy/foo
```

For each deployment object, if it has no previous traffic to `deploy/foo`, then
a table would not be generated for it.

However, the behavior we see with that indicates there is an error even when a
Service Profile is installed:

```
$ linkerd routes deploy deploy/foo
Error: No Service Profiles found for selected resources
```

## Solution

Always generate a stat table for the queried resource object.

## Validation

I deployed [booksapp](https://github.com/buoyantIO/booksapp) with the `traffic`
deployment removed and Service Profiles installed.

Without the fix, `linkerd routes deploy/webapp` displays an error because there
has been no traffic to `deploy/webapp` without the `traffic` deployment.

With the fix, the following output is generated:

```
ROUTE                       SERVICE   SUCCESS      RPS   LATENCY_P50   LATENCY_P95   LATENCY_P99
GET /                        webapp     0.00%   0.0rps           0ms           0ms           0ms
GET /authors/{id}            webapp     0.00%   0.0rps           0ms           0ms           0ms
GET /books/{id}              webapp     0.00%   0.0rps           0ms           0ms           0ms
POST /authors                webapp     0.00%   0.0rps           0ms           0ms           0ms
POST /authors/{id}/delete    webapp     0.00%   0.0rps           0ms           0ms           0ms
POST /authors/{id}/edit      webapp     0.00%   0.0rps           0ms           0ms           0ms
POST /books                  webapp     0.00%   0.0rps           0ms           0ms           0ms
POST /books/{id}/delete      webapp     0.00%   0.0rps           0ms           0ms           0ms
POST /books/{id}/edit        webapp     0.00%   0.0rps           0ms           0ms           0ms
[DEFAULT]                    webapp     0.00%   0.0rps           0ms           0ms           0ms
```

Closes #2328

Signed-off-by: Kevin Leimkuhler <kevinl@buoyant.io>
author: kleimkuhler

```
[DEFAULT]    webapp    80.95%   6.7rps          30ms          97ms         175ms
```
