review_threads.author: zaharidichev
review_threads.body:
So this piece of logic was introduced some time ago because of the situation described right [here](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/pull/3066#issuecomment-512479059). 

So originally this logic was just skipping resources that were CNI when CNI was enabled to check resources that are not CNI. Now however, we want to use this logic to check resources  that are not CNI when CNI is enabled and disabled, we also want to use it to check CNI resources when CNI is enabled. review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body:
Ok, after taking a step back, searching my soul, communing with nature, and going on a vision quest, I think I know how to simplify this.  Behold.

The `checkClusterRoles` and related methods which are part of `LinkerdPreInstallCapabilityChecks` should use `linkerd.io/control-plane-ns,!linkerd.io/cni-resource` as the label selector to select all linkerd components except the CNI ones.  This should not require checking `noInitContainer` at all since this check ONLY cares about the regular resources, not the CNI ones.  This check is run by `LinkerdPreInstallCapabilityChecks` with shouldExist=false and `LinkerdConfigChecks` with shouldExist=true.  These checks should always run, regardless of if CNI is enabled or disabled.

We should add new `checkCniRoles` and related methods.  These methods should be checked if check is run in `--pre` mode with the CNI flag enabled and also should be checked if check is run in non-pre mode and CNI mode is marked as enabled in the linkerd config.  Specifying the CNI enabled flag to a value that differs from the value in the configmap` should be a check error.  These methods should use the `linkerd.io/cni-resource` label selector to only look at CNI resources and validate that they exist.

title: Enable no-use-before-define eslint rule
body:
This is a follow-up to #3882, which adopted a bunch of new linting rules
in our Javascript codebase. The [no-use-before-define](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/no-use-before-define) rule requires
moving some functions around, so I'm doing it in a separate branch.

Note that I was originally going to also enable the react/sort-comp rule
as part of this branch, but I decided that the sort ordering doesn't
work for our codebase.

Signed-off-by: Kevin Lingerfelt <kl@buoyant.io>
author: klingerf

comments.author: klingerf
comments.body:
@alpeb For sure! The definition of the react/sort-comp rule provided by the airbnb eslint config is super customized. You can view it here:

https://github.com/airbnb/javascript/blob/6d05dd898acfec3299cc2be8b6188be542824965/packages/eslint-config-airbnb/rules/react.js#L239-L288

The sorting that they specify only makes sense if we adhere to their naming conventions for function names. For instance a function named `onClick` would sort above a function named `getInitialState`. But we don't really use consistent function names throughout the codebase, so we end up with an ordering that feels pretty arbitrary just to satisfy that rule.

One common example is that in components that poll, such as Namespace.jsx, we usually define four functions, in this order: `startServerPolling`, `stopServerPolling`, `loadFromServer`, `handleApiError`. That roughly maps to the order in which they're executed in the lifecycle of the component. But with react/sort-comp enabled, they would need to be ordered as `handleApiError`, `loadFromServer`, `startServerPolling`, `stopServerPolling`, and that doesn't make a lot of sense to me. We could add our own version of react/sort-comp that specifies an ordering that works for our existing conventions, but for now I've just disabled it.

comments.author: alpeb
comments.body: @klingerf Makes perfect sense, thanks for the detailed explanation! :smile:

comments.author: klingerf
comments.body: @scottcarol Whoa, good find! I've refactored the Navigation tests in a63aeba6 to make it more streamlined and add the default props. Let me know what you think.

comments.author: scottcarol
comments.body: I'll also create a follow-up issue since our JS tests should not pass CI if there is a warning.

title: Utilize Common Name or Subject Alternate Name for access checks (#3459)
body:
**Subject**
Utilize Common Name or Subject Alternate Name for access checks (#3459)

**Problem**
When access restrictions to API server have been enabled with the `requestheader-allowed-names` configuration, only the _Common Name_ of the requestor certificate is being checked.  This check should include the use of _Subject Alternate Name_ attributes.

**Solution**
API server will now check the SAN attributes (DNS Names, Email Addresses, IP Addresses, and URIs) when determining accessibility for allowed names.

Fixes issue #3459

title: Tracing Add-on For Linkerd
body:
Follows #3794 

This PR adds the tracing components as a Linkerd Add-On. The add-on model follows the same consistent approach both through Helm and Linkerd CLI.

The following changes are part of this PR:
- **Pre-Requisite Changes**:
   - Moved some common yaml templates like `_nodeselectors.yaml`,etc required by multiple sub-charts to `partials` for re-use. Also updating the relevant helm tests.
- **Helm Changes**:
  - A Tracing sub-chart is added with `partials` dependency (for injection). This sub-chart is also added as an optional dependency for `linkerd2` chart.
  - `Values.yaml` has been updated to include the tracing add-on config.
  -  `linkerd-values` cm has been added which stores the add-on configurations, and will only be present when there is at-least one Add-On.
- **Install Path**:
   - Updates  `installOptions` to include a `config` option, through which the configuration for the add-ons is given to the CLI.
   -  During Install, A final step has been added to read config (if given), and the default Values will be overwritten by this.
   -  If there are any add-ons present, those sub-charts are loaded and rendered in this step, by passing both `.Values.global` and the add-on values to the sub-chart.
- **Upgrade Path**:
  - The upgrade path in the final stage, now first checks if the `linkerd-values` cm exists, and updates the default addon values with the values present in `linkerd-values`, this is done to have persistent config upgrades.
   - It then checks if there is a `config` option present, and overwrite the default values further with the options from the config file. This allows users to change configuration of add-ons during upgrades.
 
The logic to Overwrite the `values` struct, is done by this fork of mergo at https://github.com/pothulapati/mergo, because of this [issue/decision](https://github.com/imdario/mergo/issues/24) from the official project.

**To try `tracing` as an add-on:**
- Create a new config file as `config.yaml`
```yaml
tracing:
  enabled: true
```
- Now Run, 
`linkerd install --config config.yaml --control-plane-tracing | kubectl apply -f -` 
and see the magic happen ;)

@ihcsim @alpeb @zaharidichev @grampelberg
author: Pothulapati

comments.author: Pothulapati
comments.body:
**Process required to add new Add-Ons:**
- A sub-chart has to be created first at `/charts/linkerd2/add-ons/<add-on>`, and added as a dependency to the `linkerd2` sub-chart, with the condition field as `<add-on>.enabled` from the `linkerd2/values.yaml`. The `linkerd2/values.yaml` will be the file where the default config for add-ons will also be present.
- The sub-chart can optionally take a dependency on `partials` to have proxy injection by including the necessary templates.
- The `Values` struct in `pkg/charts/values.go` should have the relevant field for add-on, with the same structure as that of the one present in `Values.yaml`.
- The relevant add-on config struct will added at `pkg/charts/linkerd2/<add-on>.go`, and should also implement the `AddOn` interface, as that logic is used in the `install` and `upgrade` paths to render the add-on templates.
- Finally, The `mergeAddOnValues` and `checkAddOns` functions in `install.go` should be updated to check for the relevant newly added add-ons.

title: Fix helm list of ports not rendering correctly
body:
There was a problem that caused helm install to not reflect the proper list of ignored inbound and outbound ports. Namely if you supply just one port, that would not get reflected.

To reproduce do a: 

```
 helm install \
       --name=linkerd2 \
       --set-file global.identityTrustAnchorsPEM=ca.crt \
       --set-file identity.issuer.tls.crtPEM=issuer.crt \
       --set-file identity.issuer.tls.keyPEM=issuer.key \
       --set identity.issuer.crtExpiry=2021-01-14T14:21:43Z \
       --set-string global.proxyInit.ignoreInboundPorts="6666" \
       linkerd-edge/linkerd2
```


Check your config: 

```bash
 $ kubectl get configmap -n linkerd -oyaml | grep ignoreInboundPort
 "ignoreInboundPorts":[],
```
Signed-off-by: Zahari Dichev <zaharidichev@gmail.com>
author: zaharidichev

comments.author: ihcsim
zaharidichev
comments.body: @ihcsim So I attempted that initially and the result produced for the `ignoreInboundPorts` and `ignoreOutboundPorts` when both of these are empty is `ignoreInboundPorts : [""]` and `ignoreOutboundPorts: [""]` respectively. Apart from tests failing because of that, I think that an empty string array should be different than an array of one empty string? Am I missing something?

comments.author: ihcsim
comments.body:
@zaharidichev Ah.. you are right. Out of curiosity, do you know why we converted the slices into string in [`install.go`](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/60ac0d552728e9e780102b692cd22c8b9c3741f6/cli/cmd/install.go#L704-L705), instead of just passing the slice as-is? Then the Helm workflow would just be `helm install --set ignoreInboundPorts={"port1", "port2"}`.

Thanks for looking into this.

comments.author: zaharidichev
comments.body: @ihcsim I think `IgnoreInboundPorts` and `IgnoreOutboundPorts` have been strings for a long time. It was just a matter of how we are constructing them. Before it was from a slice of uints (passed via the cli) I believe, but it was changed to be a slice of string to support port ranges.

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body:
What are the different cases that we are expecting and how do they arise?  Are these inputs valid?

* $ports is length 0
* $ports is length 1 and contains just an empty string
* $ports is length 2 and the second element is an empty string

review_threads.author: zaharidichev
review_threads.body:
So if by inputs you mean what is passed to `global.proxyInit.ignoreInboundPorts`, then: 

- if its empty, its an empty string, so after split $ports will be a list of one empty string, which we filter
- if its just "", then its the same case as above
- if the length is two, then we do not do any validation to guard against an empty string not being a port.

Essentially what is happenign here is the following: 
- We fix the problem where specifying just one port will result in it not getting written to the config map
- We make sure that we have an empty `global.proxyInit.ignoreInboundPorts` we do not end up with an array that looks like `[""]` in the config map. 

I think any further validation on input is pushing the helm functionality a bit too far. WDYT? 
As you suggested in https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/pull/3953#discussion_r369298051, I am fine with factoring all that out into a function of its own so we can reuse it.

review_threads.author: ihcsim
zaharidichev
review_threads.body: Alright, so I rebased against #3953 (so this needs to go in first) and used your suggested approach for both fixes. Now these splitting functions are refactored in _helpers.tpl. Does that look better?

title: Show traffic split metrics from sources in all namespaces
body:
Fixes #3562 

When a pod in one namespace sends traffic to a service which is the apex of a traffic split in another namespace, that traffic is not displayed in the `linkerd stat trafficsplit` output.  This is because when we do a Prometheus query for traffic to the traffic split, we supply a Prometheus label selector to only select traffic sources in the namespace of the traffic split.

Since any pod in any namespace can send traffic to the apex service of a traffic split, we must look at all possible sources of traffic, not just the ones in the same namespace.

Before:

```
$ bin/linkerd stat ts
NAME           APEX     LEAF       WEIGHT   SUCCESS   RPS   LATENCY_P50   LATENCY_P95   LATENCY_P99
webapp-split   webapp   webapp       900m         -     -             -             -             -
webapp-split   webapp   webapp-2     100m         -     -             -             -             -
```

After:

```
$ bin/linkerd stat ts
NAME           APEX     LEAF       WEIGHT   SUCCESS      RPS   LATENCY_P50   LATENCY_P95   LATENCY_P99
webapp-split   webapp   webapp       900m    80.00%   1.4rps          31ms          99ms        2530ms
webapp-split   webapp   webapp-2     100m    60.00%   0.2rps          35ms          93ms          99ms
```

Signed-off-by: Alex Leong <alex@buoyant.io>
author: adleong

title: Trim space when comparing roots between the issuer secret and the config
body:
This fix ensures that we ignore whitespace and newlines when checking that roots match between the Linkerd config map and the issuer secret (in the case of using external issue + Helm). 

Fixes: #3907
Signed-off-by: Zahari Dichev <zaharidichev@gmail.com>
author: zaharidichev

comments.author: zaharidichev
comments.body:
@adleong @alpeb  I did the following to test all this: 

First install cert manager: https://cert-manager.io/docs/installation/kubernetes/

1. Generate root cert and create anchors secret: 

```
step certificate create identity.linkerd.cluster.local ca.crt ca.key \
  --profile root-ca --no-password --insecure &&
  kubectl create secret tls \
   linkerd-trust-anchor \
   --cert=ca.crt \
   --key=ca.key \
   --namespace=linkerd
```

2.  Create an issuer
```
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1alpha2
kind: Issuer
metadata:
  name: linkerd-trust-anchor
  namespace: linkerd
spec:
  ca:
    secretName: linkerd-trust-anchor
EOF
```

3. Create a certificate resource: 

```
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1alpha2
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: linkerd-identity-issuer
  namespace: linkerd
spec:
  secretName: linkerd-identity-issuer
  duration: 24h
  renewBefore: 1h
  issuerRef:
    name: linkerd-trust-anchor
    kind: Issuer
  commonName: identity.linkerd.cluster.local
  isCA: true
  keyAlgorithm: ecdsa
  usages:
  - cert sign
  - crl sign
  - server auth
  - client auth
EOF
```

4. Install with helm
```
 helm install \
  --name=linkerd2 \
  --set-file global.identityTrustAnchorsPEM=ca.crt \
  --set identity.issuer.scheme=kubernetes.io/tls \
  --set installNamespace=false \
  charts/linkerd2
```

5. Run `linkerd check` and you will see: 

```
linkerd-identity
----------------
× certificate config is valid
    IdentityContext.TrustAnchorsPem does not match ca.crt in linkerd-identity-issuer
    see https://linkerd.io/checks/#l5d-identity-cert-config-valid for hints
```

If you use this branch instead, you will not encounter the problem. You can also change the number of newlines in the ca.crt file in order to test what happens when there are more than one line breaks. One particular thing to notice is that one might expect that the problem is introduced by our `trim` function in the helm chart. If that was indeed the case, simply supplying a ca.crt file that has no line breaks would fix the problem. However if you try doing that and going through this procedure, you will convince yourself that this is not the case as cert-manager adds one \n at the end of the ca.crt in the `linkerd-identity-issuer` secret. In fact it is also interesting to observe that in this scenario the values of `tls.crt` in `linkerd-trust-anchors` and `ca.crt` in the `linkerd-identity-issuer` secrets differ in the number of their trailing \n chars. 

Hope this is all useful

title: Remove dependency on httpbin in egress integration test
body:
The egress integration test works by running a set of `bb` pods in `egress` mode which each are configured to send requests to a different combination of method and url in the `httpbin.org` domain.  We then verify certain properties of the response.

This is problematic because our integration tests rely on the availability and specific behavior of a service outside of our control.  Furthermore, using `bb` as part of this test can be problematic because `bb` sends a body with each request (including GETs) which is not handled well by all webservers.

We simplify this test by running a single `linkerd-debug` pod instead of a set of `bb` pods.  Our test can then run `curl` commands from inside this container using `kubectl exec`.  We use `linkerd.io` instead of `httpbin.org` as our egress target and we relax the check to simply verify that a non-error response is received.

Fixes https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/issues/2316

title: Allow CI to run concurrent builds in master
body:
Fixes #3911

Refactors the `cloud_integration` test to run in separate GKE clusters
that are created and torn down on the fly.
It leverages a new "gcloud" github action that is also used to set up
gcloud in other build steps (`docker_deploy` and `chart_deploy`).

The action also generates unique names for those clusters, based on the
git commit SHA and `run_id`, a recently introduced variable that is
unique per CI run and available to all the jobs.
This fixes part of #3635 in that CI runs on the same SHA don't interfere
with one another (in the `cloud_integration` test; still to do for
`kind_integration`).

The "gcloud" GH action is supported by `.github/actions/gcloud/index.js`
that has a couple of dependencies. To avoid having to commit
`node_modules`, after every change to that file one must run
```bash
# only needed the first time
npm i -g @zeit/ncc

cd .github/actions/gcloud
ncc build index.js
```
which generates the self-contained file
`.github/actions/gcloud/dist/index.js`.
(This last part might get easier in the future after other refactorings
outside this PR).

title: Run integration tests for forked repos
body:
## Motivation

Pull Requests from forked repositories do not automatically run integration
tests. This is because integration tests are run on KinD clusters that are
created on a docker host that requires an SSH setup.

Upon each Pull Request from a Linkerd organization member, every GH Action job
sets up SSH access (if the job requires it) and sets that machine as it's
docker host. Each job uses the same host to create a test cluster, run
integration tests, and cleanup for future use.

This workflow is limited by the fact that secrets are needed for most steps,
and secrets are not available to forked repositories. Therefore, when a Pull
Request from an external user is merged, integration tests have not been run
already (if not done manually) and we find out in the *master* branch push if
everything works properly.

## Solution

This change introduces an alternate path in the workflow that does not require
secrets since every job runs its tests within its own VM. This path is
available to all Pull Requests who's repository is a fork.

### Unit tests

Unit tests continue to run for every Pull Request and Push. These tests have
never required more than a VM through GH Actions to run and that remains
unchanged.

### Docker Pull

This job is only run on Pushes and non-forked Pull Requests. It requires
registry access which requires secrets. This saves some time in the `Docker
Build` step.

### Docker Build

The new path in this job for forked repositories uses the GH Action
[upload-artifact](https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact).

First it builds the docker images (no cache is used right now) and copies the
CLI binary into an `archives` directory.

Next it saves the previously built docker images (controller, grafana, proxy,
and web) as tarballs and `docker save`s those into the `archives` directory.

The `archives` directory is then uploaded as an artifact and can be used by the
integration test jobs running in parallel.


### KinD Setup

This job is only required for the host builds. Since the host builds all run on
the same *host*, the KinD cluster names must not clash. This is not a concern
for the GH Action builds because each KinD cluster runs on its own VM.

### KinD Integration Host

This job is similar to the the `Kind Integration GH` except that it is limited
to a `strategy.max-parallel: 3`. As mentioned above, all the KinD clusters run
on the same host and five parallel jobs can overrun the host.

### KinD Integration GH

Each of these jobs runs in parallel and uses the [download-artifact](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact) action to
download the previously uploaded artifacts.

Next it sets up the KinD clusters and `kind load`s the image archives into the
cluster.

Similar to the host integration test, it then runs each integration test in
parallel.

### Remaining jobs

These jobs all remain the same as they are specific to master branch pushes.

## Further pipeline improvements

Instead of using the `upload-artifact` and `download-artifact` actions, it may
be helpful to use the `cache` action more. This change introduces Go module
caching, but there is still no docker layer caching.

1. Each `Docker Build` for forked repositories is a fresh build for each image
   when it could possible uses layers from the cached images. This change would
   properly change how we use the `bin/docker-build` script so it can be a
   follow-up.

2. If `1.` works out well, moving completely to GH Actions may be something
   worth exploring. That way we do not have a dependency on the docker host, do
   not need to limit `max-parallel` jobs, and do not need to worry about the VM
   running out of space :P

Signed-off-by: Kevin Leimkuhler <kevin@kleimkuhler.com>

I'd recommend not setting `LINKERD_LOCAL_BUILD_CLI` here. That flag is intended for fast building during development. For CI, we'd want to test exactly the CLI we would ship with, built in Docker.

Taking this a step further, this means `Build docker images (host)` and `Build docker images (GitHub)` become identical, except for `DOCKER_HOST` being set. You should be able to use the `set-env` command to dynamically configure `DOCKER_HOST` when appropriate.

```yaml
  docker_build:
    name: Docker build
    runs-on: ubuntu-18.04
    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v2
    - name: Docker SSH setup
      if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || !github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork
      run: |
        mkdir -p ~/.ssh/
        touch ~/.ssh/id && chmod 600 ~/.ssh/id
        echo "${{ secrets.DOCKER_SSH_CONFIG }}"  > ~/.ssh/config
        echo "${{ secrets.DOCKER_PRIVATE_KEY }}" > ~/.ssh/id
        echo "${{ secrets.DOCKER_KNOWN_HOSTS }}" > ~/.ssh/known_hosts
        ssh linkerd-docker docker version
        echo "::set-env name=DOCKER_HOST::ssh://linkerd-docker"
    - name: Build docker images
      run: DOCKER_TRACE=1 bin/docker-build
    - name: Cache docker images
      if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork
      env:
        IMAGE_ARCHIVES_DIR: $HOME/archives
      run: |
        mkdir -p $IMAGE_ARCHIVES_DIR
        TAG="$(bin/root-tag)"
        for img in cli-bin controller grafana proxy web ; do
          docker save "gcr.io/linkerd-io/$img:$TAG" > $IMAGE_ARCHIVES_DIR/$img.tar
        done
        mv $IMAGE_ARCHIVES_DIR .
    - name: Upload image archives
      if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v1
      with:
        name: image-archives
        path: archives
```

comments.author: adleong
comments.body:
I'm trying to understand the failure case here.  Is the issue that if `pf.run()` returns an err, we still execute the next switch statement and call `pf.Stop()` which calls close on a channel that hasn't been created?

Could we simply return from the goroutine immediately after writing the err to the failure channel?  That way we will never call `pf.Stop()` at all and don't have to try to recover the panic.

comments.author: mayankshah1607
comments.body:
@adleong @ihcsim seems like that was causing the error. Could you take a look now?
Also, is it a good idea to let `recoverStop()` function be there?

comments.author: adleong
comments.body:
Ok I looked into this in more depth.  I suggest reading the comments on https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/pull/2976 since there's some good discussion there about the semantics of these methods.

My takeaway is that we need to be more consistent about who's responsibility it is to close the stop channel in case of an error.  `Init()` will call `Stop()` if there is an error running the port-forward but the `getMetrics` function also calls `Stop()` (via `defer`) if there is an error.  At other invocations such as in dashboard.go and controller/api/public/client.go we don't bother closing the channel at all in case of errors.

I think the most consistent thing would be to make it clear (in the godoc) that it is the callers responsibility to call `Stop()`, even in the case of errors.  This means that we would remove the call to `Stop()` from inside of `Init()` and potentially add a call to `Stop` in the error handling of dashboard.go and controller/api/public/client.go; although properly closing the channel in these cases probably isn't super important because the process will simply exit.  See https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/pull/2976/files#r297399887 for a description of why this can leak goroutines, but probably doesn't matter.

comments.author: ihcsim
comments.body: In general, channels are closed by the sender of the data, in this case, the callers of `Init()`. I recommend removing the `recoverStop()` function, to avoid hiding unexpected panics, and if necessary, create a separate issue to revisit the channel logic in the `Init()` constructor. Otherwise, making sure we `return` in the `if err != nil` conditionals LGTM.

comments.author: mayankshah1607
mayankshah1607
comments.body: @adleong @alpeb done! but looks like the integration tests are failing

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body: I think we should remove this entire select block.  Regardless of how `pf.run()` returned, we want to do nothing since it is always the caller's responsibility to call `pf.Stop()`.  And then, since we're removing the select block, we can remove the early return too.

review_threads.author: alpeb
review_threads.body: :point_up: that makes a lot of sense to me! It is critical indeed to clarify the responsibility here.

title: proxy: v2.85.0
body:
This release fixes a bug in the proxy's logging subsystem that could
cause the proxy to consume memory until the process is OOMKilled,
especially when the proxy was configured to log diagnostic information.

The proxy also now properly emits `grpc-status` headers when signaling
proxy errors to gRPC clients.

This release upgrades the proxy's Rust version, the `http` crate
dependency to address RUSTSEC-2019-0033 and RUSTSEC-2019-0034, and the
`prost` crate dependency has been patched to address RUSTSEC-2020-02.

---

* internal: Introduce a locking middleware (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#408)
* Update to Rust 1.40 with new Cargo.lock format (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#410)
* Update http to v0.1.21 (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#412)
* internal: Split retry, http-classify, and http-metrics (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#409)

title: Address external_issuer_test.go flakiness
body:
From time to time we get this CI error when testing the external issuer
mechanism:
```
Test script: [external_issuer_test.go] Params:
[--linkerd-namespace=l5d-integration-external-issuer
--external-issuer=true]
--- FAIL: TestExternalIssuer (33.61s)
    external_issuer_test.go:89: Received error while ensuring test app
    works (before cert rotation): Error stripping header and trailing
    newline; full output:
    FAIL
```
https://github.com/alpeb/linkerd2/runs/428273855?check_suite_focus=true#step:6:526

This is caused by the "backend" pod not receiving traffic from
"slow-cooker" in a timely manner.
After those pods are deployed we're only checking that "backend" is
ready, but not "slow-cooker", so this change adds that check.

I'm also removing the `TestHelper.CheckDeployment` call because it's
redundant, since the preceeding `TestHelper.CheckPods` is already checking
that the deployment has all the specified replicas ready.

title: stable-2.7.0
body:
## stable-2.7.0

This release adds support for integrating Linkerd's PKI with an external
certificate issuer such as [`cert-manager`] as well as streamlining the
certificate rotation process in general. For more details about cert-manager
and certificate rotation, see the
[docs](https://linkerd.io/2/tasks/use_external_certs/). This release also
includes performance improvements to the dashboard, reduced memory usage of the
proxy, various improvements to the Helm chart, and much much more.

To install this release, run: `curl https://run.linkerd.io/install | sh`

**Upgrade notes**: This release includes breaking changes to our Helm charts.
Please see the [upgrade instructions](https://linkerd.io/2/tasks/upgrade/#upgrade-notice-stable-270).

**Special thanks to**: @alenkacz, @bmcstdio, @daxmc99, @droidnoob, @ereslibre,
@javaducky, @joakimr-axis, @JohannesEH, @KIVagant, @mayankshah1607,
@Pothulapati, and @StupidScience!

**Full release notes**:

* CLI
  * Updated the mTLS trust anchor checks to eliminate false positives caused by
    extra trailing spaces
  * Reduced the severity level of the Linkerd version checks, so that they
    don't fail when the external version endpoint is unreachable
    (thanks @mayankshah1607!)
  * Added a new `tap` APIService check to aid with uncovering Kubernetes API
    aggregatation layer issues (thanks @droidnoob!)
  * Introduced CNI checks to confirm the CNI plugin is installed and ready;
    this is done through `linkerd check --pre --linkerd-cni-enabled` before
    installation and `linkerd check` after installation if the CNI plugin is
    present
  * Added support for the `--as-group` flag so that users can impersonate
    groups for Kubernetes operations (thanks @mayankshah1607!)
  * Added HA specific checks to `linkerd check` to ensure that the `kube-system`
    namespace has the `config.linkerd.io/admission-webhooks:disabled`
    label set
  * Fixed a problem causing the presence of unnecessary empty fields in
    generated resource definitions (thanks @mayankshah1607)
  * Added the ability to pass both port numbers and port ranges to
    `--skip-inbound-ports` and `--skip-outbound-ports` (thanks to @javaducky!)
  * Increased the comprehensiveness of `linkerd check --pre`
  * Added TLS certificate validation to `check` and `upgrade` commands
  * Added support for injecting CronJobs and ReplicaSets, as well as the ability
    to use them as targets in the CLI subcommands
  * Introduced the new flags `--identity-issuer-certificate-file`,
    `--identity-issuer-key-file` and `identity-trust-anchors-file` to `linkerd
    upgrade` to support trust anchor and issuer certificate rotation
  * Added a check that ensures using `--namespace` and `--all-namespaces`
    results in an error as they are mutually exclusive
  * Added a `Dashboard.Replicas` parameter to the Linkerd Helm chart to allow
    configuring the number of dashboard replicas (thanks @KIVagant!)
  * Removed redundant service profile check (thanks @alenkacz!)
  * Updated `uninject` command to work with namespace resources
    (thanks @mayankshah1607!)
  * Added a new `--identity-external-issuer` flag to `linkerd install` that
    configures Linkerd to use certificates issued by an external certificate
    issuer (such as `cert-manager`)
  * Added support for injecting a namespace to `linkerd inject` (thanks
    @mayankshah1607!)
  * Added checks to `linkerd check --preinstall` ensuring Kubernetes Secrets
    can be created and accessed
  * Fixed `linkerd tap` sometimes displaying incorrect pod names for unmeshed
    IPs that match multiple running pods
  * Made `linkerd install --ignore-cluster` and `--skip-checks` faster
  * Fixed a bug causing `linkerd upgrade` to fail when used with
  `--from-manifest`
  * Made `--cluster-domain` an install-only flag (thanks @bmcstdio!)
  * Updated `check` to ensure that proxy trust anchors match configuration
       (thanks @ereslibre!)
  * Added condition to the `linkerd stat` command that requires a window size
    of at least 15 seconds to work properly with Prometheus
* Controller
  * Fixed an issue where an override of the Docker registry was not being
    applied to debug containers (thanks @javaducky!)
  * Added check for the Subject Alternate Name attributes to the API server
    when access restrictions have been enabled (thanks @javaducky!)
  * Added support for arbitrary pod labels so that users can leverage the
    Linkerd provided Prometheus instance to scrape for their own labels
    (thanks @daxmc99!)
  * Fixed an issue with CNI config parsing
  * Fixed a race condition in the `linkerd-web` service
  * Updated Prometheus to 2.15.2 (thanks @Pothulapati)
  * Increased minimum kubernetes version to 1.13.0
  * Added support for pod ip and service cluster ip lookups in the destination 
    service
  * Added recommended kubernetes labels to control-plane
  * Added the `--wait-before-exit-seconds` flag to linkerd inject for the proxy 
    sidecar to delay the start of its shutdown process (a huge commit from 
    @KIVagant, thanks!)
  * Added a pre-sign check to the identity service 
  * Fixed inject failures for pods with security context capabilities
  * Added `conntrack` to the `debug` container to help with connection tracking
    debugging
  * Fixed a bug in `tap` where mismatch cluster domain and trust domain caused
    `tap` to hang
  * Fixed an issue in the `identity` RBAC resource which caused start up errors
    in k8s 1.6 (thanks @Pothulapati!)
  * Added support for using trust anchors from an external certificate issuer
    (such as `cert-mananger`) to the `linkerd-identity` service
  * Added support for headless services (thanks @JohannesEH!)
* Helm
  * **Breaking change**: Renamed `noInitContainer` parameter to `cniEnabled`
  * **Breaking Change** Updated Helm charts to follow best practices (thanks
    @Pothulapati and @javaducky!)
  * Fixed an issue with `helm install` where the lists of ignored inbound and
    outbound ports would not be reflected
  * Fixed the `linkerd-cni` Helm chart not setting proper namespace annotations
    and labels
  * Fixed certificate issuance lifetime not being set when installing through
    Helm
  * Updated the helm build to retain previous releases
  * Moved CNI template into its own Helm chart
* Proxy
  * Fixed an issue that could cause the OpenCensus exporter to stall
  * Improved error classification and error responses for gRPC services
  * Fixed a bug where the proxy could stop receiving service discovery updates,
    resulting in 503 errors
  * Improved debug/error logging to include detailed contextual information
  * Fixed a bug in the proxy's logging subsystem that could cause the proxy to
    consume memory until the process is OOM killed, especially when the proxy was
    configured to log diagnostic information
  * Updated proxy dependencies to address RUSTSEC-2019-0033, RUSTSEC-2019-0034,
    and RUSTSEC-2020-02
* Web UI
  * Fixed an error when refreshing an already open dashboard when the Linkerd
    version has changed
  * Increased the speed of the dashboard by pausing network activity when the 
    dashboard is not visible to the user
  * Added support for CronJobs and ReplicaSets, including new Grafana dashboards

  * Added `linkerd check` to the dashboard in the `/controlplane` view
  * Added request and response headers to the `tap` expanded view in the

  * Added filter to namespace select button
  * Improved how empty tables are displayed
  * Added `Host:` header validation to the `linkerd-web` service, to protect
    against DNS rebinding attacks
  * Made the dashboard sidebar component responsive
  * Changed the navigation bar color to the one used on the [Linkerd](https://linkerd.io/) website
* Internal
  * Added validation to incoming sidecar injection requests that ensures
    the value of `linkerd.io/inject` is either `enabled` or `disabled`
    (thanks @mayankshah1607)
  * Upgraded the Prometheus Go client library to v1.2.1 (thanks @daxmc99!)
  * Fixed an issue causing `tap`, `injector` and `sp-validator` to use 
    old certificates after `helm upgrade` due to not being restarted
  * Fixed incomplete Swagger definition of the tap api, causing benign
    error logging in the kube-apiserver
  * Removed the destination container from the linkerd-controller deployment as
    it now runs in the linkerd-destination deployment
  * Allowed the control plane to be injected with the `debug` container
  * Updated proxy image build script to support HTTP proxy options

  * Updated the CLI `doc` command to auto-generate documentation for the proxy

  * Added new `--trace-collector` and `--trace-collector-svc-account` flags to

  * Added a new `--control-plane-tracing` flag to `linkerd install` that enables

title: Integration test flakiness: endpoint version mismatch warning
body:
Updated regex for ignoring version mismatch warning events. It was only
applied for '-*upgrade' namespaces.

It is safe to ignore such warnings because the endpoint controller
retries when that happens, and if after many retries it still can't then
a different warning is thrown which is _not_ whitelisted and will make
the build fail.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.16.6/pkg/controller/endpoint/endpoints_controller.go#L334-L348

This PR also removes logging matches on expected warnings, to avoid
cluttering the CI log.

title: Service Mirroring Component
body:
This PR introduces a service mirroring component that is responsible for watching remote clusters and mirroring their services locally. Reviews on the general approach are more than welcome. 

Instructions regarding testing will come soon but for the time being any feedback regarding the overall sanity of the solution is greatly appreciated :) 

**Some implementation details** 
There two main components. The first one is responsible for watching config secrets. These secrets are created on the local cluster and contain all the needed information to construct k8s api client and initiate connection to the remote cluster. Once the creatio of such a secret is detected the a cluster watcher is created. The cluster watcher itself maintains a SharedInformer that listens for CREATE, DELETE and UPDATE events. These events are then translated into more domain specific events that are put into a queue. A main processing loop dequeues them and handles them accordingly. Special care is taken to handle some edge cases. For example if the controller crashes and an update to the remote service that is already mirrored is performed meanwhile, we recieve that as an ADD event once the watcher is started again. Instead of ignoring it because we already have a mirrored service in place we compare the resource versions of what has been mirrored with what is received as an ADD an update things accordingly. There are plenty of comments explaining these things in the code.

**Testing**
There are no unit tests at the moment as I intend to add them later but I envision that producing that will be quite easy because of the events based nature of the cluster watcher. So far I have been testing this with a cluster on GCP that I have a (very primitive) gateway nginx installed on. I will think about a better way to test all of that

**Headscratchers**
Currntly a mirrored service is a service tha has the same ports defined as the remote service. It also is associated with endpoints tha have the same ports as the service but their IPs are the ones of the external gateway (there might be more than one IP on the gateway). All of these ports forward to one specific port on the gateway. Currently I am picking the first defined port that is present on the remote gateway service. It is not quite clear to me though how we can support multiple ports on the gateway. Can that actually work? 

**TODOs**
- Handle gateway updates - currently we handle the cases when a service's gateway is changed. What is not handled however is when the resolved gateway is modified in some way (a new ip is assigned).
- Handle gateway deletion - we need to figure out what we do for all mirrored services once their gateway is deleted on the remote cluster. Do we delete the mirrors as well? 
- Improve logging
- Minor refactors here and there

Also please note that the following file is collapsed. Do not miss it: https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/pull/4028/files#diff-d826c2a036f7464e72c567626b5adce9
   
Some resources on informers: 
[Staying Informed](https://www.firehydrant.io/blog/stay-informed-with-kubernetes-informers/)
[Deep Dive into K8s Informers](https://engineering.bitnami.com/articles/a-deep-dive-into-kubernetes-controllers.html)
[Discussion on Missing events and Relists/Resyncs](https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/kubernetes-sig-api-machinery/PbSCXdLDno0)

comments.author: adleong
comments.body:
One important difference between the destination watcher code and this is that the relationship between mirrored service and gateway services makes this more stateful, and therefore more complex and fragile.  This is because changes in the mirrored services can change which services are considered gateway services and thus change which services we should be paying attention to for changes.  Furthermore, this can get us stuck out-of-sync if we miss an event and have the wrong idea about which services are gateways.

That's all to say: I think it is simpler and more reliable to do full reconciliation rather than trying to do targeted updates.  I think we can still satisfy the real-time requirements by watching for service events and then just performing full reconciliation at that time, in addition to doing it on a timer.

comments.author: zaharidichev
comments.body:
@adleong These are very good questions. I did some testing today and here are some of my thoughts on the matter.

> However, it is hard for me to be confident that there isn't some edge case of event ordering (or mis-ordering) that causes us to get into an incorrect state.

It is very likely that there is a bug somewhere in my code that will either skip events or misinterpret them and that will put us in an inconsistent state. I do not think though that if we change the approach we can guarantee that the likelihood of such (or another similar) bug creeping in will be greatly decreased. 

> I still don't understand the benefit of the event queue as opposed to just simple synchronous calls. 

For starters this is using watches, over k8s objects and as far as I take it this has quite a lot of benefits compared to hitting the API synchronously (that have been largely discussed online). What I also find quite neat is that it provides us with a stream of events that are  removing us from thinking about questions such as "How often should we poll that?" 

> I think replacing the enqueues with direct calls would leave the structure of the code pretty much the same, but it would eliminate the queue and make the order and timing of events easier to reason about.

I do not quite understand why "the queue" is bringing in so much controversy. We get events one by one, we process them as they appear, there is not much timing to think about. Nothing is happening concurrently. I guess there are a couple of distinct things that can go wrong: 

- somehow events appear out of order getting us into inconsistent state - we set our resync period to 1 minute and then we receive `UPDATE` events every single minute even for things that have not been changed, which allows us alleviate any occasional ordering glitch that is caused by client-go for example. I tested that.. it works

- we have a bug in our code that causes us to miss an event or rather not consider it - that is the most likely thing that could happen and I am not sure whether changing that to a synchronous _poll-every-x-seconds_ approach will decrease the likelihood of that happening greatly

- there is a problem and a watch is dropped and we start missing event like crazy - yes that could happen but then the shared informer will go into a mode of using get/list to resolve this problem until a watch connection can be established. So in theory everything will continue to work as expected. I tested that by breaking the credentials on the remote cluster and disallowing `watch` (removed the verb). The watcher dropped and the shared informer started repeatedly doing `GETs` to keep the state synced, effectively delivering events as I would expect. Everything continued to work as expected. The moment I repaired the credentials, things went back to normal.

- there is a bug in the cache package in go-client and things are completely broken - you got me there... if that is the case things will certainly not work. The silver lining though is that k8s as whole will most likely not work (as its one big fat shared informer under the hood) so most likely nobody will care (or notice) that our controller is broken.

>The biggest difference, I think, would be that we would no longer do delayed retries in the form of requeues. But it's not even clear to me what the benefit of requeues are

The requeues are not such a flagship feature of this whole approach, they are simply the by-product of it. (at least for me)

>If requeues are necessary, then don't we get into an irrecoverable state after exhausting the requeue limit?

We can get into a bad state because of two things. One is receving incorrect or incorrectly ordered events because of client-go, which is out of our control. If that happens as I said earlier we can rely on the fact that every X minutes a resync will happen which will rehydrate our shared informer and will give us UPDATE events that we can use to bring ourselves into consistent state. If we get into a bad state because my code is wrong, then requeues are not here to save us.

>If requeues are not necessary, then what benefit do they provide?

I think the correct way to put it is that they provide guards against failures that are _intermittent_ in nature. For example, an `UPDATE` event comes in and we try to update our service with a new gateway  but our `UPDATE` call to the k8s api fails with `metav1.StatusReasonServerTimeout` or 	`http.StatusTooManyRequests`, we can requeue immediately and try again up to x amounts of times. Now.. if requeues were not here, we are still fine because after some time (currently configured to be 10 minz) a resync will happen and we will get this `UPDATE` event once again and if the stars align we are going to be able to perform the operation successfully this time around. So the purpose of requeues are to provide faster turnaround for this whole process (in m mind).

> how does one decide what to set the requeue limit to? Under what situations would one change the default value?

I think this could be further documented but I imagine that whoever is running that can in fact make a call on what this values should be based on the error rate that is being observed. Wouldn't that make sense? A bit like setting a timeout...

The last thing I am at the moment is unreceptive to feedback and I hope this is not the way its taken. This is not what this is. I simply cannot convince myself that switching to another approach will make things easier and less dangerous. I might be quite wrong here and three months down the line we start running into massive issues with that. That would be pretty horrible and embarrassing for me , but I do not think that if we switch to a loop based approach I will sleep much better (or that you should have a reason to do so ;) ). 

As a side note there is pretty great description of this whole cache package that is [here]((https://lairdnelson.wordpress.com/2018/01/07/understanding-kubernetes-tools-cache-package-part-0/).

). Its worth taking a look.

The logic, when resolving a request seems to be:

title: Run all PRs on GH Actions VMs
body:
## Motivation

Currently all pushes to master branch, tags, and Linkerd org member PRs run
the `kind_integration_host` job on the same Packet host.

The means that parallel jobs spin up KinD clusters with a unique name and
sandbox the tests so that they do not clash.

This is problematic for a few reasons:
* There is a limit on the number of jobs we can run in parallel due to
  resource constraints.
* Workflow cancellation and re-runs conflict when the cancelled run deletes
  it's namespaces and the running one expects them to be present.
* There has been an observed flakiness with running multiple KinD clusters
  resulting in inconsistent timeouts and docker errors.

## Solution

This change moves all KinD integration testing to GH Actions VMs. This is
currently what forked repository workflows do.

There is no longer a `docker_pull` job as it's responsibilities has been moved
into one of the `kind_integration_tests` steps.

The renamed `kind_integration_tests` job is responsible for **all** PR
workflows and has steps specific to forked and non-forked repositories.

### Non-forked repository PRs

The Packet host is still used for building docker images as leveraging docker
layer caching is still valuable--a build can be as fast as 30 seconds compared
to ~12 minutes.

Loading the docker images into the KinD cluster on the GH Action VM is done by
saving the Packet host docker images as image archives, and loading those
directly into the local KinD cluster.

### Forked repository PRs

`docker_build` has been sped up slightly by sending `docker save` processes to
the background.

Docker layer caching cannot be leveraged since there are no SSH secrets
available, so the `artifact-upload`/`artifact-download` actions introduced in
#TODO are still used.

### Cleanup

This PR also includes some general cleanup such as:
* Some job names have been renamed to better reflect their purpose or match
  the current naming pattern.
* Environment variables are set earlier in jobs as a separate step if it is
  currently exported multiple times.
* Indentation was really bothering me because it switches back and forth
  throughout the workflow file, so lists are now indented.

Signed-off-by: Kevin Leimkuhler <kevin@kleimkuhler.com>
author: kleimkuhler

I think you can just do one single `wait` with no args and it'll wait for all the children jobs to finish. This also avoids having to track their pids.
BUT, we avoid the option to track individual failures for each job. If we hadn't spawned background jobs, the script would fail at the first failure (since this runs using `bash -e` according to the docs). Spawning background jobs disables that fail-fast behavior (according to my tests), so we'd have to track the exit status for each job and fail whenever one of them is > 0.
We could do that by iterating through the `jobs -f` output and inside the loop do `wait -$pid || exit 1` or something like that.

review_threads.author: kleimkuhler
review_threads.body:
I think something like this will work:

```
for image in proxy controller web cni-plugin debug cli-bin grafana; do
  docker save "$DOCKER_REGISTRY/$image:$TAG" > $ARCHIVES/$image.tar || tee save_fail &
done

# Wait for `docker save` background processes to complete.
wait < <(jobs -p)
test -f save_fail && exit 1
```

1. Each background job will create a `save_fail` file if the `docker save ..` command fails.
2. All the background jobs are waited for
3. Test for the presence of `save_fail` fail and exit if it is found.

I can test this a little more, but good find here!

title: Ensure we get the correct type out of Informer Deletion events
body:
It turns out that when we define our `DeleteFunc` handler it is possible in certain unfortunate situations to get a type different than what we were expecting (we want a *Service, we get `DeletedFinalStateUnknown`). If that happens we will probably fail with some cast exception. This Pr here ensures we consider these cases and cast/extract types in safer manner. 

 Wrt to the `DeletedFinalStateUnknown`, it  is placed into a DeltaFIFO in the case where an object was deleted but the watch deletion event was missed. In this case we don't know the final "resting" state of the object, so there's a chance the included `Obj` is stale. 

Signed-off-by: Zahari Dichev <zaharidichev@gmail.com>
author: zaharidichev

comments.author: zaharidichev

That allows me to ensure that if tomorrow someone on the k8s team decides to introduce yet another wrapper to express some state that I never though of, our code would not panic with an unsafe cast but would simply skip casting and log an error. Does that make sense or am I missing something?

review_threads.body:
It seems to be a very common pattern in the K8s code to validate the type of `object.Obj` too. I'd recommend doing the same thing. In that case, it might be easier to just not use a helper function. See

* Replicaset : https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0b2636a7e705bdf7c911e12d2e8846b9e6f88704/pkg/controller/replicaset/replica_set.go#L330-L342
* Endpoint: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0b2636a7e705bdf7c911e12d2e8846b9e6f88704/pkg/controller/util/endpoint/controller_utils.go#L219-L235
* Deployment: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0b2636a7e705bdf7c911e12d2e8846b9e6f88704/pkg/controller/deployment/deployment_controller.go#L339-L356
 * Statefulset: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0b2636a7e705bdf7c911e12d2e8846b9e6f88704/pkg/controller/statefulset/stateful_set.go#L243-L259

WDYT?

review_threads.body: Good point. Should have check how they do it. I am not a programming language expert but am I the only one finding that doing so much type checking in a typed programming language is a shame :(

review_threads.body:
I see that you're trying to factor the common code for handling the final state unknown into a common function.  Unfortunately, this introduces unnecessary use of "reflect" because Go doesn't support generics.  I'd recommend following the pattern of the k8s libraries (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0b2636a7e705bdf7c911e12d2e8846b9e6f88704/pkg/controller/replicaset/replica_set.go#L330-L342) and check the type against the final state unknown tombstone in each delete handler.

review_threads.body:
I try to avoid reflection whenever reasonable.  According to the [Go proverbs](https://go-proverbs.github.io/):

>Clear is better than clever.

title: Separate single Actions workflow into multiple workflows
body:
Depends on #4033

## Motivation

If any job fails in the current GH Actions workflow, a re-run on the same
commit SHA requires re-running *all* jobs--regardless if the job already
passed in the previous run.

This can be problematic when dealing with flakiness in the integration tests.

If a test fails due to flakiness in `cloud_integration_tests`, all the unit
tests, static checks, and `kind_integration_tests` are re-run which leads to
lots of waiting and dealing with the possibility of flakiness in earlier jobs.

With this change, individual workflows can now be re-run without triggering
all other jobs to complete again first.

## Solution

`workflow.yml` is now split into:
- `static_checks.yml`
- `unit_tests.yml`
- `kind_integration.yml`
- `cloud_integration.yml`

### Workflows

`statc_checks.yml` performs checks related to dependencies, linting, and
formatting.

`unit_tests.yml` performs the Go and JS unit tests.

`kind_integration.yml` builds the images (on Packet or the GH Action VM) and
runs the integration tests on a KinD cluster. This workflow continues to run
for **all** PRs and pushes to `master` and tags.

`cloud_integration.yml` builds the images only on Packet. This is because
forked repositories do not need to trigger this workflow. It then creates a
unique GKE cluster and runs the integration tests on the cluster.

### The actual flow of work..

A forked repository or non-forked repository opening a PR triggers:
- `static_checks`
- `unit_tests`
- `kind_integration_tests`

These workflows all run in parallel and are invidivually re-runnable.

A push to `master` or tags triggers:
- `static_checks`
- `unit_tests`
- `kind_integration_tests`
- `cloud_integration_tests`

These workflows also all run in parallel, including the `docker_build` step of
both integration test workflows. This has not conflicted in testing as it
takes place on the same Packet host and just utilizes docker layer caching
well.

Signed-off-by: Kevin Leimkuhler <kevin@kleimkuhler.com>
author: kleimkuhler

Thinking about the upcoming automated release work, what do you think about moving `chart_deploy` into a separate workflow that would be triggered by tags with the shape `(edge-.*|stable-*)`? We'd remove the `tags: *` trigger from all the other workflows, and so when we tag the release (after master would have gone green in the other workflows) only this new workflow would get triggered, unlike the current situation where we have to wait for everything to run again.
This new workflow would also contain the upcoming automated release jobs.

... to be more precise about the current situation, after the changelog changes have merged, we have to  manually cancel the build, and then tag, and it's upon this last event that the final tests are run and the release (currently just the Helm artifact) is pushed. If that last run fails, that might require pushing a fix, and some of us are familiar with the untagging/tagging business that requires :unamused: 
What I'm thinking is that we leave that first merge CI run to continue, and if it's green, tag the release to trigger the release steps.
I'm getting a little ahead into the release automation work here, but I think laying out the workflows like I described could be a good starting point.

However, as you also mention the the first merge would just continue, and once it's green we *know* that tagging that commit as a release is okay.

I would be okay with that change and think it makes sense! A push to master in order to release an edge or stable shouldn't require cancelling one CI run in order to let the other (tagged) workflow run. The possibility of tags being pushed and integration later failing should be addressed however as part of the future release automation work.

As @alpeb mentioned in this [comment](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/pull/4039#issuecomment-584791082), `chart_deploy` and other "release only" jobs should be moved to a release workflow that is responsible for pushing tagged images, deploying helm charts, etc.

review_threads.body:

It's why this change cannot just separate `chart_deploy` into its own workflow, that workflow would run at the same time as all the others and it may not be okay to deploy.

title: cli: Add label selector flag for `stat`
body:
First take on https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/issues/2734

#### Add `kubectl` like label selector for `linkerd stat`
As opposed to earlier, `linkerd stat` command now accepts a label selector via the `--selector` (or `-l` shorthand):
```bash
$ linkerd -n emojivoto stat deploy -l test.linkerd/test
```
The above command will return stats for all deployments with the label `test.linkerd/test` in the `emojivoto` namespace.

---
Follow up PRs shall be made for the following features (as a part of https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/issues/2734):
- Update `tap`, `top`, `routes` commands to accept resource lists much like `stat`
- Update `tap`, `top`, `routes` to accept label selectors

From what has been implemented currently, it looks like `buildStatsSummaryRequests()` method returns a slice of `StatSummaryRequest` where each request has `Selector.LabelSelector` being read in correctly from the `-l` or `--selector` flag.
For eg:
```bash
$ linkerd stat deploy -n emojivoto -l test-label/test
```
returns a request object where `label_selector` correctly holds the value `test-label/test`.
However, the label is being ignored while fetching the stats from API - all deployments in the namespace `emojivoto` are returned, and not just the ones with the specified label. Hmmm, I don't think the `linkerd-controller` api server is actually using the label selectors.

If we look at the `StatSummary` method in the `linkerd-controller` api server, which calls `k8sResourceQuery` to imply a request for kubernetes resources query. This method at https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/9b29a915d31f33914cdb94d71489d98f7e31c9a1/controller/api/public/stat_summary.go#L162 is called to retrieve the k8s resources, but I don't see the `selectors` being used anywhere in this path.

I also see that we are using the `labelSelectors` in the `ListPods` path at https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/9b29a915d31f33914cdb94d71489d98f7e31c9a1/controller/api/public/grpc_server.go#L104, Thus making `ListPods` tests with `LabelSelectors` pass at  https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/9b29a915d31f33914cdb94d71489d98f7e31c9a1/controller/api/public/grpc_server_test.go#L338

comments.author: christyjacob4

comments.author: cpretzer
comments.body:
@christyjacob4 

@Pothulapati provides a good snippet of code about how to handle this case and it is congruent with the comments from the [issue](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/issues/3204):

> https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/issues/3204#issuecomment-583892305

> https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/issues/3204#issuecomment-585043355

1. We shouldn't assume a registry other than the default registry
2. If the user specifies an image using this flag, then it should contain the registry and image name

Think about it this way: let's say BigBank has an airgapped environment and they use their own docker registry. They will source the prometheus image from some location and add it to their internal registry, so the repository could be something like: `docker.bigbank.internal`

They could even rename the image if they wanted to like: `bb-prom` and include their own tag `2.15.1_rc`

In that case, their install command might be like:
`linkerd install --prometheus-image docker.bigbank.internal/bb-prom:2.15.1_rc`

For this scenario, the snippet that @Pothulapati wrote would work. Additionally, for other users like `scrappystartup.com` who don't use a custom registry, they can omit the `--prometheus-image` flag and get the official image from docker hub.

I don't see added value to having constituent parts for the `repository`, `image`, and `tag` in an airgapped environment.

Hope that helps!

Instead of having grafana query prometheus for every namespace/deployment literally, we can use a globing operator to shorten the request length so results can be returned in clusters where there are large numbers of deployments and namespaces.

This is how you can reproduce the original bug:

1. Install Linkerd into the default `linkerd` namespace
1. Update the `charts/linkerd2/templates/namespace.yaml` with a new random label like `foo: bar`
1. Run `bin/go-run cli upgrade | less`. Notice that the namespace YAML has the new label
1. Run `bin/go-run cli upgrade | kubectl apply --prune -l linkerd.io/control-plane-ns=linkerd --dry-run -oyaml -f - | less`. Notice that the namespace YAML is missing, because `--prune` drops it
1. Run `bin/go-run cli upgrade | kubectl apply --prune -l linkerd.io/control-plane-ns=linkerd`. Notice that your new label is **not** added to the `linkerd` namespace

Now apply your changes:

1. Run `bin/go-run cli upgrade | less`. Notice that your `foo: bar` label still shows up
1. Run `bin/go-run cli upgrade | kubectl apply --prune -l linkerd.io/control-plane-ns=linkerd`. If the changes fixed the issue, then your new label should be added to the `linkerd` namespace

## Motivation

A release workflow will be the only triggered workflow on `push.tags` events.

As a first step in automating the release process, it should assert that
integration tests pass once the docker images have been tagged.

Both KinD and cloud integration tests should run since they have different
sets of integration tests that they are responsible for running.

It then needs to run the `chart_deploy` job.

This has been fully tested with a release tag push on my fork. The run can be

helm chart.

This workflow will:

- Build the docker images on the Packet Host
- Tag the docker images with the release tag
- Run KinD integration tests
- Run cloud integration tests
- Run `chart_deploy`

## Motivation

Creating a release tag is a manual process that is prone to error by the
release responsible member.

title: Remove envoy, contour restrictions
body:
Fixes https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/issues/3910

Currently linkerd rejects injecting proxies into envoy/contour.

The reasons were probably historical since contour didn't support header manipulation.

With https://github.com/projectcontour/contour/releases/tag/v1.1.0 you can explicitly add headers to your routes making it possible to set the required `l5d-dst-override` header for linkerd.

---

Unfortunately contour doesn't support variables when setting headers, other than those provided by [envoy's custom headers](https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/configuration/http/http_conn_man/headers#custom-request-response-headers). To make linkerd work with contour+envoy you need to explicitly set the upstream cluster (read k8s service address) for every route:
```yaml
apiVersion: projectcontour.io/v1
kind: HTTPProxy
metadata:
  name: test-httpproxy
  namespace: default
spec:
  routes:
  - conditions:
    - prefix: /testroute
    requestHeadersPolicy:
      set:
      - name: l5d-dst-override
        value: test-service.default.svc:8443
    services:
    - name: test-service
      port: 8443
      namespace: default
```

Making this easier to configure is a problem for contour though.

---

This PR removes the restriction of linkerd not injecting sidecar proxies when using contour and envoy.

title: Generate correct path regex for proto files without package name
body:
**Problem**

When generating linkerd service profile based on proto files, default path regex looks like this:

`/Package\.Service/Method`

When proto file is missing package name it looks like this:

`/\.Service/Method`

What it should look like:

`/Service/Method`

**Solution**

Check package name, change path regex accordingly

**Validation**

Generate service profiles based on proto files without package name.

title: Create linkerd/website dispatch event on release
body:
## Motivation

A goal of the release automation project is to automate the website publish
that publishes a new install script that uses the new release version.

linkerd/website#668 removed the hard coded versions from the repo and moved
the version update into the `make publish` command.

That workflow now needs to be triggered by a release in `linkerd2`.

## Solution

Once `kind_integration_tests` and `cloud_integration_test` pass, a job runs
using the [repository-dispatch](https://github.com/marketplace/actions/repository-dispatch) action to create a repository dispatch event in
`linkerd/website`.

This dispatch event will (current PR: linkerd/website#670) trigger the
publish workflow.

## Testing

Tested in my fork [here](https://github.com/kleimkuhler/linkerd2/actions/runs/45165789)

## Additional steps needed

A new `RELEASE_TOKEN` secret needs to be added to this repo. It should be the
personal access token of [l5d-bot](https://github.com/l5d-bot) with `repo` access.

title: proxy: v2.87.0
body:
This release comprises many internal changes that are not expected to
have any user-facing impact.

There is one user-facing change: the inbound router's default capacity
has been increased from 100 to 10K to accomodate environments that have
a high cardinality of virtual hosts served by a single pod.

---

* fallback: Operate on Services instead of Layers (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#432)
* internal: Extract a service-profile crate (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#433)
* Increase inbound router capacity default to 10000 (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#434)
* Upgrade to Rust 1.41 (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#437)
* cleanup: Remove various cruft (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#438)
* Generalize router::Make as stack::NewService (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#435)
* integration: Make the test controller more realistic (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#436)
* trace-context: Remove unnecessary MakeService (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#439)
* Split the `stack-tracing` crate from `app-core` (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#440)
* stack: Introduce the Proxy trait (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#441)
* timeout: Do not synthesize HTTP response (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#442)
* addr: Avoid trailing dots in authorities (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#446)
* outbound: Relax type constraints in require_identity_on_endpoint (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#447)
* Cleanup transport::Connect & http::Client types (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#443)
* app: Use locks with controller clients (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#448)

title: Fix `bin/fetch-proxy` on Linux
body:
`bin/fetch-proxy` was failing on Linux:

```bash
$ bin/fetch-proxy
linkerd2-proxy-v2.87.0/
linkerd2-proxy-v2.87.0/LICENSE
linkerd2-proxy-v2.87.0/bin/
linkerd2-proxy-v2.87.0/bin/linkerd2-proxy
bin/fetch-proxy: 31: [: Linux: unexpected operator
/home/siggy/code/linkerd2/target/proxy/linkerd2-proxy-v2.87.0
```

Also in CI:
https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/runs/473746447?check_suite_focus=true#step:5:32

Unfortunately `bin/fetch-proxy` still returned a zero exit status, because
`set -e` does not apply to commands that are part of `if` statements.
From https://ss64.com/bash/set.html:
```
-e  Exit immediately if a simple command exits with a non-zero status, unless
    the command that fails is part of an until or  while loop, part of an
    if statement, part of a && or || list, or if the command's return status
    is being inverted using !.  -o errexit
```
Fortunately when the `if` command failed, it fell through to the `else` clause
for Linux, and copied `linkerd-proxy` successfully.

Root cause was a `==` instead of `=`. `shellcheck` confirms, and also
recommends quoting:

```bash
$ shellcheck bin/fetch-proxy

In bin/fetch-proxy line 31:
if [ $(uname) == "Darwin" ]; then
     ^-- SC2046: Quote this to prevent word splitting.
              ^-- SC2039: In POSIX sh, == in place of = is undefined.
```

Apply `shellcheck` recommendations.

Signed-off-by: Andrew Seigner <siggy@buoyant.io>

title: Add kubectl-style label selectors
body:
Second take on https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/issues/2734
Also, somewhat related to https://github.com/linkerd/gsoc/pull/2 , https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/issues/3871
This PR adds support for kubectl-style label selectors for the following cmds:
- tap
- top
- routes

Example:
```bash
# tap deployments with label sample.label=test
$ linkerd -n myns tap deploy -l sample.label=test

# display live traffic from all deployments with label sample.label=test
$ linkerd -n myns top deploy --selector sample.label=test

# display route stat from all deployments with label sample.label=test
$ linkerd -n myns routes deploy -l sample.label=test
```
> Note : Label selector for stat has been addressed in https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/pull/4040

### Unresolved Questions

- Do we need to add similar support for `metrics` cmd? It looks like the same can be achieved from : 
```bash
linkerd metrics -n linkerd $(
    kubectl --namespace linkerd get pod \
      --selector linkerd.io/control-plane-component=controller \
      --output name
  )
```

### TODO
A follow up PR shall be made for :
- Add support for `tap`,`top`,`routes`,`stat` to accept list of resources. Eg:
```bash
$ linkerd -n linkerd tap deploy linkerd-controller linkerd-identity
```

cc: @ihcsim

title: Enable dst service to work with remote gateway endpoints
body:
The purpose of this change is to enable the destinations service to recognize remote gateway endpoints and be able to set the corresponding labels, identitiy and the rest of the data that will be needed for the proxy to handle the traffic properly. 

@adleong since you mostly wrote that code, it would be good to get your opinion on the direction of these changes. Effectivelly I want to express the idea that endpoints and hende `WeightedAddress` instaces can be the product of things different than pods. Still have to add more docs and write some more tests for this.

Description: 

The most prominant change here is that we break up the concrete `Address` type into three types: 

- `PodAddress` -  is an address/port combo that comes from Endpoints that have been created because of pods
- `HeadlessServiceAddress` - what it sounds like. These have been created because of a service with an associated Endpoints object that does not have ties to a Pod
- `RemoteGatewayAddress` - this is a subcase of `HeadlessServiceAddress`  but contains additional infromation for remote gateway identitiy and service fq name. 

Note that this PR is the first part of this change.  We still need to set these annotations when we create endpoitns in the mirroring controller. We also need to add metrics labels, etc and we need to eventually change the API to allow for carying data about the remote gateway (such as fully qualified name of the service we are targeting on the other end). These will come as a seprate smaller PRs. 


Signed-off-by: Zahari Dichev <zaharidichev@gmail.com>
author: zaharidichev

comments.author: olix0r
comments.body: @zaharidichev I don't want to create extra work, but would it be possible to get a "clean" change to the existing endpoints code without introducing the new features, and then following on with a PR that adds remote gateway support?

comments.author: olix0r
comments.body:
> would it be possible to get a "clean" change

Actually, on second look, the actual surface area of this change is smaller than it first appeared (thanks gofmt). If I understand correctly, this is basically introduce a polymorpish address type instead of the single concrete `Address` type? If so, i don't know a separate PR is worth it.

comments.author: zaharidichev
comments.body:
> If I understand correctly, this is basically introduce a polymorpish address type instead of the single concrete Address type?


@olix0r that is the just of it (for some definition of polymorpish that Go adopts .... )

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body:
There's nothing I love more than some good old fashioned polymorphism.  However, I'm not sure it's a good fit here.  This interface gives a false sense of encapsulation: we can use this interface in some places, but in others we have to reach inside and switch on the concrete type.

It may be simpler to deal with this as a single struct.  The `Pod`, `OwnerName`, and `OwnerKind` fields can simply be empty when they don't apply (i.e. when the address does not correspond to a pod) just like today.  And we can add an `Identity` field which can provide the identity name when the pod is not present.  I would perhaps call `FullyQualifiedRemoteName` something more aligned with how its effect such as `AuthorityOverride` or something like that.  Alternatively, we can omit this field for now since it's unused and a better name might be more obvious once we have the destination API change solidified.  The `Namespace` and `LocalServiceName` fields appear to be completely unused.  If the goal is to use them to propagate metric labels, we may want to simply have a labels map on the Address struct that we can set directly.

review_threads.author: zaharidichev
review_threads.body:
> This interface gives a false sense of encapsulation: we can use this interface in some places, but in others we have to reach inside and switch on the concrete type.

Maybe its me but I do not see this as such a problem. Seems in line with trying to express the kind of addresses as a collection of ADTs. 

> t may be simpler to deal with this as a single struct. The Pod, OwnerName, and OwnerKind fields can simply be empty when they don't apply (i.e. when the address does not correspond to a pod) just like today. 

The thing I did not like about this approach (as this is how it was before) is that we are using the presence or abence of values to determine what _type_ of thing we are lookin at. Is this a headless service or a pod address, or whatever else.. 

That all being said, lets try and see how it looks without the different types.

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body: This gets a bit philosophical, but I don't think the presence or absence of the pod field fundamentally changes the type of the address.  The way I think of it is this: if the Address has a pod, we'll use that to populate certain metadata; if it doesn't we won't.

review_threads.author: zaharidichev
review_threads.body: putting it that way, it makes sense.

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body:
There are some existing references to "Headless" services in various comments.  These are incorrect.  What they refer to as "headless services" are actually services which have endpoints that do not correspond to pods.  We should remove these misleading comments and variable names.

A headless service is one without a clusterIP.  Linkerd does not interact with the clusterIP of a service and does not care if a service is headless or not.
