title: Add -A flag to alpha stat
body:
Add an `--all-namespaces` flag to `linkerd alpha stat`.  This flag ignore the value of the `--namespace` flag and looks up resources across all namespaces.

Some example usage:

```
> linkerd alpha stat po -A
NAMESPACE  NAME                                    SUCCESS        RPS  LATENCY_P50  LATENCY_P90  LATENCY_P99
default    curl                                    100.00%     0.6rps          1ms          1ms          1ms
emojivoto  emoji-ffd474b7b-nq8wc                   100.00%     2.0rps          1ms          1ms          1ms
emojivoto  vote-bot-74c4867dc6-d5j4d                90.00%     2.0rps          3ms          4ms          4ms
emojivoto  voting-6b69659f5b-6hpvx                  78.95%     0.9rps          1ms          1ms          1ms
emojivoto  web-6cfccddd6b-vrq2q                     92.86%     5.6rps          1ms          3ms          4ms
linkerd    linkerd-controller-54bbb5d485-4p9w2     100.00%     0.3rps          1ms          1ms          1ms
linkerd    linkerd-destination-69fb65c4fb-7mthj    100.00%     0.3rps          1ms          1ms          1ms
linkerd    linkerd-grafana-ffc4d969-gf5cz          100.00%     0.3rps          1ms          2ms          2ms
linkerd    linkerd-identity-6456988769-tbkx9       100.00%     0.3rps          1ms          1ms          1ms
linkerd    linkerd-prometheus-5469d5d8fd-kskc6     100.00%     2.5rps          1ms          2ms          3ms
linkerd    linkerd-proxy-injector-658f8c4cd-pfgbt  100.00%     0.3rps          1ms          1ms          1ms
linkerd    linkerd-smi-metrics-86567c5ff4-dh7rn          -     0.0rps          0ms          0ms          0ms
linkerd    linkerd-sp-validator-54c8d7dcf9-wq6jv   100.00%     0.3rps          1ms          2ms          2ms
linkerd    linkerd-tap-574b74c964-cwm6l            100.00%     0.3rps          1ms          1ms          1ms
linkerd    linkerd-web-577755788d-95slx            100.00%     0.3rps          1ms          1ms          1ms
```

```
> linkerd alpha stat po/curl --to po
FROM  TO                              SUCCESS        RPS  LATENCY_P50  LATENCY_P90  LATENCY_P99
curl  web-6cfccddd6b-vrq2q.emojivoto  100.00%     0.9rps          1ms          2ms          2ms
```

Signed-off-by: Alex Leong <alex@buoyant.io>
author: adleong

comments.author: adleong
comments.body:
I've done some more holistic thinking about how namespaces should work and I've made a few changes according to these principles:

* The `--to` resource will always look up across all namespaces.  There is no performance cost because `--to` is implemented with filtering.  This allows us to avoid adding a `--to-namespace` flag which gets confusing and unwieldy.  It also makes sense that when doing a `--to` query, we want to see all the outgoing connections from our resource, no matter what namespaces they are in.
* `-A` cannot be used with a named resource and now fails with an error message.  This is consistent with `kubectl get`.
* If the `-A` flag is used, then we add a "NAMESPACE" column.  This is consistent with `kubectl get -A`.
* Since the `--to` resource may be in any namespace, we include the namespace in its name.  e.g. "voting.emojivoto".  In my opinion this is less clunky than having a "TO-NAMESPACE" column.

comments.author: adleong
comments.body: @alpeb @zaharidichev Thanks for your reviews!  Since the latest round of changes are quite significant, I'd appreciate it if you could give this a quick re-review.  🥂

NAMESPA  NAME

```

title: Improve release tag script
body:
## Motivation

Closes #4140

Automatically create new edge release tag:
```
❯ bin/create-release-tag edge
edge-20.3.2 tag created and signed.

tag: edge-20.3.2

To push tag, run:
    git push origin edge-20.3.2
```

Validate new stable release tag:
```
❯ bin/create-release-tag stable 2.7.1
stable-2.7.1 tag created and signed.

tag: stable-2.7.1

To push tag, run:
    git push origin stable-2.7.1
```

## Solution

The release tag script now takes a release channel argument. If the release
channel argument is `stable`, a second argument is required for the version.

If the release channel is `edge`, the script gets the current edge version and
creates a new edge version with the current year: `YY`, month: `MM`, and
increments the current month minor if it is not a new month.

If the release channel is `stable`, the script will only validate the version.

Example error cases:

```
❯ bin/create-release-tag
Error: create-release-tag accepts 1 or 2 arguments
Usage:
    create-release-tag edge
    create-release-tag stable x.x.x
```

```
❯ bin/create-release-tag foo
Error: valid release channels: edge, stable
Usage:
    bin/create-release-tag edge
    bin/create-release-tag stable 2.4.8
```

```
❯ bin/create-release-tag edge 2.7.1
Error: accepts 1 argument
Usage:
    bin/create-release-tag edge
```

```
❯ bin/create-release-tag stable
Error: accepts 2 arguments
Usage:
    bin/create-release-tag stable 2.4.8
```

```
❯ bin/create-release-tag stable 2.7
Error: version reference incorrect
Usage:
    bin/create-release-tag stable 2.4.8
```

```
❯ bin/create-release-tag stable 2.7.1.1
Error: version reference incorrect
Usage:
    bin/create-release-tag stable 2.4.8
```

title: Upload artifacts for all PRs
body:
## Motivation

#4147 adds a script for setting up a local cluster that uses the images built
from the changes introduced in a forked PR. This would be useful for all PRs.

In order to install Linkerd from a PR into a local cluster, the images still
need to be built at some point. If you happen to have SSH config setup for our
Packet host, you can pull them from there. That is not very
accessible--requiring that someone adds you as a user--so we can take a
similar approach to forked PRs.

## Solution

All PRs now make an artifact directory that is uploaded as part of the KinD
integration tests. This way, the `install-pr` script can use those images no
matter if the PR is a fork or not.

title: proxy: v2.89.0
body:
This release builds on changes in the prior release to ensure that
balancers process updates eagerly.

Cache capacity limitations have been removed; and services now fail
eagerly, rather than making all requests wait for the timeout to expire.

Also, a bug was fixed in the way the `LINKERD2_PROXY_LOG` env variable
is parsed.

---

* Introduce a backpressure-propagating buffer (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#451)
* trace: update tracing-subscriber to 0.2.3 (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#455)
* timeout: Introduce FailFast, Idle, and Probe middlewares (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#452)
* cache: Let services self-evict (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#456)

  * Fixed a bug that could cause log levels to be processed incorrectly
  * Removed cache capacity limitations, allowing services to fail eagerly

title: Add KinD option to `install-pr` script
body:
## Motivation

After #4147 added the `install-pr` script, installing PRs into existing
clusters does not work if that cluster is a KinD cluster

Changing the script to be able to use KinD, and specifically automate `kind
load` would be helpful!

## Solution

The script can now be used in the following ways.

```
❯ bin/install-pr --help
Install Linkerd with the changes made in a GitHub Pull Request.

Usage:
    --context: The name of the kubeconfig context to use

    # Install Linkerd into the current cluster
    bin/install-pr 1234

    # Install Linkerd into the current KinD cluster
    bin/install-pr [-k|--kind] 1234

    # Install Linkerd into the 'kind-pr-1234' KinD cluster
    bin/install-pr [-k|--kind] --context kind-pr-1234 1234
```

The script assumes that the cluster (KinD or not) has already been created. If
the cluster is a KinD cluster, the `-k|--kind` flag should be passed.

If the `--context` flag is not passsed, the install defaults to the current
context (`kubectl config current-context`).

I also added a [`-h|--help]` option that describes how to use the script.

title: Add retries to certain `linkerd check` checks
body:
## Motivation

Testing #4167 has revealed some `linkerd check` failures that occur only
because the checks happen too quickly after cluster creation or install. If
retried, they pass on the second time.

Some checkers already handle this with the `retryDeadline` field. If a checker
does not set this field, there is no retry.

## Solution

Add retries to the `l5d-existence-replicasets`
`l5d-existence-unschedulable-pods` checks so that these checks do not fail
during a chained cluster creation > install > check process.

body:

In reality if target port is note defined when creating the service, k8s will set the port and the target port to the same value. Seems to me that checking for the targetPort to be different than 0, is a no-op.

title: Fix error when injecting Cronjobs that have no metadata
body:
When injecting a Cronjob with no
`spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.metadata` we were getting the following
error:

```
Error transforming resources: jsonpatch add operation does not apply:
doc is missing path:
"/spec/jobTemplate/spec/template/metadata/annotations"
```

This only happens to Cronjobs because other workloads force having at
least a label there that is used in `spec.selector` (at least as of v1
workloads).

With this fix, if no metadata is detected, then we add it in the json patch when
injecting, prior to adding the injection annotation.

I've added a couple of new unit tests, one that verifies that this
doesn't remove metadata contents in Cronjobs that do have that metadata,
and another one that tests injection in Cronjobs that don't have
metadata (which I verified it failed prior to this fix).

title: Fix script argument regex
body:
Currently the release tag regex matches against arguments that have `edge` or
`stable` as a substring.

It should only match against arguments that are either `edge` or `stable`.

For example, the graceful error handling is not triggered for the following:
```
❯ bin/create-release-tag edge-20.3.3

This PR fixes the regex so that the above results in graceful error handling.

```
❯ bin/create-release-tag edge-20.3.3
Error: valid release channels: edge, stable
Usage:
    bin/create-release-tag edge
    bin/create-release-tag stable 2.4.8

title: Relax clock skew check
body:
Fixes #3943

The Linkerd clock skew check requires that all nodes in the cluster have reported a heartbeat within (approximately) the last minute.  However, in Kubernetes 1.17, the default heartbeat interval is 5 minutes.  This means that the clock skew check will often fail in Kubernetes 1.17 clusters.

We relax the check to only require that heartbeats have been detected in the past 5 minutes, matching the default heartbeat interval in Kubernetes 1.17.  We also switch this check to be a warning so that clusters which are configured with longer heartbeat intervals don't see this as a fatal error.

Signed-off-by: Alex Leong <alex@buoyant.io>

title: Add uninstall cmd functionality to cli (#3622)
body:
### Fixes #3622 
### Edit 29th March: 
PR overhauled, updated body of this msg accordingly

Signed-off-by: Matei David <matei.david.35@gmail.com>

### What
---

* Introduce an `uninstall` command to the cli to generate resources necessary to purge/uninstall Linkerd from a Kubernetes cluster (uninstall was chosen over delete for the sake of brevity and conciseness in commands);

### How
---

* `uninstall` uses `client-go` to fetch all `cluster-wide resources` (RBAC, hooks, etc.) and the control-plane `namespace` and outputs them to stdout as yaml manifests (to be piped to `kubectl delete`
* clientset is used to grab all resources that have the `linkerd.io/control-plane-ns` label. For the `namespace` itself, the name is used instead of a label selector.
* Since `gvk` is stripped down when fetching a Kubernetes resource using `client-go` ([see here](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/issues/541#issuecomment-452312901)), the `marshal` function also infers the `GVK` from the object type in case it is missing.

### Test
* Test case is quite trivial, however, it ensures that empty files (as strings) are not generated, and it ensures the `apiVersion` and `kind` are correctly injected/present (without them, the pipe to `kubectl` will fail).

* I checked the results manually by following the steps below (see attached pictures):

1. Perform a fresh install through `linkerd install | kubectl apply -f -`
2. Run  `kubectl get APIService,ClusterRoleBinding,CustomResourceDefinition,MutatingWebhookConfiguration,ValidatingWebhookConfiguration,PodSecurityPolicy,Namespace  -l linkerd.io/control-plane-ns=linkerd -o yaml` -- this outputs all resources that should be deleted (except `RoleBIndings` in `kube-system` namespace which have been added as part of this PR)
3. Run `/bin/go-run cli uninstall | kubectl delete -f - `
4. Repeat step (2) -- output is now empty list

title: edge-20.3.4
body:
This release introduces several fixes and improvements to the CLI.

* CLI
  * Added support for kubectl-style label selectors in many CLI commands (thanks
    @mayankshah1607!)
  * Fixed the path regex in service profiles generated from proto files without
    a package name (thanks @amariampolskiy!)
  * Fixed an error when injecting Cronjobs that have no metadata
  * Relaxed the clock skew check to match the default node heartbeat interval
    on Kubernetes 1.17 and made this check a warning
  * Fixed a bug where the linkerd-smi-metrics pod could not be created on
    clusters with pod security policy enabled
* Internal

title: Linkerd CLI Chocolatey Package
body:
This PR partially fixes #3063 by building a chocolatey package for Linkerd2's Windows CLI
It adds the build scripts for the Linkerd chocolatey package and based on discussions in
https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/pull/3921

The package currently exists in the `bin/win` folder
The `.nuspec` script has been modified for easy integration with the workflow
done by @ihcsim here: https://github.com/ihcsim/linkerd-chocolatey

To build outside of workflow environment (on windows system):
   - Modify `linkerd.nuspec` version tag to an available stable version of Linkerd2's cli
     eg: 2.7.0 and file tag's `src` to `tools\**`
   - Install chocolatey
   - cd into `bin/win/`
   - Run `choco pack`
   - Run `choco install linkerd -s .`  (make sure cmd/ powershell is running as administrator)
   - Run refreshenv to add `linkerd.exe` path to system
   - To unistall run `choco uninstall linkerd`

Tackling requirements discussed in https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/pull/3921
(specifically: https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/pull/3921#issuecomment-599634476)

- Followed folder structure as described here: https://github.com/ihcsim/linkerd-chocolatey
- Modified package to accept version through the metadata available in `.nuspec` file
- Modified package to override install path with command line arg/ env variable
    To run with command line argument:
    - Run `choco install linkerd -s . --params="/path:<YOUR_PATH_HERE>"`
    To run with environment variable:
    - Run `$env:linkerdPath = "<YOUR_PATH_HERE>"` in powershell
    Uses default chocolatey install path if none of the above provided.
- Modified package to accept command line args/ env variable for checksum
    To run with command line argument:
    - Run `choco install linkerd -s . --params="/checksum:<VERSION_CHECKSUM>"`
    (Keep params space seperated when specifying multiple)
    To run with environment variable:
    - Run `$env:linkerdCheckSum = "<VERSION_CHECKSUM>"`
    If no checksum provided, default null value assigned and package ignores verification step
- This package is compatible in a non-administrative environment but one must install chocolatey
in a non-administrative path.
(Steps explained here: https://chocolatey.org/docs/installation#non-administrative-install)

Further plans:
This PR is part of a set of planned PRs based on the discussions in
https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/pull/3921
(specifically: https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/pull/3921#issuecomment-599099615)

Signed-off-by: Animesh Narayan Dangwal animesh.leo@gmail.com

title: Extract common logic in scripts and CI to load images into KinD
body:
Fixes #4206 Followup to #4167

Extract common logic to load images into KinD, from `bin/kind-load`, `bin/install-pr`, `.github/workflows/kind_integration.yml` and `.github/workflows/release.yml`.

Besides removing the duplication, `bin/kind-load` will benefit in performance by having each image be loaded in parallel.

```
$ bin/kind-load -h

Load into KinD the images for Linkerd's proxy, controller, web, grafana, debug and cni-plugin.

Usage:
    bin/kind-load [--images] [--images-host ssh://linkerd-docker]

Examples:

    # Load images from the local docker instance
    bin/kind-load

    # Load images from tar files located in the current directory
    bin/kind-load --images

    # Retrieve images from a remote docker instance and then load them into KinD
    bin/kind-load --images --images-host ssh://linkerd-docker

Available Commands:
    --images: use 'kind load image-archive' to load the images from local .tar files in the current directory.
    --images-host: the argument to this option is used as the remote docker instance from which images are first retrieved
                   (using 'docker save') to be then loaded into KinD. This command requires --images.
```

title: Prometheus Alertmanager + extra args + rules
body:
This PR allow users to use linkerd metrics directly from linkerd prometheus to setup alerts, furthermore it provides flexibility by means of extra cmd line arguments.

**Add prometheus rules configurable values.**

These are set as empty by default, but allow the user to configure recording and alerting rules on the linkerd prometheus.

**Add prometheusAlertmanagers value.**

This allows configuring a list of statically targetted alertmanager instances.

**Allow addition of extra arguements.**

This allows end user flexibility for options such as log format. Rather than bubbling up such possible config options into helm values, extra arguments provides more flexibility.

comments.author: alpeb
comments.body:
Thanks @naseemkullah !

Regarding the `alerting_rules.yaml` and `recording_rules.yaml` parts, have you considered loading them through separate ConfigMaps? Instead of loading them through the main `linkerd-prometheus-config` CM, we could allow users to define as many separate CMs as they want, and Linkerd would mount them under `/etc/prometheus` for Prometheus to load them. 
So instead of declaring in `values.yaml` the content of those extra configs, we would just declare the list of extra CMs to load, e.g. in a `prometheusExtraConfigs` array. And then we'd modify `prometheus.yaml` so that it mounts them all. That might imply mounting them in subpaths and modifying the `rule_files` directive so it crawls down those subpaths.

I think decoupling these configs from the main Linkerd `values.yaml` might be more flexible. LMKWYT.

mountPath: /etc/prometheus/{{ .subPath }}
subPath: {{ .subPath }}
```
I also think we can hard-code `readOnly: true`.

I believe this also requires changing the main config mountPath below to something like:
```yaml
- mountPath: /etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml
  subPath: prometheus.yml
  name: prometheus-config
  readOnly: true
```

Here we upgrade our dependencies on client-go to 0.17.4 and smi-sdk-go to 0.3.0.  Since smi-sdk-go uses client-go 0.17.4, these upgrades must be performed simultaneously.

title: Add support for Helm configuration of per-component proxy resources requests and limits
body:
Add support for Helm configuration of per-component proxy resources requests and limits.

Currently the resource requests and limits for resources assigned to the proxy are the same for all proxies in a cluster. This results in the largest value for all proxies having to be set. Optimal values
may vary by an order of magnitude between components (e.g. `linkerd-prometheus` and `linkerd-web`

Solution:
Allow the setting of `.Values.global.proxy.perComponentResources.<resource name>.resources` to override the resource settings in the Helm chart.

Validation

Fixes #4225

title: Add liveliness checks and metrics for multicluster gateway
body:
This PR adds liveliness checks for remote gateways. The way its is done is by maintaining probes for each gateway. The probes track whether the gateway is alive by issuing an HTTP request to an endpoint. Additionally the probes publish Prometheus metrics such as number of mirrored services per gateway and histogram latencies. 

Next steps (coming in different PRs): 

- Externalize the port, path and period through  the `get-credentials` command
- Add unit tests
- Enable Prometheus to scrape the `/metrics` endpoint
- Enable users to retreive the stats of the gateways via a CLI command (similar to `stat`)

Signed-off-by: Zahari Dichev <zaharidichev@gmail.com>

@adleong very good question! So yes, all the way back these events are triggered by the informer. And indeed you are right that we can get duplicates here. However, if you trace a bit forward these particular events are triggered by the cluster_watcher. The cluster watcher assumes that you might get duplicate events from the informers (i.e. if your watcher fails and you fall back to perioding listing). because of that it makes sure that we do not create or delete a service twice. So for example if you get a service created event for a service that you already have and that has not changed, it will not try to crete the service again and as a result it will not issue an event to the prober twice. Will look at it again, but as far as I remember, this is how it was designed. I will put a comment though. I think all this deserves a good dose of tests to verify that all these edge cases are handled correctly (which I will write in time). 

That being said, in my latest commit I transitioned to keeping a set of these services (well a map, as Go does not have sets...) to track the count. That alone should serve as a second gatekeeper against duplication. Does that sound correct ?

review_threads.body: Since we know the service name when it registers interest in the gateway, we could consider having a `service` label on this gauge.  This allows us to actually list all the services behind the gateway, instead of just knowing the number of services.

review_threads.author: zaharidichev
review_threads.body: Hm, fairly new to the whole Prometheus thing, but is it possible/practical to have multi value labels.  This metric is 1 per gateway, not per service. So how can we do what you are describing?

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body: I'm suggesting adding a label for service name. This would mean the gauge would only ever take values 1 (if the service with that name is served by that gateway) or 0 (if not).

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body: in addition to having a gauge for "alive", we could also have a counter for "probes" with a label to indicate if the probe succeeded or failed.

review_threads.author: zaharidichev
review_threads.body:
I think a counter only goes up, right? And the number of probes is sublject to going down as well. What is the advantage of having this counter in addition the gauge. Does it give us something more? If we grab the gauges, we ultimatelly get the number of probes along with the information of whether the gateway is alive or not. 

Or  are you trying to measure the total number of attemptes to reach a remote cluster and partition them by success outcome?

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body: Yeah, that's right.  A total number of attempts, rather than a gauge of in-flight attempts.  This allows us to see the rate of probes over time.  For example, if for some reason probes stop happening, the alive gauge would stay at `1` and we would not be able to see that probes had stopped.  A counter would let us see this.

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body: how easy is it to expose queue depth as a prometheus metric?  how can we tell if this queue is backing up?

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body:
a simple approach would be to expose the queue length `len(probeEvents)` as a gauge.

a more sophisticated approach would be to have counters of enqueues and dequeues.  The counter approach has the benefit that not only can we see queue depth by subtrating dequeues from enqueues, but we can also have a label for event type to see breakdowns by event type.

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body: do you think it would be more robust to do something like `pw.metrics.services.SetValue(len(pw.pairedServices))`?

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body: I like using `map[string]struct{}` for stuff like this.  The problem with storing a boolean value is that it's easy to make the mistake of setting the value to false when unpairing a service (rather than deleting the key) which would cause a bug.

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body:
Using time.Sleep and Ticker together is a bit confusing.  Also, this can sleep up to `probeTickerPeriod` making the time between probes potentially as long as 2*`probeTickerPeriod`.  

Consider instead a ticker with some random jitter like https://github.com/projectcalico/felix/blob/master/jitter/jittered_ticker.go

review_threads.author: zaharidichev
review_threads.body: Makes sense, however I think this only reflects the start point. The time between probes will be equal to `probeTickerPeriod`. It just that there is delay of when the probing starts.

review_threads.author: zaharidichev
review_threads.body: But fine, I will just grab this jittered ticker. Looks like a nice utility anyway.

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body: I don't know what we do or don't have to do legally, when copying Apache 2 code like this, but it's my instinct that we should at least give attribution by including a link to the code that this was copied from.

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body: I think these probe fields are unused and shouldn't be part of the RCSW.  I think we decided that the probe configuration should be loaded from the gateway annotations and stored on the gateway spec, instead of being per cluster.

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body: It might be more clear and concrete to hold a `*ProbeManager` instead of a totally generic `func(event interface{})`.  I don't think the generality really gets us anything useful since we only ever enqueue to a ProbeManager.

review_threads.author: zaharidichev
review_threads.body: I wanted to keep it like that for test purposes. Namely., i want to exercise a bunch of events coming from the informer and expect that a bunch of other events will be send to the ProbeManager. And in tests, I think it might be cleaner to just provide a function that buffers them rather than mocking the ProbeManager (for some definition of Mocking that Go adopts... )

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body: What do you think about creating a `ProbeEventSink` interface which defines just a `send` method?  This is basically exactly what you already have, but using an interface feels a bit more like idiomatic go than passing around an anonymous function.  TIOLI.

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body: should we log if any of these errs are not nil?  if we move all the parsing of the ProbeConfig into a separate method that returns `(*ProbeConfig, error)` we can be a bit more idiomatic about error handling and avoid nesting if statements so deeply.

title: Add `operationID` field to tap openapi response
body:
This fixes an issue users are experiencing when upgrading from from Linkerd
2.6 to 2.7 and use the [kubernetes-external-secrets]() project.

The change introduced by #3700 resulted in the tap service showing up in the
`/openapi/v2` API response. I confirmed this with a local build.

A dependency within the project expects the `operationID` field to be present
in the swagger definition. It is optional as stated in the
[spec](https://swagger.io/docs/specification/paths-and-operations/). It's
purpose is to identify an operation and should be unique.

This change adds that field to tap service swagger spec. While this can be
fixed in the KES dependency, it certainly does not hurt to add and other
libraries may similarly expect this field.

Signed-off-by: Kevin Leimkuhler <kevin@kleimkuhler.com>

title: Add `unmeshed` flag to stat command
body:
## Motivation

Introduces an `unmeshed` flag to the `stat` command so that users can opt-in
to viewing unmeshed resources in the `stat` output.

This changes the existing behavior of the `stat` command such that unmeshed
resources no longer render by default in the output.

Before:

```
❯ bin/linkerd stat -A deploy
NAMESPACE     NAME                     MESHED   SUCCESS      RPS   LATENCY_P50   LATENCY_P95   LATENCY_P99   TCP_CONN
kube-system   coredns                     0/1         -        -             -             -             -          -
kube-system   local-path-provisioner      0/1         -        -             -             -             -          -
kube-system   metrics-server              0/1         -        -             -             -             -          -
kube-system   traefik                     0/1         -        -             -             -             -          -
linkerd       linkerd-controller          1/1   100.00%   0.3rps           1ms           2ms           2ms          2
linkerd       linkerd-destination         1/1   100.00%   0.3rps           1ms           1ms           1ms         11
...
```

After:

```
❯ bin/linkerd stat -A deploy
NAMESPACE   NAME                     MESHED   SUCCESS      RPS   LATENCY_P50   LATENCY_P95   LATENCY_P99   TCP_CONN
linkerd     linkerd-controller          1/1   100.00%   0.3rps           1ms           1ms           1ms          2
linkerd     linkerd-destination         1/1   100.00%   0.3rps           1ms           2ms           2ms         13
...
```

Closes #3871

## Solution

Using the meshed pod count in the stat response, resources with a count of `0`
are not rendered in the table.

The `-l`/`--selector` flag do not work for all resource types, so applying a
default label does not solve this problem. While it works for pods, it does
not work for deployments as the `linkerd.io/inject` is an annotation that
cannot be selected on.

I did not think a shorthand flag was necessary for this. I do not think users
will commonly pass this flag to the `stat` command, and I didn't think adding
an additional short flag such as `u` was necessary.

title: Upgrade crashes proxy-init when skipping ports
body:
Fixes #4257

This was introduced in 2.7.0. When performing an upgrade on an
installation having used `--skip-outbound-ports` or

ConfigMap, parses them wrongly, and then when proxy-init picks them the
iptables commands fail.

I've also improved one of the upgrade unit tests to include these flags,
and confirmed it failed before this fix.

  * Fixed a bug that caused the proxy to crash after upgrade if
    `--skip-outbound-ports` or `--skip-inbound-ports` were used
  * Added `unmeshed` flag to the `stat` command, such that unmeshed resources
    are only displayed if the user opts-in
  * Added a `--smi-metrics` flag to `install`, to allow installation of the
    experimental `linkerd-smi-metrics` component
  * Fixed a bug in `linkerd stat`, causing incorrect output formatting when using
    the `wide` flag
  * Fixed a bug, causing `linkerd uninstall` to fail when attempting to delete
    PSPs
* Controller
  * Improved the anti-affinity of `linkerd-smi-metrics` deployment to avoid
    pod scheduling problems during `upgrade`
  * Improved endpoints change detection in the `destinations` service, enabling
    mirrored remote services to change cluster gateways     

Signed-off-by: Zahari Dichev <zaharidichev@gmail.com>

title: Add rolling update strategy to for HA deployments
body:
This introduces a rolling update strategy to Linkerd deployments that have
three replicas during HA deployments. This allows for at most one pod to begin
terminating before a new pod ready is ready.

This allows for upgrades to take place on three node clusters. As a pod begins
terminating, it opens up the node for the new pod to start initializing.

`.Values.enablePodAntiAffinity` was chosen as the conditional here because it
is set by the `values-ha.yaml` config on HA deployments

title: Support Multi-stage install with Add-On's
body:
This PR add's support for multi stage install with add-ons. When we did the initial add-on model, Multi-stage wasn't supported as we had only one add-on and it was optional. This meant that users couldn't use multi-stage with add-ons i.e the full add-on manifests would be part of the `ControlPlaneStage`. (no `ConfigStage` for addons)

But now that we are adding grafana and prometheus as add-on's, It's important that all the things that are part of the install path are supported in the add-on model. This PR does this by separating the add-on template files into `ConfigStageTemplates()` and `ControlPlaneStageTemplates` which will be called based on the stage.

Once this is merged, Users should be able to perform multi-stage normally along with `--addon-config` flag to pass add-on configuration.

Linkerd with Tracing add-on can be installed in multiple stages as follows:

Let `addons.yaml` be
```yaml
tracing:
  enabled: true
```

Config Stage:

```bash
linkerd install config --addon-config addons.yaml
```

Control-Plane Stage:
```bash
linkerd install control-plane --addon-config addons.yaml
```

This follows the usual requirement that, users must pass the same flags on both these stages.


**Changes include:**

- Replacing `Templates()` with `ConfigStageTemplates()`, `ControlPlaneStageTemplates()` func's in the `addOn` interface, to separate out add-on template files.
- Add Install and Upgrade Unit tests for Multi-stage with add-ons.


Signed-off-by: Tarun Pothulapati <tarunpothulapati@outlook.com>

title: Add MeshedPodCount field to TS resource rows
body:
The addition of the `--unmeshed` flag changed the rendering behavior of the
`stat` command so that resources with 0 meshed pods are not displayed by
default.

Rendering is based off the row's `MeshedPodCount` field which is currently not
set by `func trafficSplitResourceQuery`. This change sets that field now so
that in rendering, the trafficsplit resource is rendered in the output.

The reason for this not showing up in testing is addressed by #4272 where the
`stat` command behavior for no traffic is changed.

The following now works without `--unmeshed` flag being passed:

```
❯ bin/linkerd stat -A ts
NAMESPACE   NAME                    APEX          LEAF          WEIGHT   SUCCESS   RPS   LATENCY_P50   LATENCY_P95   LATENCY_P99
default     backend-traffic-split   backend-svc   backend-svc     500m         -     -             -             -             -
default     backend-traffic-split   backend-svc   failing-svc        0         -     -             -             -             -
```
author: kleimkuhler

comments.body:
The other solution for this is that `linkerd stat ts` command just turns on the unmeshed flag by default.

These resources are unmeshed, so it's another reasonable solution. I chose to do use `MeshedPodCount` though because once the unmeshed flag is turned on, it would be on for everything in the `linkerd stat` command

title: Extend Helm chart to allow disabling secret resources for self-signed certs.
body:
## Problem ##
The linkerd2 helm chart currently generates secrets for the certificates for the webhooks for the proxy-injector and service profile validator as well as the K8s API server extension smi-metrics and tap respectively.

## Solution ##
This change adds four configuration options (`*.externalSecret`) to the helm chart to allow disabling the creation of the following secrets:
* `linkerd-proxy-injector-tls`
* `linkerd-sp-validator-tls`
* `linkerd-smi-metrics-tls`
* `linkerd-tap-tls`

It also splits the explicit configuration between the certificate (`certPEM`) and the CA bundle (`caBundle`). For those users that currently explicitly set the certificate and private keys, **this is a breaking change**, as they now also have to configure the CA bundle.

For current users that do not configure this at all, nothing changes.

## Validation ##
The MR is currently lacking a proper test. I am working on that.

Fixes #4288

Signed-off-by: Lutz Behnke <lutz.behnke@finleap.com>

But during the roll-over we could not have recovered any failed linkerd side-cars. We have the production services in a HA setup, so even a failing side-car or application pod would not have taken our service down, but still.

title: Add Kubeconfig contex namespace to cli commands' options (#4197)
body:
### Issue: #4197 
---

### What

According to the original issue, when using a `cli` command that operates on namespaced resources, the `-n` flag has to be used even when the resources are in the __default namespace of the Kubeconfig context__.  For example, if the currently used context by the Kubeconfig has the default namespace as `emojivoto`, doing `kubectl get pods` should list everything under the `emojivoto namespace`. Issue #4197 requested similar behaviour out of the `cli` commands. 
 

### How

* The `cli` has a set of options for each command. In implementing this feature, my first step was to compile a list of commands that act on namespaced resources and accept an `-n` flag. The command names are listed below:
```
(linkerd)
1. metrics
2. edges
3. get
4. profile
5. routes
6. top
7. tap
```

* I added a new function in `cli/cmd/root.go` called `getDefaultNamespace()` that infers the default namespace based on the currently active context. To do, it makes use of loading rules and and a `DeferredLoadingClient`. Once the loader is initialised with the loading rules, we can get access to the client configuration (i.e kubeconfig) and find the namespace associated with the currently active context (through the `Namespace()` function).
* For each command previously listed, in the `options` structure, instead of hardcoding the default namespace as `default` or `""`, I initialise it using the `getDefaultNamespace()` function.

* I thought in this case unit tests are trivial, since it would only test if a string = another string, and mostly test the functionality of `client-go`. Instead, I wrote a new function in the integration test helper that allows changing the default namespace of the currently used context. 
* I thought a full integration test might not be the best use of space, so I have instead added two new cases to the integration tests of `linkerd get` and `linkerd tap` respectively. My rationale is that if it works for these two, it will work for the rest since it's the same principle. I chose `get` and `tap` because they included more than one case each and it made the most sense (from a design perspective).

Looking forward to some feedback :)

I thought initially this approach broke the unit tests but it doesn't. Let me know if that sounds better and I'll put it in.

review_threads.author: zaharidichev
review_threads.body: I start to wonder how severe this error actually is. Do we want to recover from it or we rather fail the whole command invocation right away? Is it safe to assume that if we error out here, we can simply return the "default" namespace ?

review_threads.author: mateiidavid
review_threads.body:
Hi @zaharidichev  I've looked at the `Namespace()` method implementation in the `DeferredLoadingClientConfig` type to determine what will explicitly happen if an error is encountered.  The function errors out if the client config cannot be created properly (in which case it returns an empty string), the client config is created based on the rules and rule loader that are created at the start of the `getDefaultNamespace()` function. The rest of the `Namespace()`method either returns the namespace defined in the context or if the namespace is `"default"` tries to work out whether it was an implicit or explicit choice.

> Is it safe to assume that if we error out here, we can simply return the "default" namespace

I assume so, yes. If the function fails, it means for whatever reason, the config was not properly initialised/created. The single point of error when creating the client config is when the rules are loaded in. A reason for failure, in this case, would be that the config cannot be parsed or loaded from a `kubeConfig` file.

To my understanding (and skill), this is what is happening under the hood when we are creating and loading those config "rules". Based on this, I think on error it is safe to just return the `"default"` namespace. In this context (no pun intended) it seems a default is more sensible since we might not know what the underlying issues with the `kubeConfig` are in the `cli` client environment.

Tl;dr To my understanding the point of error happens when either the config or the rules are not loaded in properly, in which case I think it is sensible to just return a default. If the problem persists (i.e context namespace simply won't be inferred), the namespace can just be overridden with the `-n` flag. If instead we just fail the command invocation outright, it might be that none of the commands will work, since all `cli` command options are making a call to `getDefaultNamespace()` so options will never be initialised if it all fails.

Of course, this is just my opinion, look forward to hearing what you think :)

review_threads.body: Yes, I see. That makes sense to me.

title: Go test failure message wrappers to create GH Annotations
body:
First part of #4176

## Problem

Failures in go tests need to be properly formatted as Github annotations
so that we can fetch them through Github's API for aggregation and
analysis.

## Solution

A wrapper for error messages has been created in `testutil/annotations.go`.
The idea is that instead of throwing test failures like this:

```go
t.Failf("error retrieving data;\nExpected: %#v\nActual: %#v", expected,
actual)
```

We'd throw them like this:
```go
testutil.AnnotationFatalf("error retrieving data", "error retrieving data;\nExpected: %#v\nActual: %#v", expected,
actual)
```

That will continue reporting the error as before (when using `go test`
or another test runner), but as a side-effect it will also send to
stdout something like:

```
::error file=pkg/inject_test.go,line=133::error retrieving data
```
Which becomes a GH annotation, visible in the CI run summary screen.

The fist string art is used to have the GH annotation be a generic error message
that can be aggregated and counted across multiple test runs. If `testutil.Fatalf(str, args...)`
is called instead, the original error message will be used.

Note that that the output will be produced only when the env var
`GH_ANNOTATION` is set (which will when tests are triggered from a
Github Actions workflow).

Besides `testutil/annotation.go` and its accompanying unit test file,
other changes were made in other tests as examples, the plan being that
in a further PR _all_ the tests will use these wrappers.

Edit: replaced ext_err approach with annotations.go

And indeed, the plan is to use `WithAnn` only in those places where the original error would be too specific (say containing details such as a pod name that is different on each run), the idea being to tell how many times that type of error appeared.

What do you think about having `Error`, `Errorf`, `Fatal`, and `Fatalf` methods in `testutil` that take `testing.T` as a parameter?  I think there are a few advantages to this:
* less verbose at the call site: `testutil.Fatalf(t, "Unexpected error: %s", err)`
* easier to audit for tests that don't use the wrapper: no test should call `t.Errorf` etc directly
* Possible to add `testutil.AnnotatedErrorf(t, "Unexpected error", "Unexpected error: %s", err)` style methods to avoid the `with` design pattern.

That being said, I share the feeling that all this is a bit hacky, but I can't figure an alternative way while conserving the default testing framework for go...

title: Inject LINKERD2_PROXY_DESTINATION_GET_NETWORKS proxy variable
body:
Fixes #3807

By setting the LINKERD2_PROXY_DESTINATION_GET_NETWORKS environment variable, we configure the Linkerd proxy to do destination lookups for authorities which are IP addresses in the private network range.  This allows us to get destination metadata including identity for HTTP requests which target an IP address in the cluster, Prometheus metrics scrape requests, for example.

This change allowed us to update the "direct edges" test which ensures that the edges command produces correct output for traffic which is addressed directly to a pod IP.

We also re-enabled the "linkerd stat" integration tests which had been disabled while the destination service did not yet support these types of IP queries.

title: Add check for validating that remote clusters share the same trust an…
body:
In order to enable TLS across cluster boundaries, we need to ensure that the issuer certs can all be verified with a common trust acnhors. In roder to ensure that all remote cluster that are monitored, share the same anchors, we add them as annotation to the remote cluster config secret. This allows us to easily compre the anchors of all currently watched clusters to the local ones. This PR makes this process part of the `check` command

Signed-off-by: Zahari Dichev <zaharidichev@gmail.com>
author: zaharidichev

comments.author: alpeb
comments.body: Thinking about edge cases, would cross-cluster communication work if they had different anchors that were themselves rooted on the same root cert? Or what if one if the clusters had an anchor with a bundle containing the other cluster's cert? If so, can this check be more generic to allow those situations?

comments.author: grampelberg
comments.body: I'm not sure I understand how this is working. Would you mind doing a step by step?

comments.author: zaharidichev
comments.body: @grampelberg Sure. So the secrets that contain the remote cluster api config that we generate with `get-credentials` are not modified to also contain the trust roots that are present in the linkerd config map. because these secrets end up on the local cluster, we can actually verify that all roots of remote clusters we are mirroring match with the roots of our local linkerd installation. @alpeb is right about these edge cases though.. Maybe this check is a bit too naive..

comments.author: grampelberg
comments.body: @zaharidichev I see, but that would be a point in time snapshot. If someone was to rotate the certificate on the other side, it'd stop working again, right? Would the liveness check test for this? If it did, we'd need a good error message for this specific use case as my suspicion is that it will be the biggest problem most folks run into.

comments.author: adleong
zaharidichev
grampelberg
comments.body: @zaharidichev The two trust roots can be different, yet still allow traffic (imagine a whole trust chain, or a bundle with swapped entries). My suggestion was to test an actual connection and examine the error that comes back (invalid certificate).

title: Probe manager events emission tests
body:
This PR provides a set of tests that verify the cluster watcher issues correct events to the probe manager when the state of the remote clusters is modified. This required a bit of reorg of the tests to make things slightly more reusable. Namely, we now have the concept of a test environment, that describes the state of the local and remote clusters and what events are enqueued. title: update changelog for edge-20.4.5
body:
This edge release includes several new CLI commands for use with
multi-cluster gateways, and adds liveness checks and metrics for
gateways. Additionally, it makes the proxy's gRPC error-handling
behavior more consistent with other implementations, and includes a fix
for a bug in the web UI.

* CLI
  * Added `linkerd cluster setup-remote` command for setting up a
    multi-cluster gateway
  * Added `linkerd cluster gateways` command to display stats for
    multi-cluster gateways
  * Changed `linkerd cluster export-service` to modify a provided YAML
    file and output it, rather than mutating the cluster
* Controller
  * Added liveness checks and Prometheus metrics for multi-cluster
    gateways
  * Changed the proxy injector to configure proxies to do destination
    lookups for IPs in the private IP range
* Web UI
  * Fixed errors when viewing resource detail pages
* Internal
  * Published a Chocolatey package for the Linkerd CLI
* Proxy
  * Changed the proxy to set a `grpc-status: UNAVAILABLE` trailer when a
    gRPC response stream is interrupted by a transport error

Signed-off-by: Eliza Weisman <eliza@buoyant.io>

comments.author: Pothulapati
comments.body:
This PR can be tested both using the CLI and Helm. 

**Testing through CLI:**

`--addon-config` flag is used to pass the configuration of add-ons. The same format and fields from `values.yaml` can be used/overwritten. Some examples of overwriting values can be found [here](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/88dafe6ad6141b19fa60c8d7ff35b5da0c930d0f/cli/cmd/upgrade_test.go#L1729)

*For upgrades:*

- First, the default values are read from `values.yaml`, which are overwritten by values from `linkerd-config-addons` (if present) and which can be further overwritten by `--addon-config` to add/remote/update config of add-ons during upgrades.
- One thing to note is that, when an enabled add-on is disabled during upgrade we don't delete the already created add-on resources but any configuration w.r.t add-on applied in the control-plane components will not be present. This can be solved by using `--purge` when applying.

**Testing through Helm:**

The good thing about Helm is that we don't have to manage anything regarding state of values, etc as Helm takes care of it. All the configuration including that of add-ons is stored and re-used during upgrades, where overwriting is also allowed. 

We still need the `linkerd-config-addons` cm even when the installation is done through Helm, is to have add-on specific health-checks as they need add-on configuration as shown [here](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/pull/4321/files#diff-4d95af557bb1b4c9b3c9a50e7f9dbb50R42). Also, it makes sense to have consistent configuration across installation ways.

title: Don't send NoEndpoints during pod updates for ip watches
body:
When the proxy has an IP watch on a pod and the destination controller gets a pod update event, the destination controller sends a NoEndpoints message to all listeners followed by an Add with the new pod state.  This can result in the proxy's load balancer being briefly empty and could result in failing requests in the period.  

Since consecutive Add events with the same address will override each other, we can simply send the Adds without needing to clear the previous state with a NoEndpoints message.

title: Make gateway require TLS for incoming requests
body:
This PR introduces a few changes with the aim of making the multicluster setup a bit more secure:

- The service mirror controller will now be injected
- The proxy on the gateway will require identity on the two ports that are exposed through the gateway (the incoming port and the probes port)
- The probe worker now uses the `l5d-require-id` when doing the HTTP get requests to the gateways to  inform the outbound proxy of the expected identity of the remote peer (the gateway)
- There are two sets of probes on two different ports. One is local and can work without identity (this is for Kubelet) and the other is remote and requires identity (for the prober that is part of service mirror).

This all should guarantee that non TLSed traffic coming from outside the cluster will be banned by the proxy that is injected on the gateway pod. I have tested that and it works. No port skipping is happening anywhere

This all depends on https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/pull/507
author: zaharidichev

comments.author: zaharidichev
comments.body:
> One possible solution is to define two sets of checks on separate ports. One will be for the traffic that is coming from outside the cluster( the liveliness prober) and will go through the proxy, while the other ones will be for local only traffic and will be coming from Kubelet and bypassing the proxy (we can do that with ` --skip-inbound-ports`, right? )

This is what I did, and it works pretty well actually

comments.author: olix0r
comments.body:
@zaharidichev This sounds like a good workaround to unblock us, but I still have some reservations about this being a generally feasible approach... We also have to take care to ensure that this healthcheck port doesn't expose any possibility to route requests or access sensitive diagnostic information.

Can you help me think through the alternatives? Can we know the node's IP at pod-creation time and allow traffic that originates from the node?

olix0r

> Possibly, but as far as I take it, pods can move nodes

Not true. A deployment/replicaset creates a pod, and it's pinned to its node/ip/etc throughout the lifetime of the pod. For the pod to "move" it terminates and a new pod is scheduled on another node. The injector hooks into the pod creation event.

comments.body: I see, that makes sense. So I guess we can possibly do something like that. I will investigate. What about the possibility os just checking whether the process is alive through a shell command?

title: remove admin server timeouts
body:
The Linkerd control plane components' admin servers have an idle connection timeout of 10 seconds.  This means that they will close connections which have been idle for 10 seconds.  These components are also configured with a 10 second period for liveness checks.  This introduces a race condition where connections will be idle for approximately 10 seconds between liveness checks and can idle out, potentially causing the next liveness check to fail.

We remove the idle timeout so that the connection stays alive.

review_threads.author: olix0r
review_threads.body: Can we just unset all of these timeouts? Why are they set?

review_threads.author: olix0r
review_threads.body: If we unset these, we could simplify this all to `http.ListenAndServe(addr, h)`

review_threads.author: olix0r
review_threads.body: Here's where it was introduced https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/commit/682b0274b5ff4535d1c4d088650cf6d13e508b31#diff-b5ab530c184ee6c6d6fe09ad488de24aL79 -- previously we used the simpler constructor. No explanation in commit message or code.

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body:
read and write timeouts seem like reasonable safety nets for these unary APIs.  If any HTTP message takes longer than 10 seconds to read or write, we probably want to abort it.

Removing idle timeout would be fine, I think, but it doesn't appear to be possible to have a read timeout but no idle timeout (????) since an unset idle timeout defaults to the read timeout.  But as long as this is long enough and we have the liveness checks to keep the connection open, this should amount to the same thing.

review_threads.author: olix0r
review_threads.body:
As I mentioned in the issue, I think we could set a ReadHeaderTimeout if we really want to, but I would prefer just using the defaults. In all of the cases we care about (prometheus, healthchecking), the clients will enforce some timeout.

If we do want to keep timeouts here, we need to document why we've chosen these values and what problem they solve. I don't want to cargo-cult arbitrary configuration (that has caused problems).

I'm specifically -1 on setting an IdleTimeout, though. We can clients choose how they want to manage connections.

Pothulapati
comments.body:
We actually ran into an issue as per https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/issues/4572 as we were putting default values i.e image, args, etc into `linkerd2/values.yaml` which implies that they get saved into `linkerd-config-addons` preventing us from updating the defaults as values are always overwritten finally by `linkerd-config-addons`.

As per https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/issues/4572#issuecomment-642659009, we thought the solution was to put default values in templates directly but this was causing problems as when we have a default args as 
```yaml
args:
  storage.tsdb.path: /data
  storage.tsdb.retention.time: 6h
  config.file: /etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml
  log.level: info
```
and the user wants to overwrite with (using `--addon-config`)
```yaml
args:
  log.level: debug
```
This essentially appends the extra args into templates causing the same arg to occur twice making prometheus fail.

So, The solution that we came up (the PR is  updated accordingly) is to put **default values in `<addon>/values.yaml`** which means that the overwritten values get merged (not appended) and thus overwrites occur correctly. 

_(These same changes will be done both with tracing and grafana add-ons next)_


**To test this PR:**
Support for most configuration like args, scrape_configs, globalConfigs, etc have been moved under `prometheus` field in `values.yaml` and they can all be configured now. Once configured they are stored under `linkerd-config-addons` and used with upgrades. 

An example full configuration file is available [here](https://gist.github.com/Pothulapati/f7c5c589b1d563546374d370d4082e3b), which can be applied by running
```bash
# Install recording and alerting rules which are used by the prometheus instance
k apply -f https://gist.githubusercontent.com/Pothulapati/00194de1dd0d819c4b853df96a8b3dfe/raw/881a5f5cd8dee4601c1ded77393ab0cbe4c459c5/linkerd-rules.yaml
# Install Linkerd
./target/cli/linux/linkerd install --addon-config ./config.yaml | k apply -f -
``` 

Once applied the configuration can be checked from the prometheus UI by port-forwarding the service (where there are options to see and check the configuration of the isntance)

comments.author: Pothulapati
comments.body:
This PR also has the following additional changes:
- `prometheusImage` and `prometheusLogLevel` flags have been removed as when these flags are set we would essentially want to set `prometheus.` fields which in the default case are not present as those fields are commented out in `values.yaml` and defaults are in `prometheus/values.yaml` and would cause additional complexity to create an append. This is not worth in my opinion as users can now set these values in `prometheus.image` and `promtehus.args.log.level` through the `addon-config` file.

title: edge-20.5.2 changes
body:
## edge-20.5.2

This edge introduces a number of new features that provide diagnostic
information for multicluster setups as well as proxy performance
improvements.

* CLI
  * Added a section to the `linkerd check` that validates that all
    clusters part of a multicluster setup have compatible trust anchors
  * Modified the `export-service` command to work by transforming yaml
    instead of modifying cluster state
  * Added functionality that allows the `export-service` command to
    operate on lists of services   
* Controller
  * Changed the multicluster gateway to always require TLS on connections
    originating from outside the cluster
  * Removed admin server timeouts from control plane components, thereby
    fixing a bug that can cause liveness checks to fail
* Helm
  * Moved Grafana templates into a separate add-on chart    
* Proxy
  * Added configurable middleware that rejects connections with no identity
    targeting specific ports
  * Improved latency under high-concurrency use cases.
author: zaharidichev

title: Separate grafana image tag in template
body:
Currently, `image` in grafana, has a hard dependency on the linkerd tag.

So, even if users add a config like
```yaml
grafana:
  image: my-registry/grafana
```

it is required that the user has a image *with linkerd version* in the registry.

This is obviously a pretty bad requirement, and I missed updating this. 

So, now a separate field called `tag` is added through which user can specify a tag, whose default is `*linkerd-version`, which would be the current version of the CLI/Helm-Chart. 

Also, made sure that we build `gcr.io/linkerd-io/grafana` for each version as a tag.



@alpeb

title: Exit tests if linkerd resources exist
body:
## Motivation

As mentioned in the [Testing RFC](https://github.com/linkerd/rfc/blob/master/design/0003-isolated-integration-tests.md#constraints):
> The integration test setup checks require that certain conditions are
> satisfied by the given cluster. A surprising condition is that no
> pre-existing Linkerd installation resource may exist; if it does then it is
> deleted.

## Solution

`init_test_run` which runs before integration tests start will now exit the
script if any Linkerd resources exist on the cluster.

Example bad path:
```
Checking the linkerd binary...[ok]
Checking if there is a Kubernetes cluster available...[ok]
Checking if Linkerd resources exist on cluster...
Linkerd resources exist on cluster:

pod/hello-6b6b5d644d-xrnhn
pod/hello-slow-cooker-h8xn2
pod/world-fc8f457b7-gj7wq
pod/gateway-676fd64cb9-j57k6
pod/hello-c767bf764-cbdqh
pod/hello-slow-cooker-fqmxr
pod/slow-cooker-ftxdx
pod/t1-855c678bdd-vdg96
pod/t2-76989f94d4-d5fv8
pod/t3-75c8877797-hfwgc
pod/world-6784d4f65c-cn6vl
replicaset.apps/gateway-676fd64cb9
replicaset.apps/hello-c767bf764
replicaset.apps/t1-855c678bdd
replicaset.apps/t2-76989f94d4
replicaset.apps/t3-75c8877797
replicaset.apps/world-6784d4f65c
job.batch/hello-slow-cooker
job.batch/slow-cooker

Help:
    Run [/home/kevin/Projects/linkerd/linkerd2/bin/test-cleanup]
    Specify a cluster context [/home/kevin/Projects/linkerd/linkerd2/bin/test-run /home/kevin/Projects/linkerd/linkerd2/target/cli/linux/linkerd [l5d-integration] [context]]
exit
```

Example good path:
```
Checking the linkerd binary...[ok]
Checking if there is a Kubernetes cluster available...[ok]
Checking if Linkerd resources exist on cluster...[ok]
```

Signed-off-by: Kevin Leimkuhler <kevin@kleimkuhler.com>

For example if a test installs Linkerd into `linkerd` ns, pods are created and injected in `default` ns, and then `linkerd` ns is deleted, there will be pods remaining in `default` ns that have the `linkerd.io/control-plane-ns: linkerd` label.

For the test script that is good; we don't want any resources still around when starting a new test.

title: Lint all markdown files in CI
body:
## Motivation

linkerd/rfc#22

## Solution

Use the [markdown-lint-action](https://github.com/marketplace/actions/markdown-linting-action) to lint all `.md` files for all pull requests
and pushes to master.

This action uses the default rules outlined in [markdownlint
package](https://github.com/DavidAnson/markdownlint/blob/master/doc/Rules.md).

The additional rules are added are explained below:
- Ignore line length lints for code blocks
- Ignore line length lints for tables
- Allow duplicate sub-headers in sibling headers (e.g. allowing multiple ##
  Significant headers in `CHANGES.md` as long as they are part of separate
  release headers)

title: Flaky tests: when installation test fails, fetch logs and events
body:
Re #4371

When a test fails in `./test/install_test.go`, trigger the `TestLogs`
and `TestEvents` tests in a separate process in order to output any
unexpected logs/events that might have caused the initial test failure.

For instance, currently we're sporadically experiencing pod restarts.
Instead of ignoring them, this might help provide us with the real
underlying cause.
author: alpeb

comments.author: alpeb
alpeb
comments.body:
Great feedback :+1: 
I ended up extracting the log/event retrieval log into separate functions, containing both the network calls and the regex matching. There's no longer need for shelling out, and the `fetchLogsEvents` was renamed. LMKWYT.

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body: I don't really understand why we enable and disable this in a few places.  Is this to prevent infinite recursion or something?

review_threads.author: alpeb
review_threads.body: Before installing anything in the cluster, if a test fails, fetching the logs takes an eternity because it tries unsuccessfully to pull them for each container on each pod of the control plane, with a long timeout for each. So I'm only enabling fetching the logs after the tests that attempt installing the CP. And then I'm disabling that on the `TestLogs` test indeed for avoiding infinite recursion if that test fails.

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body: I'm confused about this `run` field.  It seems that we only check if it's empty but never check the value.  What is it supposed to do?

review_threads.author: alpeb
review_threads.body: That was used to identify when we shell out, so to avoid calling `TestLogs` and `TestEvents` recursively in the child process, but we're already avoiding that with the `fetchLogsEvents` var, so I think I can get rid of this...

review_threads.body: Why do we invoke these tests by shelling out instead of calling the test functions directly?

review_threads.author: alpeb
review_threads.body: From within `TestMain` there are no references to `t`, so I couldn't find a way to call a test function directly. I would be glad to find there's a better way than shelling out.

review_threads.body: I think this should be descriptive rather than imperative.  i.e. it should be called `controlPlaneInstalled` or something and indicate that the control plane has been installed.

review_threads.author: adleong

This changes the gateway's `incomingPort` to 4180 and the `probePort` to
4181 to fit into Linkerd's other port range being in 41XX.

title: Properly show the meshed count for non-selector services
body:
When viewing the output of `linkerd stat` for services which do not have a selector (such as services created by the service-mirror, for example) the meshed count column shows the total number which exist, even though the service actually selects no pods at all.

We update the StatSummary implementation to account for services which have no selector.

Additionally, we update the logic of the `--unmeshed` flag.  When the `--unmeshed` flag is not set, we typically skip rows for unmeshed resources because those resources would have no stats.  This is not appropriate to do when the `--from` flag is also set because in this case, metrics are not collected on the target resource but are instead collected on the client-side.  This means that stats can be present, even for unmeshed resources and these resources should still be displayed, even if the `--unmeshed` flag is not set.

Signed-off-by: Alex Leong <alex@buoyant.io>

title: edge-20.5.4
body:
* CLI
  * Fixed the display of the meshed pod column for non-selector services in
    `linkerd stat` output
  * Added an `addon-overwrite` upgrade flag which allows users to overwrite the
    existing addon config rather than merging into it
  * Added a `--close-wait-timeout` inject flag which sets the 
    `nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_close_wait` property which can be used to mitigate
    connection issues with application that hold half-closed sockets

  * Restricted the service-mirror's RBAC permissions so that it no longer is

  * Moved many multicluster components into the `linkerd-multicluster` namespace
    by default
  * Added multicluster gateway mirror services to allow multicluster liveness
    probes to work in private networks
  * Fixed an issue where multicluster gateway mirror services could be
    incorrectly deleted during a resync
* Internal
  * Fixed many style issues in build scripts (thanks @joakimr-axis!)
* Helm
  * Added `global.grafanaUrl` variable to allow using an existing Grafana
    installation

Signed-off-by: Alex Leong <alex@buoyant.io>

comments.body:
Running `linkerd cluster install --gateway=false` gives two `linkerd-multicluster` namespace manifests as
```yaml
tarun@tarun-Inspiron-5559:work/l5d-az-multi ‹master*›$ linkerd cluster install --gateway=false
kind: Namespace
apiVersion: v1
metadata:
  name: linkerd-multicluster

---
kind: Namespace
apiVersion: v1
metadata:
  name: linkerd-multicluster
---
``

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body: I think we need to indicate here that this takes an option name parameter.  I also think we need to provide guidance on what the name is for.  In a few places we call this the "remoteClusterName" but that might be confusing if users think they need to figure out what the name of the remote cluster is before they can use this.  In reality, this name can be anything and will be referenced by the `link` command.  So I think the help text should make it clear that we are creating a name here.

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body:
I think having a default might be more harm than good.  This may be easier to explain and understand if users are required to give a name with `allow`.  

Users can still use the link multiple cluster re-using the same service account if they want to, they just have to reference it by name.

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body: I don't know what this is.  It seems unused?

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body: @zaharidichev can you explain this to me?

review_threads.author: alpeb
review_threads.body:
`--cluster-server` is for overriding the k8s api server url to avoid this:
https://github.com/olix0r/l2-k3d-multi/blob/f64de67f0a7766b04f0b288b8e0128363fd2b2ed/link.sh#L12-L19

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body:
Oh, this is the address of the target cluster's kubernetes API server.  Gotcha.

Can we maybe call this `--api-server-address` or something?  I had no idea what `cluster-server` meant.  The flag description "Custom remote cluster domain" is also incorrect, I think.

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body:
This starts to get confusing because there are several names in play now: 
* the service account name, which is also called the remote cluster name, which is represents the source cluster
* the cluster name, which represents the destination cluster, (the destination cluster is often referred to as the "remote cluster").

So a typical command might be 

```
linkerd --context west cluster link east --cluster-name west | kubectl --context east apply -f -
```

Is anyone going to get all those contexts and cluster names and service account names right?  It's very confusing which things refers to which thing.

At the very least we need to differentiate between service account names and cluster names.

```
linkerd --context west cluster allow east-sa | kubectl --context west apply -f -

linkerd --context west cluster link east-sa --cluster-name west | kubectl --context east apply -f -
```

This is a little better, but still pretty confusing.  

Better yet would be to give the cluster a fixed name at multicluster install time so that this doesn't get mixed up with the service account dance at all.

```
linkerd --context west cluster install west | kubectl --context west apply -f -

linkerd --context west cluster allow east | kubectl --context west apply -f -

linkerd --context west cluster link east | kubectl --context east apply -f -
```

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body:
Let's use the term "target cluster" instead of "remote cluster".  Or perhaps this could be clear from context without explicitly specifying which cluster.  e.g.

"Outputs credential resources that allow service-mirror controllers to connect to this cluster"

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body:
Just to be super clear about this: this flag only controls the namespace that the service account is created into.  It does NOT restrict the RBAC of the service account to this namespace.  

In other words, this really doesn't do anything different than what `multicluster install` does.  @olix0r @grampelberg does this match your expectations?  I don't really understand in what situation a user would use `multicluster allow`.

review_threads.author: olix0r
review_threads.body: Perhaps we should call it --service-account-namespace?

review_threads.author: adleong
review_threads.body:
To me the bigger question is: what is the purpose of this command?

If it is to be able to create a SA with namespace scoped RBAC then additional work is needed to add that functionality.

As currently written, I don't think it does anything different than what `multicluster install` does.

review_threads.author: zaharidichev
review_threads.body: yes I am not exactly sure. This is mainly the result of the proposed install flow. I do not think it is a command that adds much value... ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

review_threads.author: adleong

Maybe something like this:

"Outputs a Kubernetes secret that allows a service mirror component to connect to this cluster"

title: Add multicluster daisy chain check
body:
A mirror-service is one that has been created by the mirror service controller and resolves to a gateway in another cluster.  If a mirror service is exported (and thus mirrored into another cluster) this creates a "daisy chain" where requests can come in to the cluster through the local gateway and be immediately sent out of the cluster to a remote gateway.  If the remote gateway is in the source cluster, this can create an infinite loop.

Similarly, if an exported service routes to a mirror service by a traffic split, the same daisy chain effect occurs.

One example where this can come up is with multicluster fail-over.  If both clusters simultaneously fail-over even a portion of their traffic, a loop is created.

We add a check that detects either of the above conditions and warns of the existence of a daisy chain.

Signed-off-by: Alex Leong <alex@buoyant.io>

title: Wait for KinD nodes to be ready in CI
body:
Recently we have been seeing the following error in `Run integration tests` job
of the `KinD integration` workflow:

```
...
##[error]Process completed with exit code 2.
```

After some testing in a fork and changing the `linkerd check` to output to
`stout` instead of `/dev/null`, these errors show up periodically:

```
× no unschedulable pods
    linkerd-controller-7b65fdf847-rqqhn: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had taint {node.kubernetes.io/not-ready: }, that the pod didn't tolerate.
    linkerd-destination-77b66ff5b-zg9ht: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had taint {node.kubernetes.io/not-ready: }, that the pod didn't tolerate.
    linkerd-grafana-7c87b95798-h4qbf: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had taint {node.kubernetes.io/not-ready: }, that the pod didn't tolerate.
    linkerd-identity-7c7f4694bf-d2wwb: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had taint {node.kubernetes.io/not-ready: }, that the pod didn't tolerate.
    linkerd-prometheus-d479547f-j2b2l: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had taint {node.kubernetes.io/not-ready: }, that the pod didn't tolerate.
    linkerd-proxy-injector-885845b8-xk974: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had taint {node.kubernetes.io/not-ready: }, that the pod didn't tolerate.
    linkerd-sp-validator-7d6f48c48c-ctjkt: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had taint {node.kubernetes.io/not-ready: }, that the pod didn't tolerate.
    linkerd-tap-74c6649ffd-x245h: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had taint {node.kubernetes.io/not-ready: }, that the pod didn't tolerate.
    linkerd-web-6cdf6db9f6-2bbcg: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had taint {node.kubernetes.io/not-ready: }, that the pod didn't tolerate.
    see https://linkerd.io/checks/#l5d-existence-unschedulable-pods for hints
```

This is fairly simple to reproduce locally; the kind control plane node is not
immediately ready after `bin/kind create cluster`.

The solution is to wait for all nodes to be ready. Currently, there is only ever
one node, but as this will likely change in the future this covers all cases.

So far this has only happened on forks--so while this may not be the only
issue--it is at least one.
