title: release notes for stable-2.10.1
body:
## stable-2.10.1

This stable release adds CLI support for Apple Silicon M1 chips and support for
SMI's TrafficSplit `v1alpha2`.

There are several proxy fixes: handling `FailedPrecondition` errors gracefully,
inbound TLS detection from non-meshed workloads, and using the correct cached
client when the proxy is in ingress mode. The logging infrastructure has also
been improved to reduce memory pressure in high-connection environments.

On the control-plane side, there have been several improvements to the
destination service such as support for Host IP lookups and ignoring pods
in "Terminating" state. It also updates the proxy-injector to add opaque ports
annotation to pods if their namespace has it set.

On the CLI side, `linkerd repair` has been updated to be aware about the control-plane
version and suggest the relevant version to generate the right config. Various
bugs have been fixed around `linkerd identity`, etc.

**Upgrade notes**: Please refer [2.10 upgrade instructions](https://linkerd.io/2/tasks/upgrade/#upgrade-notice-stable-2100)
if you are upgrading from `2.9.x` or below versions.

* Proxy:
  * Fixed an issue where proxies could infinitely retry failed requests to the
    `destination` controller when it returned a `FailedPrecondition`
  * The proxy's logging infrastructure has been updated to reduce memory pressure
    in high-connection environments.
  * Fixed a caching issue in the outbound proxy that would cause it to
    forward traffic to the wrong pod when running in ingress mode.
  * Fixed an issue where inbound TLS detection from non-meshed workloads
    could break
  * Fixed an issue where the admin server's HTTP detection would fail and
    not recover; these are now handled gracefully and without logging warnings
  * Control plane proxies no longer emit warnings about the resolution stream ending.
    This error was innocuous.
  * Bumped the proxy-init image to v1.3.11 which updates the go version to be 1.16.2

* Control Plane:
  * Fixed an issue where the destination service would respond with too big of a
    header and result in http2 protocol errors
  * Fixed an issue where the destination control plane component sometimes returned
    endpoint addresses with a 0 port number while pods were undergoing a rollout
    (thanks @riccardofreixo!)
  * Fixed an issue where pod lookups by host IP and host port fail even though
    the cluster has a matching pod
  * Updated the IP Watcher in destination to ignore pods in "Terminating" state
    (thanks @Wenliang-CHEN!)
  * Modified the proxy-injector to add the opaque ports annotation to pods
    if their namespace has it set
  * Added Support for TrafficSplit `v1alpha2`
  * Updated all the control-plane components to use go `1.16.2`.

* CLI:
  * Fixed an issue where the linkerd identity command returned the root
    certificate of a pod instead of its leaf certificates
  * Fixed an issue where the destination service would respond with too
    big of a header and result in http2 protocol errors
  * Updated the release process to build Linkerd CLI binaries for Apple
    Silicon M1 chips
  * Improved error messaging when trying to install Linkerd on a cluster
    that already had Linkerd installed
  * Added a loading spinner to the linkerd check command when running
    extension checks
  * Added installNamespace toggle in the jaeger extension's install.
    (thanks @jijeesh!)
  * Updated healthcheck pkg to have hintBaseURL configurable, useful
    for external extensions using that pkg
  * Fixed TCP read and write bytes/sec calculations to group by label
    based off inbound or outbound traffic
  * Fixed an issue in linkerd inject where the wrong annotation would
    be added when using --ingress flag
  * Updated `linkerd repair` to be aware of the client and server versions
  * Updated `linkerd uninstall` to print error message when there are no
    resources to uninstall.

* Helm:
  * Aligned the Helm installation heartbeat schedule to match that of the CLI

* Viz:
  * Fixed an issue where the topology graph in the dashboard was no
    longer draggable.
  * Updated dashboard build to use webpack v5
  * Added CA certs to the Viz extension's metrics-api container so
    that it can validate the certifcate of an external Prometheus
  * Removed components from the control plane dashboard that now
    are part of the Viz extension
  * Changed web's base image from debian to scratch

* Multicluster:
  * Fixed an issue with Multicluster's service mirror where its endpoint
    repair retries were not properly rate limited

* Jaeger:
  * Fixed components in the Jaeger extension to set the correct Prometheus
    scrape values

title: Add support for --short flag in check command
body:
The `check` command is useful in verifying if a cluster is ready for
linkerd to be install or if a linkerd installation was successful. In
most cases, all check results are green and all checks results are
displayed to the user, however, this output can be verbose especially
when copying and pasting it around for other users to see.

This change introduces a `--short` flag for the `check` command where it
only shows errors or warnings encountered when `check` is run. It then
show the regular overall `Status check results are...` message once
complete. If all checks pass, we only show the check results message.

This change also includes a code reorg refactor for the `check.go` file
by moving all output format related code into `healthcheck.go`. It also
includes some code to output a new header for core checks in the `'basic'`
format.

```bash
Linkerd core checks
===================


Status check results are √
```

Some outstanding questions:
- Feedback on the current formatting of the `--short` is welcome. I did
not change the wording but rather just omitted successful checks.
- This change does not include the short flag for extension specific
checks. My thinking was that those checks are not as verbose as the
parent linkerd check and do not need the flag.

* When rendering the main checks, we want to only print errors and only print category headers if that category has an error in it
* When rendering the extension checks, we want to only print errors but always print the category header

Rather than distributing this logic between here and  prettyPrintResults, I think we need multiple different `prettyPrintResults` functions that perform each of the correct behaviors.  e.g. `prettyPrintShortResults` and `prettyPrintShortExtensionResults`. title: Remove the `linkerd-controller` pod
body:
Now that we got rid of the `Version` API (#6000) and the destination API forwarding business in `linkerd-controller` (#5993), we can get rid of the `linkerd-controller` pod.

## Removals

- Deleted everything under `/controller/api/public` and `/controller/cmd/public-api`.
- Moved `/controller/api/public/test_helper.go` to `/controller/api/destination/test_helper.go` because those are really utils for destination testing. I also extracted from there the prometheus mock structs and put that under `/pkg/prometheus/test_helper.go`, which is now by both the `linkerd diagnostics endpoints` and the `metrics-api` tests, removing some duplication.
- Deleted the `controller.yaml` and `controller-rbac.yaml` helm templates along with the `publicAPIResources` and `publicAPIProxyResources` helm values.

## Health checks

- Removed the `can initialize the client` check given such client is no longer needed. The `linkerd-api` section was left with only the check `control pods are ready`, so I moved that under the `linkerd-existence` section and got rid of the `linkerd-api` section altogether.
- In that same `linkerd-existence` section, got rid of the `controller pod is running` check.

## Other changes

- Fixed the Control Plane section of the dashboard, taking account the disappearance of `linkerd-controller` and previously, of `linkerd-sp-validator`.

### What

Fixes #5838 

* Opaque ports should still work on an unmeshed service. Currently, there
is no integration test to validate that traffic between a meshed app and
an unmeshed (but opaque) service works as expected.

* This change adds a new integration test that confirms opaque ports
behaves correctly in the given scenario. Correct behavior in this case
means that there will only be TCP metrics available on the inbound side
(and not on the outbound, unmeshed side). Furthermore, no HTTP metrics
should be recorded by either side (as consequence of opaqueness).

### How

I tried to keep as much as possible to the current style of the tests. There are three main implications that arise from opaque ports between a meshed and unmeshed workload:
  1. We have no L7 protocol metrics (inbound/outbound);
  2. No TCP metrics on server, TCP metrics on client (inbound yes, outbound no -- lack of proxy);
  3. No mTLS (unmeshed pod doesn't have the proxy TLS identity).
 
Based on these 3 implications I designed the test in the same format as the existing ones.
* First, we add an unmeshed service and pod -- I put these in a separate yaml file. The Service has an opaque ports annotation. I wanted to avoid reading the file contents in so I created a test helper function to just `kubectl apply -f` them 
(**Note**: *wanted to use an existing function but the ones we have in only execute commands with data from stdin, e.g `kubectl apply -f - `*).
We also add in a meshed SC that sends stuff over http to our unmeshed pod. We check the pods have spun up.
* Second, we check the inbound side. For the meshed app, we expect to see TCP metrics but no HTTP metrics. I added new regex expressions to account for no TLS. If either of these two conditions (TCP/HTTP) are not met, we fail.
* Third and final, we check the unmeshed service. If we have _any_ metrics, we fail. Our pod is unmeshed and the traffic is opaque, we wouldn't expect to have anything in there. I created an http response metric to make sure we don't get anything on the inbound.


I created the regex expressions based on what metrics look like when no TLS identity is discovered, I've appended them below in case someone wants to double check.
<details> <summary> Click me for metric examples </summary>

```sh
# TCP  tcp_open_connections{direction="inbound",peer="src",target_addr="0.0.0.0:4191",tls="no_identity",no_tls_reason="no_tls_from_remote"} 1      tcp_open_connections{direction="outbound",peer="src",target_addr="10.43.251.103:8080",tls="no_identity",no_tls_reason="loopback"} 1

# HTTP INBOUND (meshed pod)
response_latency_ms_bucket{direction="inbound",target_addr="0.0.0.0:4191",tls="no_identity",no_tls_reason="no_tls_from_remote",status_code="200",le="30000"}

# HTTP OUTBOUND (unmeshed pod)
request_total{direction="outbound",authority="svc-opaque-unmeshed.linkerd-opaque-ports-test.svc.cluster.local:8080",target_addr="10.42.0.169:8080",tls="no_identity",no_tls_reason="not_provided_by_service_discovery",dst_deployment="opaque-unmeshed-svc",dst_namespace="linkerd-opaque-ports-test",dst_pod="opaque-unmeshed-svc-5f9bd44cfc-thcpm",dst_pod_template_hash="5f9bd44cfc",dst_service="svc-opaque-unmeshed",dst_serviceaccount="default"} 16
```
</details>

Let me know if I missed anything or if I can improve this. Naming suggestions also very welcome, feel like I didn't do a great job on the naming side this time around 😄. 

Signed-off-by: Matei David <matei@buoyant.io>

title: Release notes for edge-21.4.4
body:
## edge-21.4.4

This edge release further consolidates the control plane by removing the
`linkerd-controller` deployment and moving the `sp-validator` container into the
`destination` deployment.

Annotation inheritance has been added so that +all* Linkerd annotations
on a `Namespace` resource will be inherited by pods within that namespace.
In addition, the `config.linkerd.io/proxy-await` annotation has been added which
enables the [linkerd-await](https://github.com/olix0r/linkerd-await)
functionality, simplifying the implementation of the await behavior.

Some of the `linkerd check` functionality has been updated. The command
ensures that annotations and labels are properly located in the YAML and
displays hinit anchors for core health checks.

Finally, the nginx container has been removed from the multicluster gateway pod,
which will impact upgrades. Please see the note below.

**Upgrade note:** When the multicluster extension is updated in both of the
source and target clusters there won't be any downtime because this change only
affects the readiness probe. The multicluster links must be re-generated with
the `linkerd mc link` command and the linkerd multicluster gateways will show
the target cluster as not alive until the `linkerd mc link` command is re-run,
however that shouldn't affect existing endpoints pointing to the target cluster.

* Added proxy checks for core control plane and extension pods
* Added support for awaiting proxy readiness using an annotation
* Added namespace annotation inheritance to pods
* Removed the `linkerd-controller` pod
* Moved `sp-validator` container into the `destination` deployment
* Added check verifying that labels and annotations are not mixed up
  (thanks @szymongib@)
* Enabled support for extra initContainers to a daemonset (thanks @mhulscher!)
* Removed nginx container from multicluster gateway pod
* Added an error message when there is nothing to uninstall
* Fixed hint anchors for core health checks

Signed-off-by: Charles Pretzer <charles@buoyant.io>

title: Support Traffic Splitting through `ServiceProfile.dstOverrides`
body:
Initial part of #6054 

This PR 
- updates the destination logic to prevent the override of `ServiceProfiles.dstOverrides` when a `TS` is absent and no `dstOverrides` set. This means that any `serviceprofiles.dstOverrides` set by the user are correctly propagated to the proxy and thus making Traffic Splitting through service profiles work.
- This also updates the `profile_translator.toDstOverrides` to use the port from `GetProfiles` when there is no port in `dstOverrides.authority`


After these changes, The following `ServiceProfile` to perform
traffic splitting should work.

```yaml
apiVersion: linkerd.io/v1alpha2
kind: ServiceProfile
metadata:
  name: backend-svc.linkerd-trafficsplit-test-sp.svc.cluster.local
spec:
  dstOverrides:
  - authority: "backend-svc.linkerd-trafficsplit-test-sp.svc.cluster.local.:8080"
    weight: 500m
  - authority: "failing-svc.linkerd-trafficsplit-test-sp.svc.cluster.local.:8080"
    weight: 500m
```


This PR also adds an integration test i.e `TestTrafficSplitCliWithSP` which  checks for
Traffic Splitting through Service Profiles. This integration test follows the same pattern 
of other traffic split integration tests but Instead, we perform `linkerd viz stat` on the
client and check if there are expected server objects to be there as `linkerd viz stat ts`
does not _yet_ work with Service Profiles.

---
- update trafficsplit adapter to not do anything when ts are not present
- relax requirements of routes in sp-validator and Open API Validation
- nit: Update to the expectedLeaf to have the correct value
- add TestTrafficSplitCliWithSP integration test
author: Pothulapati

After this change, if there is no TS and no DstOverrides are set by the user, it seems like we keep the DstOverrides as an empty list.  Is that change intentional?  Is it the behavior that we want?

review_threads.author: Pothulapati
adleong
review_threads.body: That sounds right, but since this is a change from how we do it today, I just wanted to confirm that you've tested it and that having an empty list of DstOverrides works as expected.

review_threads.author: kleimkuhler
review_threads.body: @Pothulapati Do we know how this interacts with the proxy performing a `Get` request? The default override was added to close #4879. With this change, `GetProfile` for a service will not return destination overrides so I don't think we'll perform `Get` on the endpoints now. This could lead to the proxy not performing its load balancing on the endpoints.

review_threads.author: kleimkuhler
review_threads.body:
So talking this through a little more we still do want to make sure `dst_overrides` for the destination profile is set if the service profile has none itself.

We should change the check here though to not be an `else` for `tsa.split != nil`. We instead would want a separate check for `if len(merged.Spec.DstOverrides) == 0`. If this is the case, we know that the traffic split added no overrides and the service profile has no overrides. Therefore, the response's `dst_overrides` should be set so that the proxy still performs its own load balancing.

body:
PR#6038 refactored `healthcheck_output.go` to accomodate the printing
check results in `short` output. In that refactor the spinner display
was code section was changed so that that code could be shared in the
different `prettyPrintResults` functions.

Previously, the function would exit early prior to printing to avoid
showing the the check error output if the check was undergoing a retry.
After the refactor, that code was inadvertently removed causing check
to always print the error message and then continue retrying.

This caused output like this:

title: Introduce support for StatefulSets across multicluster
body:
### What
---

The purpose of this PR is to prototype (and demonstrate) StatefulSets in a multicluster setting. Currently, it isn't possible to communicate with a specific pod in a StatefulSet across clusters without manually creating clusterIP services for each pod backing the StatefulSet in the target cluster.

After some brainstorming, we decided that one way to solve this problem is to have the Service Mirror component create a "root" headless service in our source cluster along with clusterIP services (one for each pod backing the StatefulSet in the target cluster). The idea here is that each individual clusterIP service will also have an Endpoints object whose only
host is the Gateway IP -- this is the way mirrored services are constructed in a multicluster environment. The Endpoints object for the root service will contain pairs of hostnames and IP addresses; each hostname maps to the name of a pod in the StatefulSet, its IP corresponds to the clusterIP service that the Service Mirror would create in the source cluster.

To exemplify, assume a StatefulSet `foo` in a target cluster `west` with 2 pods (foo-0, foo-1). In the source cluster `east`, we create a headless root service foo-west` and 2 services (`foo-0-west`, `foo-1-west`) whose  Endpoints point to the Gateway IP.  Foo-west's Endpoints will contain an  AddressSet with two hosts:
```yaml
# foo-west Endpoints
  - hostname: foo-0 
     ip: <clusterIP of foo-0-west>
  - hostname: foo-1 
     ip: <clusterIP of foo-1-west>
```

By making these changes, we solve the concerns associated with manually creating these services since the Service Mirror would reconcile, create and delete  the clusterIP services (as opposed to requiring any interaction from the end user). Furthermore, by having a "root" headless service we can also configure DNS -- for an end user, there wouldn't be any difference in addressing a specific pod in the StatefulSet as far as syntax goes (i.e the host `foo-0.foo-west.default.svc.cluster.local` would point to the pod foo-0 in cluster west).

#5162 contains the background information, thought process, problem statement as well as any back and forth conversations we had on the topic.

### Changes
---

To achieve this "redirection", the service mirror needs to distinguish between a normal exported service and a headless exported service. Additionally, the destination service should resolve a clusterIP service marked as "headless" to one Endpoint (weighted addr set) in GetProfile. With this in mind, broadly speaking the changes are in two places: _the cluster watcher component_ (in the Service Mirror controller) and _the destination service_.

#### 1. Service Mirror Controller

What I thought we should do is:
* Introduce a new annotation (or label) to distinguish between mirrored services and mirrored headless services.
* If we want to mirror a service which is headless, we also need to _identity the name of the pods that are part of the headless service's StatefulSet_ and then for each of these pods we want to create a clusterIP service to "mirror" the pod.
* For each clusterIP service corresponding to a pod, we want to create an Endpoints object with the Gateway address inside.
* At the end, we want to mirror the headless service, this means we want to set its clusterIP to `None` in the object spec, collect all previously created services' clusterIPs and create an Endpoints object with (hostname, IP) pairs where each hostname corresponds to a pod name and each IP to the mirrored clusterIP service.
* When we repair endpoints, we want to reconcile the headless service's endpoints based on the clusterIP services that are currently mirrored (that is, if a pod is deleted and its mirrored service is deleted, we want this update to be reflected in the Endpoints of the root headless service).

For the purpose of this prototype I cut some corners and didn't really concern myself with deleting/modifying/reconciling the root service or any of its nested clusterIP services. In an actual implementation we'd want to be considerate of all of these cases, for e.g in this branch if we delete the root headless services the clusterIP services still linger around and don't get cleaned up properly.

Additionally, there are some assumptions that I made:
* We only have one Gateway address (so that each clusterIP Service's Endpoints will contain just one address)
* If a service is headless, endpoints repair should just ignore it (we'd ideally deal with this differently in the actual implementation), 
* For simplicity, we create the Endpoints objects based on pod specs (I think a better way to do this, retrospectively, is to do it based on the Endpoints object of the headless service in the target cluster)

To list pods I have also changed the local and remote clientsets to be configured with a Pod informer (and RBAC rules).

*Note*: at first I thought it made sense to have an annotation to mark services are headless but I think it would make more sense to have it as a label, it would also be consistent with other parts of the API (specifically, `mirror.linkerd.io/exported` which is a label).

#### 2. Destination Service

Ideally we want to avoid doing a `Get` call in the destination service. So as part of this prototype I made some changes to return an endpoint in `GetProfile` when we resolve a clusterIP service. Ideally, we would make this process a bit more efficient and tidied up (adding another branch in GetProfile does complicate everything).

Overly simplified, if a clusterIP service has the headless annotation, we build an address set based on the gateway IP that's in the Endpoints object. We also fetch the gateway identity from the Endpoints annotation and return it as an endpoint to the proxy with no subsequent updates.

### Tests
---

I tested this with `mehdb` that I also used in the issue to talk through the approach. One caveat here is that mehdb is a simple KV store and works over http, I'm not sure if TCP would work out of the box with the current approach.

I have tried to see whether StatefulSets can be reached across clusters through both `GetProfile` (returning an endpoint) and `Get`. The latter seems to work well out-of-the-box, for `GetProfile` the destination doesn't seem to get overwritten; while the request successfully makes it to the inbound proxy of the gateway, it doesn't get routed to the service:


```sh
 go run controller/script/destination-client/main.go -method getProfile -path 10.43.93.228
INFO[0000] retry_budget:{retry_ratio:0.2 min_retries_per_second:10 ttl:{seconds:10}} endpoint:{addr:{ip:{ipv4:2886991878} port:4143} weight:10000 metric_labels:{key:"namespace" value:"default"} metric_labels:{key:"service" value:"mehdb-0-west"} metric_labels:{key:"target_cluster" value:"west"} metric_labels:{key:"target_service" value:"mehdb-0.mehdb.default.svc.west.k3d.example.com"} metric_labels:{key:"target_service_namespace" value:"default"} tls_identity:{dns_like_identity:{name:"linkerd-gateway.linkerd-multicluster.serviceaccount.identity.linkerd.west.k3d.example.com"}} protocol_hint:{h2:{}}}
```

</details>

**Note**: to force the proxy to go through `Get` instead of `GetProfile` with the new destination changes, we can remove the headless annotation from the clusterIP service. E.g if we remove it from `mehdb-0-west` the proxy will call a Get on the dst_override it gets from `GetProfile`. This was helpful in my tests since it let me see whether services were mirrored correctly; 

```sh
# first, test whether key is persisted locally (from west to west)
# helps us ensure the KV store behaves correctly
root@network-utils:/# curl http://mehdb-0.mehdb.default.svc.west.k3d.example.com:9876/get/westkey
west

# second, test whether key is persisted across clusters
# key is westkey and expected value is headless 
# (note: this was done through Get, GetProfile didn't get routed correctly)
root@network-utils:/# curl http://mehdb-0.mehdb.default.svc.west.k3d.example.com:9876/get/key
headless

```

**TL;DR of my findings**:

* Service Mirrors will mirror services and endpoints correctly;
* Destination service will return an endpoint in `GetProfile` if the service is headless (and mirrored);
* Requests to StatefulSet pods across clusters works, however, at the moment they only seem to work when the proxy makes a subsequent call to `Get` (so when we return a profile from `GetProfile` rather than an endpoint).

Will continue looking into why that happens and will update this with logs. Let me know what you think!


Signed-off-by: Matei David <matei@buoyant.io>

---

### Questions, concerns and assumptions.

* **Work still to be done**: 
    - [x] Clean up nested clusterIP services. At the moment, if we unexport a mirrored service, even if it's headless it will be 
      cleaned up. Nested clusterIPs however aren't being cleaned up.
   - [x] Improve on how we work with subsets. At the moment, the main assumption is that the endpoints object has just one 
      subset. In reality, there can be more than one. My main concern here is that there will be a lot of looping but overall the 
      logic should be the same.
  - [x] ~**Tests**: integration~ (separate PR)
  - [x] **Tests**: unit (_destination service_)
  - [x] **Tests**: unit (_service mirror_)
  - [x] Feature-gate the Endpoints informer (?) -- would mean this has to be enabled to get StatefulSets to work. Might be good to do until we get some feedback.

* **Questions/Concerns**: it would be great to get some feedback on these points.
    - [x] Endpoints reconciliation. Does the reconciliation logic seem to hold? (_yes, but we should move to a filtered 
       informer as a follow up_)
    - [x] APIServer calls. We are making a lot of calls to the API Server to retrieve endpoints and services. Is this an issue? 
       Should we be concerned with optimising this at this point and can anything be done? I would hate to repeat an error 
       like in #5684
    - [x] Unmeshed clients won't be able to talk to the remote service. The request makes it to the inbound side of the 
       gateway but is not mTLS'd so it's never forwarded to the service. Is this something that we want to address?
   - [x] [A question on subsets when diffing between remote and local Endpoints](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/pull/6090#discussion_r643135956)

### Update

Fixed the issue I was having where an endpoint resolved through `GetProfile` wouldn't reach the StatefulSet pod on the other cluster. The problem was that there was some misconfiguration in the weighted address returned:

* **Identity**: the endpoint didn't have the identity of the gateway, this was fixed -- we are now using the identity from 
   the Endpoints object (GatewayIdentity annotation).
* **AuthorityOverride**: this wasn't set on on the endpoint. The inbound proxy on the gateway side was handling this in 
   legacy mode; by setting the authority override the transport header is set correctly and the requests are routed to the 
    right pod.

comments.body:
> Ah indeed, that had escaped me too. IIUC then you could also stop getting info from the pods and retrieve the host names from the endpoint as well...

Yup! This was one of the questions I had myself -- can we just use the host from the endpoint instead of fetching pods. It seems to work properly and its covered in the new update that I pushed.

### Update
---

Made a couple of changes based on some open questions I had and also the initial feedback from @alpeb. *TL;DR*: watch endpoints to update mirrored resources, use hostnames from Endpoints objects instead of pods and remove headless annotation.

* *Destination service*: small change, we no longer check for a headless annotation we just check to see if the service has a mirrored fqn annotation.

* *Cluster Watcher*: added a new informer to watch for Endpoints updated events. There are a _lot_ of those so I tried to filter some out, we mainly care about events that belong to a headless Endpoints object (they all have a headless [annotation by default from k8s](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/labels-annotations-taints/#servicekubernetesioheadless)) and we do not care about Endpoints that have entries in `NotReadyAddresses` -- we want to process only hosts that are ready to accept traffic.

I extracted the previous clusterIP Service creation for headless hosts into its own function to simplify some of the logic. Most of the new logic is in `updateHeadlessEndpoints()` where we diff the state of the remote Endpoints object against the local Endpoints object and either add/remove from it (similar to how Endpoints Translator works). I left a bunch of comments in, some with assumptions, some with indications and some with questions. I'll be working on updating the OP with a list of questions that I (or anyone else) may have.

As an aside, the diff took me a while to wrap my head around. We cannot compare using just remote Endpoints (e.g old remote diffed with new remote) since by "old" k8s understands the last known state; this can lead to some undefined behaviour. I played with scaling and it all seemed to work well, scaled up then down then up and so on. The last commit doesn't seem to break anymore.

My biggest concern around this so far is working with multiple AddressSets (and multiple Subsets). The logic is already quite complicated without having to add even more loops and sets to the mix. If anyone has any thoughts on this it would be really appreciated.

### Tests
---

* I followed the same scenario as above to make sure I didn't accidentally break what was already working. In our remote cluster, we create the StatefulSet, export the service and then in the src cluster we create a slowcooker job that sends PUT requests to the remote StatefulSet to update a key (called "key") whose value we expect to be `headlessworks`.

    ✅  DNS gets set-up as expected in the src cluster (we make calls to `mehdb-0.mehdb-west.<namespace>.svc.<east-cluster-domain>`)
    ✅  DNS gets resolved to the clusterIP service we create in the src cluster for that host (in our case a service called `mehdb-0-west`)
    ✅  Outbound proxy on slowcooker side calls `GetProfile` with the IP, gets back an Endpoint. Transport Header should be set to the FQN of the mirrored service (`mehdb-0.mehdb.<namespace>.svc.<west-cluster-domain`)
    ✅ Gateway correctly routes to service/pod based on Transport Header

...and finally, key is updated.

End result:  
```sh
# In a net utils container
bash-5.1$ curl http://mehdb-0.mehdb.default.svc.west.cluster.local:9876/status
leader # applied StatefulSet in remote cluster, pods spun up

# Get key named "key", nothing so far service not exported
bash-5.1$ curl http://mehdb-0.mehdb.default.svc.west.cluster.local:9876/get/key

# Service exported, slowcooker deployed, try to get the key
bash-5.1$ curl http://mehdb-0.mehdb.default.svc.west.cluster.local:9876/get/key
# nothing yet

# try again
bash-5.1$ curl http://mehdb-0.mehdb.default.svc.west.cluster.local:9876/get/key
headlessworks
# key was set from the source cluster

---

# inbound proxy for our StatefulSet shows the call was forwarded by the gateway
57399s] DEBUG ThreadId(01) inbound:accept{client.addr=10.42.0.24:51330}:server{port=9876}:proxy:http{v=h2}:http1{name=mehdb-0.mehdb.default.svc.west.cluster.local:9876}:profile:http1: linkerd_proxy_http::client: headers={"sc-req-id": "13", "user-agent": "Go-http-client/1.1", "content-length": "13", "forwarded": "by=linkerd-gateway.linkerd-multicluster.serviceaccount.identity.linkerd.west.cluster.local;for=default.mehdb-test.serviceaccount.identity.linkerd.east.cluster.local;host=mehdb-0.mehdb.default.svc.west.cluster.local:9876;proto=https", "host": "mehdb-0.mehdb.default.svc.west.cluster.local:9876", "l5d-dst-canonical": "mehdb-0.mehdb.default.svc.west.cluster.local:9876"}

```

Previous scenario works but I also wanted to test with the new Endpoint update logic if we can scale the StatefulSet up/down and still make it work. Here is what we currently have in the src cluster (east):
```
❯ k get svc
NAME           TYPE        CLUSTER-IP      EXTERNAL-IP   PORT(S)    AGE
kubernetes     ClusterIP   10.43.0.1       <none>        443/TCP    26m
mehdb-0-west   ClusterIP   10.43.239.153   <none>        9876/TCP   17m
mehdb-1-west   ClusterIP   10.43.88.2      <none>        9876/TCP   17m
mehdb-west     ClusterIP   None            <none>        9876/TCP   17m

❯ k get ep
NAME           ENDPOINTS                            AGE
kubernetes     172.20.0.4:6443                      26m
mehdb-0-west   172.20.0.6:4143                      17m
mehdb-1-west   172.20.0.6:4143                      17m
mehdb-west     10.43.239.153:9876,10.43.88.2:9876   17m
```

The StatefulSet had just 2 pods. I first scaled it up to 4. We'd expect to see 2 new clusterIP services and we'd expect `mehdb-west` Endpoints object to contain those new IPs in its spec.
```
# scale in west
❯ k scale statefulset mehdb --replicas=4 --context=k3d-west
statefulset.apps/mehdb scaled

# results in east
❯ k get svc
NAME           TYPE        CLUSTER-IP      EXTERNAL-IP   PORT(S)    AGE
kubernetes     ClusterIP   10.43.0.1       <none>        443/TCP    30m
mehdb-0-west   ClusterIP   10.43.239.153   <none>        9876/TCP   21m
mehdb-1-west   ClusterIP   10.43.88.2      <none>        9876/TCP   21m
mehdb-west     ClusterIP   None            <none>        9876/TCP   21m
mehdb-2-west   ClusterIP   10.43.131.3     <none>        9876/TCP   2m45s
mehdb-3-west   ClusterIP   10.43.229.4     <none>        9876/TCP   2m

❯ k get ep
NAME           ENDPOINTS                                                         AGE
kubernetes     172.20.0.4:6443                                                   30m
mehdb-0-west   172.20.0.6:4143                                                   21m
mehdb-1-west   172.20.0.6:4143                                                   21m
mehdb-2-west   172.20.0.6:4143                                                   2m47s
mehdb-3-west   172.20.0.6:4143                                                   2m2s
mehdb-west     10.43.239.153:9876,10.43.88.2:9876,10.43.131.3:9876 + 1 more...   21m

# ep mehdb-west -o yaml
subsets:
- addresses:
  - hostname: mehdb-0
    ip: 10.43.239.153
  - hostname: mehdb-1
    ip: 10.43.88.2
  - hostname: mehdb-2
    ip: 10.43.131.3
  - hostname: mehdb-3
    ip: 10.43.229.4
  ports:
  - port: 9876
    protocol: TCP

# Test with slowcooker again this time key is "upkey" expected value "scaledup"
bash-5.1$ curl http://mehdb-0.mehdb.default.svc.west.cluster.local:9876/get/upkey
scaledup
```

*Note*: scaling StatefulSets takes a long time. The Endpoints object will update itself many times; unlike pods, StatefulSets come up incrementally, so if we scale to 4 we first have to wait for `mehdb-2` to come up. This means 2 Endpoints updates: (1) when the remote Endpoints object (in west) gets a new entry for `mehdb-2` under `NotReadyAddresses` and (2) when the pod is ready, Endpoints object will be updated to include the pod in its Subset. Therefore there are 4 updates, 2 for each pod we add to the set.

<details>
<summary> More scaling </summary>

```
matei in east
❯ k get svc
NAME           TYPE        CLUSTER-IP      EXTERNAL-IP   PORT(S)    AGE
kubernetes     ClusterIP   10.43.0.1       <none>        443/TCP    3m27s
mehdb-0-west   ClusterIP   10.43.166.110   <none>        9876/TCP   5s
mehdb-west     ClusterIP   None            <none>        9876/TCP   5s

❯ k get ep
NAME           ENDPOINTS            AGE
kubernetes     172.20.0.4:6443      3m29s
mehdb-0-west   172.20.0.6:4143      7s
mehdb-west     10.43.166.110:9876   7s


# Scale up to 2
matei in west
❯ k scale statefulset mehdb --replicas=2 --context=k3d-west
statefulset.apps/mehdb scaled
```

### Update
---

> The labeled service creation is caught first, but it doesn't have endpoints yet so it bails out.
> 13 seconds later the endpoints creation is caught, but as they're labeled with `service.kubernetes.io/headless` they're ignored and have to wait for the watch reconciliation 5 minutes later for the service to be given another chance.
> You mentioned above we're reacting to headless endpoints creation, but according to [this](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/pull/6090/files#diff-58391f2b0ac5849326792fbaf12a8e4aa8b06886acbe9fda308357d131ed38dcR956-R962) we're actually letting the service event take over.... can you please clarify? 🙏

Ah, this is a really good catch! At first, I meant to say that the creation is entirely left up to the function that creates the service; so when we create a service we also create its endpoints and then in the endpoints update we just process update events. This approach doesn't seem to work when we apply a service already exported -- in this case, the Endpoints subset is not yet finalised so it's not a good idea to create the local endpoints object.

I've pushed some changes that work around this. We _no longer create the endpoints object when we create the service, if the service is headless_ -- we leave the creation logic to the endpoints handler. In the endpoints handler, if there isn't a local endpoints for the service we create one, otherwise we just update. Think this is also a bit easier to reason with and read.

Also, I wanted to include a small list of things to keep in mind, open questions and assumptions that I had.

* **Work still to be done**: 
    - [x] Clean up nested clusterIP services. At the moment, if we unexport a mirrored service, even if it's headless it will be 
      cleaned up. Nested clusterIPs however aren't being cleaned up.
   - [ ] Improve on how we work with subsets. At the moment, the main assumption is that the endpoints object has just one 
      subset. In reality, there can be more than one. My main concern here is that there will be a lot of looping but overall the 
      logic should be the same.

* **Questions/Concerns**: it would be great to get some feedback on these points.
    - [ ] Endpoints reconciliation. Does the reconciliation logic seem to hold? 
    - [x] **Q**: APIServer calls. We are making a lot of calls to the API Server to retrieve endpoints and services. Is this an issue? 
       Should we be concerned with optimising this at this point and can anything be done? I would hate to repeat an error 
       like in #5684
           **A**: with the Endpoints using a shared informer in `createOrUpdateHeadlessEndpoints` repeated calls shouldn't hit the API Server so we might be safe for now.
    - [x] **Q**: Unmeshed clients won't be able to talk to the remote service. The request makes it to the inbound side of the 
       gateway but is not mTLS'd so it's never forwarded to the service. Is this something that we want to address?
           **A**: out of scope

* **Assumptions**:
    - (_for now_) we only deal with one subset & port.
    - A main assumption made is that we are dealing only with StatefulSets. Any pod can make use of a headless service when the end-user wants to talk directly to pod. Moving forward it would be helpful to clarify whether we expect _any_ headless service to work. If we do, some assumptions in the code might not hold up, e.g

```Go

# in cluster_watcher.go
function createOrUpdateHeadlessEndpoints(){ 
  ...
  ...
        // When we reconciliate local addresses with remote ones, we exit early if
       // both endpoints have the same number of hosts -- for StatefulSets this makes sense
      // since hostnames will be consecutive, if local == 4 then so will remote (pod-0, pod-1, .., pod-4). 
     // For a random headless service this wouldn't be the case though since pod names are randomly generated.
	if len(localHosts) == len(remoteHosts) {
		return nil
	}
}
   ```

This is it at the moment off the top of my head, as we progress through the feedback I'll update the list.

### Update
---

In the latest update, I resolved Alejandro's comments and implemented the clean-up logic.

**Feedback**:

* Introduced a new `checkEndpointsValid` function so we can re-use the check in other places. For an Endpoints object to be valid for processing, it must have at least one `Ready` address and at least one Subset. Without either, we get nil ptr dereferences when looping.
* Removed `szHosts` field and cleaned up the `createOrUpdateHeadlessEndpoints` function to get rid of early optimisations and make the function more readable. Also added/changed debug statements.
* Added a shared informer for Endpoints in `createOrUpdateHeadlessEndpoints`.
* Lastly, in the event handler functions (Endpoints shared informer) we are now also checking whether the Endpoints has the exported annotation (which it will inherit from the service). This helps us skip Endpoints that we're not concerned with, but it also prevents us from processing a service's Endpoints _after it has been unexported_ (otherwise, since the Endpoints change they're picked up and deletion in the local cluster is unsuccessful).

**Clean-up logic**:

* Added service mirror labels to headless mirrors (i.e nested services) so they can be cleaned up properly when a cluster is unlinked. (we clean up based on these labels  -- mirror.mirrored and mirror.clusterName)
* Added logic to delete headless mirrors when a service is unexported (in `handleRemoteServiceUpdate`) (1)
* Added logic to delete headless mirrors when a service is deleted (in `handleRemoteServiceDeleted`) (2)
* For both (1) and (2) I created a function that adds clusterIP services from local cluster to queue as deletion events (so we don't delete directly but rather pass them through the same function a remote service would go through)

---

**Misc**:

Lastly, I noticed some undefined behaviour:
 
* when a service would be exist and would be edited to be exported, the Endpoints object wouldn't be picked up by the informers (bit weird since the Endpoints inherits the label so I would assume it's updated and hence picked up);
* when a service would exist and would be exported before the service mirror in local was ready, again the Endpoints wouldn't be picked up.

To fix, I added a new event handler for `Endpoints Add` events (along with a new event type in the cluster_watcher). This seemed to work well, think it doesn't hurt to process `Add` events -- we process them the same as with `Update`s.


---

* updated OP with more to-dos and stuff that's been ticked off.

comments.body:
### Update
---

Pushed some new changes! Most notably, the new commit addresses the use of all subsets in an Endpoints object (as opposed to working on just one subset as it was before). To help with this, I changed the way we diff Endpoints in `createOrUpdateHeadlessEndpoints()`.

Other changes include:
 * **Unit tests** for creation/updates for headless Endpoints (would need someone to have a look and give an opinion here if possible 🙏🏻 )
 * **Refactoring**: moved headless endpoints creation to its own function so `createOrUpdateHeadlessEndpoints` is easier 
 to read and go through. Removed a lot of comments that either did not apply anymore or didn't add any value.
* Removed the headless annotation `mirror.linkerd.io/remote-svc-headless: true`.

#### Diff logic
---

If we have a _mirrored_ headless service that is backed by a number of Stateful pods, we need to reconcile the remote Endpoints with the local ones when the StatefulSet is scaled. Reconciliation implies two different scenarios:
 1) When the remote set is scaled up, we need to add the new pods to the local headless Endpoints object. This means we need to create new clusterIP services for these hosts and then add the hosts to the Endpoint's addresses.
2) When the remote set is scaled down, we need to remove the hosts from the local Endpoints and delete the clusterIP service.

Before, when we had just one subset to deal with, this was handled in a pretty straightforward way: make a new host set with new subset hosts and then diff against the local version, if the remote set has a host that's not present in local, create it. If local has a host not present in remote, delete it.

With multiple subsets, this becomes a bit trickier to do. I'm not convinced ordering is guaranteed, so we cannot maintain the same approach. For example, if the remote version has two subsets:
```
A: [10.2.1.1:555]
B: [10.2.1.2:777]
```

and the local just one:
```
A: [10.2.1.1:555]
```
we would be able to diff the hosts and add the address from B, but we wouldn't know which subset it belongs to. Processing subsets consecutively is not guaranteed to produce the same order in local as is on remote.

I'd like to think the new diffing logic is a bit more simple. What we do now is go through each subset in the remote Endpoints object and process each host; if the host does not have a corresponding clusterIP service, we create it and add the host to the subset (with the IP of the recently created clusterIP). If the host's service does exist, we take the existing clusterIP service and the host to the subset. Each time we update we replace the entire Endpoint's subsets. This takes care of scenario (1) when we need to add a new address/host. We also keep track of all hosts that _should_ be in the local Endpoints in a map and add each host to the map during processing.

Before, we used to add an annotation to the root service to indicate it's a headless, mirrored service. I've removed that and added a new label `root-headless-name` to all mirrored nested services. This serves as a way to identify the group of all nested services that belong to a root headless. To take care of scenario (2) when we need to remove an address, the logic becomes way simpler. If the address needs to be removed, then it will not be added in the subsets as described above and it will also not exist in the host map. To remove, we collect all services that are nested under the headless root using a label selector. As we go through each service, if the service's name is not found in the hostmap created above, then it likely means it needs to be cleaned up so we delete it. Since we update the subsets every time we don't need to do any more work on the Endpoints object, so removing consists solely of deleting clusterIP services.

Using the example above:
```
Remote subsets (east):
A: [host-foo: 10.2.1.1:555]
B: [host-bar: 10.2.1.2:777]


Local (west)
A: [host-foo: someClusterIP]
host-foo-west of type service: someClusterIP

1. Go through subsets A and B and create a map with the hosts that should exist in local => map[host-foo-west: struct{}{}, host-bar-west: struct{}{}]. We create new subsets: 

toCreate = [A:[host-foo: someClusterIP], B:[host-bar: someNewlyCreatedClusterIP](also create the clusterIP here)]

2. Get the two clusterIP services with the label selector: both service's name exist in the map so nothing to delete.
3. Apply update => 

Local (west) is now:
A: [host-foo: someClusterIP]
B:[host-bar: someNewlyCreatedClusterIP]
host-foo-west of type service: someClusterIP
host-bar-west of type service: someNewlyCreatedClusterIP
-----

If we scale down:

Remote subsets (east):
A: [host-foo: 10.2.1.1:555]

Local (west):
A: [host-foo: someClusterIP]
B:[host-bar: someNewlyCreatedClusterIP]
host-foo-west of type service: someClusterIP
host-bar-west of type service: someNewlyCreatedClusterIP

1. Create subsets (just A this time), map[host-foo-west: struct{}{}]
2. Loop through services [host-foo-west, host-bar-west]: bar-west not found in map => delete it.
3. Apply update =>

Local (west) is now:
A: [host-foo: someClusterIP]
host-foo-west of type service: someClusterIP
```

comments.body:
Wanted to give a quick update on the scope of this PR after an off GitHub discussion with @olix0r, @adleong  and @kleimkuhler. 

1) **Destination controller changes**: We discussed the destination controller changes that were made as part of this PR. The current changes allow the controller to return just one endpoint to the Gateway for a mirrored service, as part of the `GetProfile()` call that the proxy makes when first establishing a connection. This change allows us to avoid building a load balancer (that would otherwise be built in a follow-up `Get()` call to do service discovery for the mirrored service); this is a good idea in practice since load balancing across multiple Gateway pods in the target cluster is handled by the `LoadBalancer` type service that exposes the gateway (that is to say, a cloud lb or something similar would load balance in the target cluster so it is unnecessary for us to load balance requests in the source cluster). This, however, would be incompatible with `NodePort` type gateways (in which case we'd want to lb from the source cluster). The current implementation also couples the controller (part of core Linkerd) to concepts specific to an extension (in this case the mirror fqn label) -- this is something we'd ideally like to avoid, we should instead have an implementation that allows us to use this behaviour while also being extension agnostic. Lastly, this solution does not fix an important problem that we have with StatefulSets: _fqns that include an instance ID should always get just one endpoint back_ -- this doesn't hold in the target cluster in this scenario. For example, assume a mirrored headless service `foo` with one pod. While `GetProfile(foo-0-remote.foo-remote.default.svc.cluster.local)` in the src cluster would return one endpoint to the gateway, in the target cluster, the outbound proxy call to `GetProfile(foo-0.foo.default.svc.cluster.local)` would **not**. This is an important distinction; we want in the second case to have just one endpoint because failures in such cases are handled differently; we do not want a load balancer for _just one instance_.

2) **Alternative implementation to mirror headless services**:  we discussed an alternative way of implementing this. In an effort to simplify the service mirror changes, we could handle headless services in the same way we handle normal clusterIP services in the mirror controller. Given an Endpoints object for a service to be mirrored, if the object has no named hosts we could simply create in the local cluster a version of the Endpoints with the gateway address; if the object has named hosts we would also create a clusterIP service with that hosts name. The drawback of this design is that we will no longer get the logical grouping (and DNS entries) that a headless service provides. We decided not to move ahead with this for the time being so we can preserve the logical grouping and "mirror" (no pun intended) the headless behaviour K8s has as closely as possible.

**TL;DR**: will remove changes in destination controller in this PR since it doesn't solve the problem we want to solve at the moment to support statefulsets. We'll revisit the idea of a gateway endpoint at a later date; for now, I'll follow up with a separate PR to allow `GetProfile()` to return an endpoint for a pod fqn (e.g `pod-0.pod.namespace.svc.cluster.local`). Raised #6253 to track the work.

comments.body:
### Update
---

Based on recent feedback, I refactored the code to be more expressive. In all of the new methods (and functions) that deal with Endpoints objects, I have renamed most variables to better align with @adleong's suggested changes:
 * Services and objects in the target cluster now have an `exported` prefix (e.g `exportedServiceInfo`, `exportedEndpoints`). 
 * Services and objects in the source cluster now have a `mirror` prefix (e.g `mirrorServiceName`, `mirrorHeadlessService`).
 * ClusterIP services that have been created based on an exported service's hostnames are now referred to as `endpointMirrorServices` (or in some places simply `endpointMirror`). 

I realise these names will not be consistent with the rest of the code which refers to exported resources as `remote` and to mirror resources as `local` but I thought it would make everything easier to review and to understand. If consistency is an issue here, I am more than happy to revert some of the changes (particularly around parameters whose names contain the `exported` prefix). 

I have also changed the logic in two significant ways:
 * first, we no longer use a target ref's name to build endpointMirrors, instead we use the hostname of the address in the Endpoints object;
 * second, deletion now works differently. Instead of having two separate places where we delete endpointMirrors (when we have an `OnDeleteCalled` event and when we update a service that is no longer exported), we delete them in `handleRemoteServiceDeleted`. We also remove endpointMirrors based on a label selector now, as opposed to looping through the Endpoints object of the headless mirror. Finally, instead of adding an event for each endpointMirror, we simply delete all mirrors in one go, along with the headless mirror -- I thought it'd be more correct to do it this way since we can retry on any failure, even though it's more of an all-or-nothing situation. 

I removed the `checkEndpointsValid` function since it didn't add any value; I erroneously thought that we will get a nil ptr dereference when we loop through an empty subset or address set but that's not the case. I have also changed the `"root headless service"` label's key and value to better align with the new naming choice. 

For the tests, I have renamed the helper functions to again align better with the new names.

comments.body:
Thanks, @kleimkuhler! my statefulset was missing the `serviceName` property.  With this in place, all of the services and endpoints I was expecting were created correctly.  Unfortunately I wasn't able to test further because I ran into unrelated problems with my cluster.  I will continue testing with a brand new cluster tomorrow.

In the mean time, it's worth thinking about how we want to handle headless services for things other than statefulsets.  For example, if you export a headless service for a  deployment, the resulting mirror service will havean empty set of endpoints since there are no endpoint mirror services.

comments.author: mateiidavid
comments.body:
> In the mean time, it's worth thinking about how we want to handle headless services for things other than statefulsets. For example, if you export a headless service for a deployment, the resulting mirror service will have an empty set of endpoints since there are no endpoint mirror services.

This is a good point. As far as I can tell, this would work with individual pods whose `hostname` is explicitly set in the pod spec. Unfortunately, deployments don't support arbitrary hostnames for their pods. We could probably get the name of the pod in these situations from the `targetRef`, however, I'm not sure this is a good approach.

For example, something like this would probably work:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: default-subdomain
spec:
  selector:
    name: busybox
  clusterIP: None
  ports:
  - name: foo # Actually, no port is needed.
    port: 1234
    targetPort: 1234
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: busybox1
  labels:
    name: busybox
spec:
  hostname: busybox-1
  subdomain: default-subdomain
  containers:
  - image: busybox:1.28
    command:
      - sleep
      - "3600"
    name: busybox
```

Since the endpoints object would have the `hostname` field:
```yaml
subsets:
- addresses:
  - hostname: busybox-1
    ip: 10.42.0.89
    nodeName: k3d-west-server-0
    targetRef:
      kind: Pod
      name: busybox1
      namespace: default
      resourceVersion: "1264662"
      uid: 8ad3c95f-b1bc-4f9c-ba18-a43319831d2a
```

But something like this wouldn't:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nginx-deploy
spec:
  selector:
    app: nginx-dep
  clusterIP: None
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nginx-dep
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx-dep
  replicas: 3
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx-dep
    spec:
      hostname: foo
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx
```

since the Endpoints object will not contain the `hostname` field:
```yaml
subsets:
- addresses:
  - ip: 10.42.0.86
    nodeName: k3d-west-server-0
    targetRef:
      kind: Pod
      name: nginx-dep-7589444684-rzqv9
      namespace: default
      resourceVersion: "1264437"
      uid: 3640a1f3-0c43-4bea-bbd4-d767ed9ec577
```

I'm open for suggestions here. I'll do a bit of research and see if there's anything we can do.

**Edit**: we talked a bit about this off GitHub. Currently, there are two things that we could do:
   * use the `targetRef` field of a pod instead of the hostname when dealing with a deployment;
   * revert back to creating a clusterIP headless service when we have a deployment.

I'll look into the advantages and disadvantages of each solution and report back.

I haven't been able to get this working end-to-end.  In particular, when attempting to make a request to a headless mirror service, I get a 404 response.  Digging into the logs of the gateway proxy, I see the following line:

```
 linkerd-proxy [    50.741429s]  WARN ThreadId(01) inbound:accept{client.addr=10.138.0.16:52039}:server{port=4143}:direct:gateway{dst=web-0.web.emojivoto.svc.cluster.local:8080}:http{v=h2}: linkerd_app_core::errors: Failed to proxy request: bad domain client.addr=10.138.0.16:52039
 linkerd-proxy [    50.741463s] DEBUG ThreadId(01) inbound:accept{client.addr=10.138.0.16:52039}:server{port=4143}:direct:gateway{dst=web-0.web.emojivoto.svc.cluster.local:8080}:http{v=h2}: linkerd_app_core::errors: Closing server-side connection
 linkerd-proxy [    50.741471s] DEBUG ThreadId(01) inbound:accept{client.addr=10.138.0.16:52039}:server{port=4143}:direct:gateway{dst=web-0.web.emojivoto.svc.cluster.local:8080}:http{v=h2}: linkerd_app_core::errors: Handling error with HTTP response status=404 Not Found version=HTTP/2.0
```

It seems that the gateway is expecting the fqn in the OT header to be a logical service.  https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/main/linkerd/app/gateway/src/gateway.rs#L66

In other words, when we do a profile lookup for `web-0.web.emojivoto.svc.cluster.local:8080` we get a destination profile with an Endpoint whereas the proxy requires that the destination profile have a logical addr instead.  Do we perhaps need to add support for this case into the proxy?

comments.author: mateiidavid
comments.body:
**Update**: I added an event recorder to emit events when we skip mirroring services (e.g when a headless service doesn't have any exposed ports).

@adleong I also looked into the error you mentioned and into how to deal with headless services backed by a deployment/replicaset. 

### Bad Domain Error

Thank you so much for flagging this! It was very easy to replicate and it kind of gets in the way of rolling out this change. I wanted to use this space to give some context for other people. Recently, we merged #6260. This changed the destination controller to add an endpoint in the profile received by the proxy, when the profile request includes a pod DNS. 

When dealing with multicluster traffic, the profile request will not be made using an IP address, it will be made using the FQN of a service (or a pod DNS name, in the case of StatefulSets). In the remote cluster, on the outbound gateway side, the destination is chosen based on an FQN (or pod DNS name) taken from the OpaqueTransport (OT) header. Every mirror service has an annotation with its FQN in the target cluster; endpoint mirrors have the same FQN with an instance name prepended (e.g nginx-0.nginx.namespace.(...)). When the gateway receives the traffic from the local cluster, it looks at the OT to determine the destination and consequently sends a profile request with the FQN from the OT header.

Like you pointed out, the gateway expects the profile response to have authority of the destination. It never accounts for an endpoint and tries to build a logical service; since the authority for a StatefulSet is the pod DNS name, this will not work. We would probably need to add support in the proxy to connect to a logical address or an endpoint if the profile contains one. I don't think the change would be that big, I had a look at https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/main/linkerd/app/outbound/src/switch_logical.rs#L38 to see what we could do to get a similar behaviour in outbound side of the gateway. Tagging @olix0r here for an opinion.

### Headless services with deployments

The main usecase for a headless service backed by a deployment is (in my mind) when the user wants to do service discovery and load balancing on their own (i.e when a user wants to bypass kube-proxy). The problem that we have is that a deployment or replicaset will not allow for arbitrary hostnames in the pod template and we create endpoint mirrors based on those hostnames. There are two solutions to this:

1) When we have a headless service used with a deployment, mirror the service as clusterIP. This wouldn't give the user a good way to do service discovery, but it would still mirror the service and make it accessible from a different cluster. This would rely on Linkerd's load balancing, since the call may get routed to any pod backing the deployment in the target cluster. To implement this, we would need to "validate" the service when we first create it (similar to how we handle services with no exposed ports). Of course, there is no easy way to get the associated replicaset/deployment/statefulset, so we'd have to probably go through the endpoints and see if we have any hostnames associated with the IP addresses. If we have none, then the service should not be mirrored as headless. We would also need to do something similar in `createOrUpdateHeadlessEndpoints()` so we don't process the endpoints of a mirror service that _is not headless even though the exported service is_. We can also emit events when the validation fails and we create a clusterIP service.

2) When the hostname is absent, use the `targetRef` name of the address. This is how the PR was structured initially. It's an easier change to do than the first solution but it has its own limitation. First, pod names will be too large. We could think of a naming convention here but it will slightly complicate the implementation; a name such as `nginx-61q24dffg-west` is 
not very appealing. Second, this approach will make it harder to assume certain things such as a guaranteed pod ordering, smaller number of replicas and longer pod lifetimes, assumptions that we can make because we deal specifically only with StatefulSets (or individual pods with an arbitrary hostname). The shorter lifetime _may_ also impact performance since we can expect more changes to the Endpoints object and more creation/deletion requests, however this is just me speculating and I haven't proven this.

I prefer the first solution to the second, even though it brings about more changes. I think if people will want to address a specific pod it should have a hostname or it should be behind a StatefulSet. We can also revisit this in the future if there is a use for it, but at the moment I don't think we should support this.

### Quick update

* Re-worked some of the code and tests, minor refactoring for log messages and function parameters.
* Rebased off latest main, we should now have the proxy changes (PR#1157) to handle endpoint targets in the gateway, this should unblock this PR.
* Functional changes: added events and validation for services with no ports and validation for headless services whose endpoints don't contain any named addresses (see above message).

For those looking to review, [this repository](https://github.com/mateiidavid/l2d-k3d-statefulset) includes scripts to set the clusters up as well as the manifests for the tests described below.

### Tests

I did a bit of manual testing now that the proxy PR has been merged. I won't post the output for the tests, you can instead find the manifests at the bottom of this post to re-create the tests. If a test is checked off it means my results were positive.

1. [x] Test once a headless service is exported we can send a request from source to target cluster to a specific instance of a statefulset -- before, it threw 404 and BadDomain errors. **Passed** curl command gets a response back, gateway logs show request is redirected on the outbound side.
2. [x] Test once a headless service is exported, we can scale its associated statefulset up and down with no errors. **Passed**, no errors, scaled up to 4 replicas then down to 1.
3. [x] Test we can remove the export annotation and source cluster mirrors will be cleaned up. Also tested we can re-export the service with no errors. **Passed**.
4. [x] Test we can delete an exported service and see its mirrors cleaned up in the source cluster. **Passed**.
5. [x] Test that a headless service with no exposed ports will NOT be exported, expect to see an event on the service with mirroring skipped. **Passed** (event is on the remote/exported service).
6. [x] Test a headless service backed by a deployment (=> no named addresses in its Endpoints object) will be exported as **clusterIP**. **Passed**.

For (6), we check the endpoints object to see if we have any named addresses. The problem is that we can't guarantee the endpoints object will exist when the service is created (an endpoints will be created by the controller based on a service). I am willing to try to query the APIServer directly as opposed to relying on an informer. comments.author: mateiidavid
comments.body:
Thank you Kevin for finding the edge case. We (Alex, Kevin and I) had a chat off GitHub about the problem, I'll try to summarise it in two sentences below and describe our fix.

> This means that in handleRemoteServiceCreated we are somehow getting past the shouldExportAsHeadless check and trying to create the service

Kevin was seeing this because our `shouldExportAsHeadless` check would always either fail to get the Kubernetes object (because it was not in existence at that point in time) or would fetch the object but not process any addresses inside. Effectively, what we were trying to do was to check if the service we are processing now has any named addresses (e.g has a pod with a hostname backing it) to know whether it should be mirrored as headless or not. The distinction matters -- a headless service with no named addresses would act as if managed by a deployment and shouldn't necessarily be mirrored as headless but as a clusterIP service (in-depth discussions about this above).

We could never process any endpoint data associated with the service at that point in the lifecycle of the service because it was still too early. Pods would still be uninitialized and as a result so would the endpoint objects. Our approach now is different, instead of creating a headless service in `handleOnCreateOrUpdateService`, we are doing it in the endpoints handler and invert the authority or control to the endpoints. The first step when processing a set of endpoints now is to create a mirror for the associated exported headless service. We will have access to the addresses inside and this will let us make the decision that we were unable to make prior -- should the service be clusterIP or headless. Once we know and create the service, we also create its endpoints in the src cluster, if its clusterIP its endpoints will point to the gateway otherwise they'll point to endpoint mirrors.

```

❯ kubectl --context=k3d-west get svc
```

review_threads.author: mateiidavid
review_threads.body:
Going through this again a few days after I wrote it, I'm not convinced we should skip processing a host if it already exists, would really appreciate someone double checking me here. Here is why I think we shouldn't do this:

An Endpoints object has X subsets, where X !=0  and a subset is represented as a group of addresses with a common set of ports. The set of all endpoints in an Endpoints object is the union of all subsets. This means an address with multiple associated ports (that may come from multiple containers in the pod) will be in more than 1 subset. No address may be under NotReadyAddresses and ReadyAddresses at the same time in one subset.

This leads me to believe that if we go through a subset and process a host that is then found in the next subset, the current logic will skip adding it to the 2nd subset since it will already be present in the map. I don't think skipping here brings any benefit -- since we're using an informer there is also no performance cost from retrieving the same associated clusterIP service multiple times during this loop.

We do a similar thing when we create Endpoints too. Any thoughts on this?

More on subsets:
https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/api/core/v1#Endpoints
https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/api/core/v1#EndpointSubset

review_threads.author: kleimkuhler
review_threads.body:
After some off GitHub discussion we decided it does make sense to process all hosts even if it exists in the map already.

This is because it is valid for two subsets to exist in an endpoints object where each subset contains the same `TargetRef.Name` but different ports. Let's say subset 1 has a ready endpoint for `foo.svc:8080` and subset 2 has a ready endpoint for `foo.svc:8081`. If we were to skip the second `foo.svc` because it was already added to `hosts` by the first subset, then we would skip adding `8081` as a port that is ready for that service.

Processing each subset's hostnames regardless of it being present in the map or not ensures that the source cluster's endpoints object is closer to the actual state of the target cluster's endpoints object.

Ugh, this is news to me. I looked into it and can confirm headless services are allowed to be created without a `Ports` field. I think the rationale here is that they may be created since they serve to set up DNS entries which makes the port optional. It turns out, when the clusterIP is set to None or to an external address, Endpoints are still created [[1]](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/49686) [[2]](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/47250). Unfortunately, this is not documented in the official k8s docs (or at least no docs that I know of). We can't really get around this since our endpoint mirrors will require a port to be created.

title: Add support for server resource aware completion
body:
Linkerd's CLI offers basic shell suggestions on most of its subcommands.
These suggestions are based on hardcoded suggestion lists, for example such
`viz stat` auto suggests a list of all resources types supported by that
command located in `k8s.go`. Although this provides basic suggestions
for k8s manifest resources, prior to this change, there currently is no
way to get auto suggested resources from the k8s cluster linkerd is
installed in.

This change adds a new `CommandCompletion` module that reads arguments
and a substring, and queries the k8s API to determine what suggestions
to provide to the user. The current implementation makes the module
generic enough to query most Kubernetes resourcesand can be used for all
subcommands in the CLI.

This change only applies this behavior to the `stat` command as first
step. Adding auto completion for other commands will be done in a number
of follow up PRs.

To test out the change on this branch:
- Build the CLI binaries on this branch
- install the completion scripts for your shell environment. Running
`linkerd completion -h` should give you more info on how to do that.
- If not installed already, install `linkerd viz`
```
linkerd viz install | k apply -f -
```
- test out completion by typing
```
linkerd viz stat [tab][tab]
```

Part of #5981 

Signed-off-by: Dennis Adjei-Baah <dennis@buoyant.io>
author: dadjeibaah

You therefore don't need to do this parsing yourself. >	// The returned group and resource lists might be non-nil with partial results even in the
	// case of non-nil error.

[[ref]](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/master/discovery/discovery_client.go#L103)

How likely would it be that a user is restricted from accessing _some_ resources in the cluster? Would this be a cause for error?

I'm thinking if a user has RBAC configured in the `kubeconfig` and we use the config to initialise the clientset (`k8sAPI`), then we _might_ see errors similar to the ones displayed in informers when they don't have necessary permissions? title: Versioned `linkerd check` hint URLs
body:
Supersedes #5885

We've recently refactored the linkerd docs in the website to host separate sections for each major 2.x version. The [Troubleshooting page](https://linkerd.io/2.10/tasks/troubleshooting/) section is also versioned, but currently the hint URLs output by `linkerd check` commands point to `https://linkerd.io/checks` which redirects to `https://linkerd.io/2.10/tasks/troubleshooting`.

This PR changes the base of those hint URL so that instead it points to `https://linkerd.io/{version}/checks` where `{version}` is the CLI's major version. If the CLI is not in a stable version (edge or local dev version) then `{version}` will be `2` which the site will redirect to the latest stable version.

This change is coupled with linkerd/website#1069 that takes care of the website-side of things.

title: proxy: v2.143.0
body:
This release simplifies internals so that endpoint-forwarding logic is
completely distinct from handling of load balanced services.

The ingress-mode outbound proxy has been simplified to *require* the
`l5d-dst-override` header and to fail non-HTTP communication. This
ensures that the ingress-mode proxy does not unexpectedly revert to
insecure communication.

Finally, a regression was recently introduced that caused all proxy logs
to be output with ANSI control characters. Logs are now output in
plaintext by default

---

* discover: replace `linkerd-channel` with `tokio-util` `PollSender` (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#969)
* replace `linkerd-channel` with `tokio-stream` (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#970)
* concurrency-limit: use `tokio-util`'s `PollSemaphore` (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#968)
* http: Do not fail fuzz tests when all IO is not read (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#973)
* transport: Fix orig-dst compilation on non-Linux targets  (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#974)
* Update trust-dns to fix possible panic (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#975)
*  addr: fix `to_http_authority` panic with IPv6 (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#976)
* outbound: skip logical stacks when no profile is discovered (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#963)
* split: change traffic splits to require a profile (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#964)
* inbound: only build profile route stacks when a profile is resolved (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#966)
* profiles: make receiver param in `route_request` non-optional (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#967)
* outbound: move target types into stack modules (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#971)
* outbound: only build logical stacks for profiles with logical addrs (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#972)
* app: inbound: add fuzzer (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#977)
* admin: Fail connections when HTTP detection fails (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#979)
* reduce error boilerplate with `thiserror` (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#980)
* app: inbound: fuzzer: generalise fuzzers and solve coverage build (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#978)
* admin: Assume meshed connections are HTTP/2 (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#982)
* chore: Fix deprecations on nightly (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#983)
* fuzz: Add logging to fuzz targets (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#985)
* fuzz: don't panic when the proxy closes the conn (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#986)
* Commit lock files for fuzzers (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#984)
* fuzz: allow client requests to fail  (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#989)
* tower: update dependency to 0.4.7 (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#990)
* outbound: Make the Endpoint::logical_addr field optional (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#991)
* trace: explicitly disable ANSI terminal colors (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#994)
* ingress: Require the l5d-dst-override header (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#992)
* outbound: Do not support TCP-forwarding in ingress-mode (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#995)
* Decouple tcp forward stack from Endpoint target (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#996)
* Pickup linkerd-await wrapper in docker build (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#999)
* docs: Add fuzzing report (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#1000)
* tests: Use io::Error in mocked connector (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#1001)
* outbound: Decouple endpoint & logical stacks (linkerd/linkerd2-proxy#1002)
